Replace voltage regulator - see 12 32 000, or replace or disassemble alternator and inspect components - see 12 31 020.
Where can I find the nominal values for voltage and current specifications?
See nominal value microfiche for voltage specifications and see wiring diagram for wire connection details.
What is the tearing-out force specification for the ignition lead after installation?
The tearing-out force should be ≥ 200 N / 44 lbs.
How much should you strip the end of the ignition lead and what wire cross section size should be used?
Strip the end of the ignition lead by 6 mm with stripping pliers for 1.5 mm wire cross section size.
What should be applied to the guiding sleeve of Special Tool 12 1 092?
Spray a thin coat of lubricant 12 1 098 on the guiding sleeve of Special Tool 12 1 092.
What is the procedure for installing the connector after placing it on the ignition lead?
Move clamping jaws together by turning screw against stop, then after squeezing, release jaws and take out the ignition lead.
What voltage system does this spark plug connector replacement procedure apply to?
This procedure applies to the non-disconnectable version 30 kV system.
What is the first step when replacing a spark plug connector according to procedure 12 12 072?
Cut off the ignition lead as shown.
What caution is given about tightening the screw in step 26 12 105?
Tighten screw enough that the pliers can be pulled back. Opening the pliers too much could cause the plug receptacle to break.
How should the ignition lead be positioned during the connector installation process?
Unscrew screw, slide in ignition lead against stop, follow with pliers and slide in ignition lead further until connector is heard to engage.
What alternative tool set is mentioned as being available for this procedure?
The required special tools 12 1 091/092/098 are also available as a complete set 12 1 090.
What is shown in the plug receptacle illustration for better understanding?
The plug receptacle is shown cut open for better illustration.
What test should be performed after the connector installation is complete?
Perform tear-out test by hand with a tearing-out force of ≥ 200 N / 44 lbs.
What wire color is used for the generator charge indicator connection?
Blue wire is used for the generator charge indicator (D+ connection).
Which pin number corresponds to the oil level static connection?
Pin number 2 corresponds to the oil level static (STAT) connection.
What are the wire colors for the coolant temperature gauge connection?
The coolant temperature gauge (FT) uses brown/violet wire colors.
What is the difference between pins 6 and 7 in terms of fuse protection?
Pin 6 (15 S) has voltage with ignition on and fuse protection, while pin 7 (15 U) is the same as pin 6 but without fuse protection.
Which connection uses white/green wire colors for the service indicator?
Pin 11 (SI) for the service indicator reset uses white/green wire colors.
What wire colors are used for the speedometer signal connection?
The speedometer signal (TACH) connection uses black/white wire colors.
Which pin number is assigned to the electric fuel pump connection?
Pin number 13 is assigned to the electric fuel pump (EKP) connection.
What connection uses black/yellow wire colors?
Pin 18 (50) for voltage while starting uses black/yellow wire colors.
Which pins are used for engine diagnostic connections?
Pin 16 (Airb.) is used for the engine plug/diagnosis plug connection with white/black wire colors.
What wire color is specified for the FTM connection on pin 20?
Pin 20 (FTM) uses brown wire color.
What is the maximum allowable slip ring out of true measurement?
The maximum slip ring out of true is 0.03 mm (0.001").
What important note is given regarding soldering when replacing carbon brushes?
Only use a small amount of solder for soldering to prevent hardening of leads.
What components are indicated by callouts 1 and 2 in the voltage regulator removal diagram?
Callout 1 indicates the bolts to unscrew, and callout 2 indicates the regulator to take off carefully.
What inspection should be performed on slip rings during installation?
Check slip rings for wear, and if necessary, remove rotor and fine grind as well as polish the slip rings as part of Pos. 12 31 201.
What maintenance should be performed on contact surfaces during regulator installation?
Clean contact surfaces and check tension of spring contacts, correcting if necessary.
How should the regulator be initially mounted during installation?
Mount regulator at first with one bolt screwed in finger tight, then press alternator to final installed position carefully, install and tighten all bolts.
What procedure number is referenced for slip ring grinding and polishing?
Position 12 31 201 is referenced for slip ring grinding and polishing procedures.
What should be checked for wear during the carbon brush replacement process?
Check slip rings for wear, and fine grinding may be necessary if wear is detected.
What is the procedure section number for removing and installing/replacing the voltage regulator?
Section 12 32 000 covers removing and installing/replacing the voltage regulator.
What precaution should be taken when removing the voltage regulator?
Unscrew bolts carefully and take off regulator carefully during the removal process.
What are the testing requirements before troubleshooting the starter?
Correct connections on battery and starter, good ground connection between engine and body, and charged battery.
What should I do if the starter slips?
Remove starter and check gear ring teeth on flywheel for damage.
If the lights go out while starting, what does this indicate?
Short in starter.
What are the possible causes if the starter does not turn but only clicks in the solenoid?
Carbon brushes worn or solenoid faulty.
If the starter works when bridging connections 30 and 50, but doesn't work normally, what should I check?
Check for faulty wires and connections on starter switch, or starter switch faulty.
If the flywheel gear ring teeth are okay but the starter still slips, what should I repair?
Repair starter: drive pinion (one-way clutch), engaging mechanism, or planet gears faulty.
What special tool is needed to place the ignition lead in the spark plug connector?
Special Tool 12 1 096 is needed to place the ignition lead in the spark plug connector and slide it into the connector until connection is heard to engage.
What testing procedure should be performed on M3/M5/M6 models when replacing spark plug connectors?
Measure shielded resistance after unscrewing the ignition lead tube and pulling out the spark plug connectors.
How much ignition lead insulation should be stripped when replacing a screwed connection for ignition lead?
Strip the ignition lead insulation by about 12 mm (1/2 inch) with stripping pliers after cutting off the connection.
What is the recommended bend length for the wire when replacing ignition lead connections?
Bend the wire at a length of about 6 mm (1/4 inch).
What lubricant should be applied when installing the rubber cap on spark plug connectors?
Give the rubber cap a thin coat of lubricant to make installation easier. The specific lubricant is referenced in the specifications section.
What testing should be performed when replacing shielded connector and ignition lead contact for M3/M5/M6 models?
Measure shielded resistance after pulling off the shielded connector and unscrewing the ignition lead.
What tool is specified for stripping insulation on ignition leads?
Insulation stripping pliers are specified for cutting off the old lead contact and stripping insulation on the ignition lead.
What should be done after installing a new lead contact with pliers for ignition lead contacts?
Perform a tear out test and apply a thin coat of lubricant to make installation easier before screwing the shielded connector on the ignition lead.
Which models require unscrewing the ignition lead tube when replacing spark plug connectors?
M3/M5/M6 models require unscrewing the ignition lead tube when replacing spark plug connectors.
What is the procedure for removing rubber caps from spark plug connectors?
Pull off the rubber cap toward the rear, then unscrew the spark plug connector.
What should be applied to make installation easier when working with ignition lead contacts?
Apply a thin coat of lubricant to make installation easier, as referenced in the specifications section with HWB as the source of supply.
What final step is performed when placing the connection flush with pliers?
Place the connection flush with pliers and press on to complete the installation.
What procedure code covers disassembling and assembling the starter?
Procedure code 12 41 103 covers disassembling/assembling the starter.
What components need to be removed before taking off the circlip, shims, and seal?
The starter (see 12 41 020), solenoid switch (see 12 41 041), and cap must be unscrewed before removing the circlip, shims, and seal.
What should be checked during installation of the armature?
Check axial play of armature and correct with shims if necessary.
What should be applied to the housing bolts and insulator during installation?
High melting point grease should be applied to the housing bolts and insulator to each other.
What lubrication is specified for the bearing sleeve in the drive bearing bracket?
The bearing sleeve should be lubricated with oil before installing.
How should the bearing race be removed from the shaft?
Push back bearing race with a piece of suitable pipe, pry circlip apart and pull it off the shaft, then remove burrs with a file.
What components are labeled 1, 2, and 3 in the drive pinion assembly diagram?
Component 1 is the bearing race, component 2 is the new circlip, and component 3 is the drive pinion.
What should be checked when inspecting carbon brushes?
Check carbon brushes and commutator for wear, repairing if necessary (see 12 41 551).
What must be done to remove the pole housing?
Unscrew engaging lever bolt and remove rubber seal to remove the pole housing.
What inspection should be performed on the intermediate bearing during installation?
Check sleeve in intermediate bearing, replacing if necessary.
What lubrication should be applied to the drive pinion bearing surface during installation?
Lubricate bearing surface for drive pinion with grease during installation.
How are critical emission control faults displayed to the driver?
Critical emission control relevant faults are displayed in the instrument cluster by the "Check Engine" control lamp coming on and staying on continuously.
How many different faults can be detected while driving or operating the car?
Four different faults will be detected while driving or operating the car.
What position must the ignition key be in to read fault codes?
The ignition key must be in the "ignition on" position to read out fault codes with the help of a flashing code prior to starting the engine.
What does Code 1 indicate in the flashing code output?
Code 1 indicates a faulty air flow sensor.
What fault does Code 3 represent?
Code 3 represents a faulty engine temperature sensor.
What component does Code 4 diagnose as faulty?
Code 4 indicates a faulty idle speed switch.
How long is each timing interval in the flashing code pattern?
Each timing interval in the flashing code pattern is 3 seconds long, with 1 second lamp on and 1 second lamp off periods within the codes.
What does Code 2 diagnose in the fault code system?
Code 2 indicates a faulty oxygen sensor.
How is a fault cancelled from memory after repair?
A fault is cancelled in the memory automatically after repairing after the engine has been started five or at the most ten times.
How does the fault lamp behave when displaying fault codes?
The fault lamp will be switched off and on in accordance with the fault number, following the flashing code pattern shown in the diagram.
What pin on the universal adapter is used for the ignition final stage ground connection?
Pin 1 (term. 1) on the universal adapter is used for the ignition final stage ground connection.
What test equipment is needed to check the signal on Pin 1 for ignition final stage testing?
An oscilloscope is needed to check the signal while cranking the engine with the starting motor.
What corrective measure should be taken if the ignition final stage tests are okay up to this point?
Replace the DME control unit if tests up to this point are okay.
Which pins are used for testing the final stage of fuel injectors for cylinder 2-4-6 on the M20 engine?
Pins 17 / 14 are used for testing the final stage of fuel injectors for cylinder 2-4-6 (M20 engine).
What additional tests should be performed besides checking the signal with an oscilloscope for fuel injector testing?
Check plug connections and leads for fuel injectors, and test the fuel injectors themselves.
Which cylinders are tested using pins 16 / 14 for fuel injector final stage testing?
Pins 16 / 14 are used for testing the final stage of fuel injectors for cylinders 1-3-5 on the M20 engine.
What type of engine designation is specified for the fuel injector testing procedures shown?
The fuel injector testing procedures are specified for the M20 engine.
What components should be checked in addition to the oscilloscope signal test for ignition final stage diagnosis?
Check the power supply for ignition coil, ignition coil, distributor and leads, and spark plugs.
What is the recommended corrective action if fuel injector final stage tests are satisfactory?
Replace the DME control unit if tests up to this point are okay.
What diagnostic tool is consistently specified for checking signals in all the test procedures?
An oscilloscope is consistently specified for checking signals in all the test procedures shown.
How should the engine be operated when testing Pin 1 for ignition final stage ground?
Crank the engine with the starting motor while checking the signal with an oscilloscope.
What page number is shown at the top of this service manual section?
Page 12-112/3 is shown at the top of this service manual section.
What page should you refer to for instructions on working with transistor coil ignition systems?
Refer to page 12-0 for instructions for working on transistor coil ignition systems.
What are the removal steps for a TCi Control Unit (Bosch)?
Take off cap, unlock lock wire and pull off plug, then unscrew screws and remove control unit.
What preparation should be done to sealing surfaces during installation?
Clean sealing surfaces, grinding down with sandpaper if necessary to guarantee good thermal carrying-off.
What product should be applied to the back of the control unit during installation?
Coat back of control unit with Curil K 2 before installation of the control unit.
What must be checked after installation of a TCi control unit?
Check ignition timing after installation, correcting if necessary.
How do you remove a TCi-S Control Unit (Siemens/Telefunken)?
Pull off plug, then unscrew nuts and remove control unit.
What is the difference in removal procedure between the Bosch and Siemens/Telefunken TCi control units?
The Bosch unit requires taking off a cap and unlocking a lock wire before pulling the plug, while the Siemens/Telefunken unit only requires pulling off the plug directly.
What is shown in the top diagram image 30 12 045?
The diagram shows the TCi Control Unit (Bosch) with arrows indicating the removal process including the cap, lock wire, and plug connection.
What component is illustrated in the bottom diagram image 30 12 051?
The diagram shows the TCi-S Control Unit (Siemens/Telefunken) with arrows indicating the plug removal and nut locations.
What is the source reference for the Curil K 2 product mentioned?
Source: HWB Product Range (Division of BMW), as noted in the footnote with double asterisks.
What page number contains information about TDC position transmitter replacement or check?
Page 12-130
On which page can I find the procedure for alternator troubleshooting?
Page 12-140
What vehicle models does this Engine Electrical Equipment section cover?
Where can I find information about spark plug connector replacement?
What page covers the starter solenoid replacement procedure?
Page 12-152
Which page contains the voltage regulator removal and installation procedure?
What components need to be unscrewed to remove the shielded capacitor?
Unscrew the shielded capacitor itself, unscrew nuts on B+ and D+ studs, and take off the diode plate with stator coil.
Which terminals are mentioned for nut removal during disassembly?
B+ and D+ studs.
What components are removed together with the diode plate?
The diode plate is removed with the stator coil.
What type of capacitor is being removed in this procedure?
A shielded capacitor.
What action should be taken if the insulating sleeves and washers are damaged?
Replace them if necessary during installation.
What is shown in the bottom diagram?
The rear view of the alternator housing showing the internal diode arrangement and wiring connections.
What special tool is required to pull off the ball bearing during alternator disassembly?
Special Tool 00 7 500 is required to pull off the bearing.
What should be replaced during ball bearing installation if it was damaged?
Replace the cover for the bearing if it had been damaged through application of the special tool.
What important caution is given when unsoldering the stator coil on the diode plate?
Excessive heat from soldering iron would destroy the diodes.
What are the two main procedures shown for replacing the diode plate?
Unscrew bolts and remove diode plate, then check condition of insulating sleeves and insulators during installation.
What specific position check is mentioned for ball bearing installation?
Check installed position of washer - collar faces bearing.
Which BMW part numbers are shown for the ball bearing replacement procedure?
12 31 581 for replacing ball bearing and 12 31 691 for replacing diode plate.
What component is shown in diagram 630 12 178?
The stator coil on the diode plate that needs to be unsoldered.
What is illustrated in diagram 630 12 172?
The installation procedure showing the bearing cover replacement process.
What does diagram 630 12 173 show regarding the diode plate?
The diode plate with arrows indicating the bolt locations that need to be unscrewed for removal.
What component orientation detail is specified for the washer installation?
The collar of the washer must face the bearing during installation.
What are the main alternator service procedures covered in this section?
Replacing ball bearing (12 31 581) and replacing diode plate (12 31 691) with the alternator removed and disassembled.
What is the resistance specification for an 80 A alternator rotor coil?
For an 80 A alternator, the rotor coil resistance should be 2.8 to 3.0 ohms.
How do you check the rotor coil for breaks and shorted turns?
Connect test leads for resistance test on slip rings using a BMW service tester.
What is the nominal resistance value when checking the rotor coil for ground contact?
The nominal value should be infinity or greater than 999 k-ohm display.
What should you check if the slip rings show fine grinding during rotor coil ground contact testing?
Check slip rings, fine grinding if necessary - see section 12 31 200.
Where do you connect the test leads when checking the stator coil for ground contact?
Connect test leads for resistance test on solder point and stator (coil carrier).
What is the expected display reading for a proper stator coil ground contact test?
Nominal value: infinity or greater than 999 k-ohm display.
How do you check the negative diodes in the alternator?
Connect test leads for diode test with negative lead on cooler and positive lead on one of the negative diode connections. Display with perfect condition diodes shows polarity.
What is the procedure for checking positive diodes?
Connect negative lead on B+ connection pin and positive lead on one of the positive diode connections. Display with perfect condition diodes shows polarity.
What should you do if a diode is defective?
If a diode is defective, replace entire diode plate - 12 31 691.
What tool is required to perform the alternator component tests described?
Perform tests with a BMW service tester.
What components are visible in the upper left diagram showing the alternator stator?
The diagram shows the alternator stator with multiple coil windings and connection points for testing.
Which terminal provides the oxygen sensor signal?
Terminal L (terminal 5) provides the oxygen sensor signal.
What function does terminal A serve on the diagnosis plug?
Terminal A (terminal 6) is the diagnosis lead for airbag.
Which two terminals are used for TDC position transmitter signals?
Terminals P+ (terminal 8) and P- (terminal 10) are both used for TDC position transmitter signals.
What signal is provided by terminal 61?
Terminal 61 (terminal 12) provides the alternator charge indicator signal.
Which terminal number corresponds to the service indicator?
Terminal SI (terminal 7) corresponds to the service indicator.
What is the function of terminal 50 on the diagnosis plug?
Terminal 50 (terminal 11) provides power while starting.
Which terminal provides the speed signal?
Terminal 1 (terminal 13) provides the speed signal.
What does terminal 15 represent in the diagnosis plug connection?
Terminal 15 represents power with ignition turned on.
Which terminal is designated as Battery + on the diagnosis plug?
Terminal 30 (terminal 14) is designated as Battery +.
What is the distance 'V' for new condition carbon brushes in the voltage regulator?
The distance 'V' for new condition carbon brushes is approximately 12 mm (0.472").
What should be done if the battery charge indicator lamp goes out while the engine is running and the regulating voltage is not reached?
If the harmonic wave ratio and oscillograph are okay as shown, the voltage regulator has to be replaced according to section 12 32 000.
What components should be checked for wear during installation?
Check slip rings for wear, fine grinding and polishing if necessary.
What does the oscillograph pattern show for a defective power or exciter diode?
The oscillograph shows a square wave pattern with distinct flat-topped sections, indicating defective power or exciter diode.
What action should be taken if the specified charging current is not reached during testing?
If the specified charging current is not reached, remove and disassemble alternator, and inspect components according to section 12 31 020/513.
What should be done with the voltage regulator if the indicator lamp stays on continuously?
Remove voltage regulator and check carbon brushes, replacing if necessary according to section 12 31 200.
What does the oscillograph pattern show for a break in one exciter diode?
The oscillograph shows a pattern with missing or reduced amplitude sections, indicating a break in one exciter diode.
What test equipment should be connected during installation?
Connect BMW service test unit, then start engine and compare test values with nominal values.
What are the terminals labeled in the alternator diagram?
The terminals are labeled D+ and B+ in the alternator connection diagram.
What is the procedure number for checking and adjusting ignition timing?
The procedure number is 12 11 005.
What engine oil temperature is required before testing ignition timing?
The engine must be at operating temperature with oil temperature at 80°C (140°F).
What testing equipment should be connected for ignition timing procedures?
Connect a BMW service tester or BMW digital tester to operating instructions.
Can the dwell angle be adjusted on this system?
No, the dwell angle is given by design and can be checked, but not adjusted.
What should you do with the vacuum hose when checking ignition timing?
Pull off the vacuum hose for advance control.
What happens to the TCI control unit if it malfunctions?
The TCI control unit is no longer ready for operation in case of malfunction.
What equipment must be installed before testing?
A TDC transmitter must be plug-in installed.
How do you correct ignition timing if adjustment is necessary?
Correct by loosening the bolt and turning the distributor accordingly.
What do the + and - symbols indicate for ignition timing adjustment?
+ means advanced ignition timing and - means retarded ignition timing.
What must match the nominal value microfiche specification?
The distributor number must be the same as specified on the nominal value microfiche.
At what engine speed should you start and run the engine for testing?
Start and run the engine at test speed.
Where can you find additional specifications referenced in this procedure?
See Specifications and see Nominal Value Microfiche as referenced at the bottom of the page.
What is the main purpose of Test 1 in the Digital Motor Electronics troubleshooting section?
Test 1 is for testing the SPEED AND REFERENCE MARK SENSORS.
What should you check first when troubleshooting the speed and reference mark sensors?
Check wires for tight fit and damage, then check connections and arrangement of plug connections.
How is the reference mark sensor identified in the engine bay?
The reference mark sensor (B) is marked with a ring and can be found at reference location 12 14 510 / 515.
What multimeter functions are referenced for testing the DME pulse sensor?
Use resistance function (M 06) and oscillograph function (M 22/23) with the BMW service tester at reference 12 14 510.
What procedure should be followed when checking the DME control unit connections?
Take off trim panel, pull off plug on control unit and connect on universal adapter with (35-pin) test lead as shown in the illustration.
What components are labeled as 'D' and 'B' in the engine bay photographs?
Component 'D' appears to be a connector or electrical component, while 'B' is the reference mark sensor that is marked with a ring.
What additional testing reference is mentioned for engine test procedures?
Testing instructions refer to the BMW SERVICE TEST, specifically engine test/test step 05 (P 05).
What should be checked regarding power flow in the DME wires?
Check power flow and insulation (M 06) in wires on specified pins.
What important limitation is mentioned about this troubleshooting survey?
The checked causes of malfunction might not always be sufficient to eliminate a defect, so under certain circumstances additional tests could be necessary.
What should be done with the engine when checking resistance and oscillograph readings?
Turn engine with the starter while checking resistance (M 06) and oscillograph (M 22/23) on disconnected pulse sensor plug with BMW service tester.
What cross-references are provided for additional information?
See Specifications, Source: HWB (= Division of BMW), and See engine wiring diagram for additional information.
What temperature should the coolant temperature switch be checked at?
The coolant temperature switch should be checked at a temperature below 45°C (113°F).
What should you do with the idle control unit plug when checking the coolant temperature switch?
Pull off the plug on the idle control unit located in the glove box above the L-Jetronic control unit.
What vacuum advance control simulator part number should be connected for troubleshooting?
Connect vacuum advance control simulator 12 1 460.
What does it mean if the 'tp' lamp is not flashing during vacuum advance control troubleshooting?

If the 'tp' lamp is not flashing, it indicates no tp signal, no power supply for the simulator, L-Jetronic control unit connections or wire harness defective, or the engine is not running correctly or at all.
What are the possible causes if the 'MV' lamp is not on during vacuum advance control testing?
If the 'MV' lamp is not on, the causes are no power supply for the simulator, wire harness to simulator defective, or vacuum advance control relay defective.
What should you check if there is no advance control during testing?
If there is no advance control, check for vacuum advance control relay defective, connections or wire harness for solenoid defective.
What are the possible causes if ignition timing is not reached when vacuum is supplied to the advance control box?
The possible causes are solenoid defective, vacuum hose leaks, or distributor defective.
What should be done with the switches when checking the intake air temperature switch resistance?
The switches should be connected during the check with control simulator.
At what engine speed should the vacuum advance control system troubleshooting be performed?
Run the engine at idle speed when troubleshooting the vacuum advance control system.
What type of check should be performed on both the coolant temperature switch and intake air temperature switch?
Check resistance on both the coolant temperature switch and intake air temperature switch.
What should you do before removing the starter from the BMW E30?
Disconnect battery ground lead and remove air cleaner with air flow sensor.
What are the numbered components in the solenoid switch diagram?
Component 1 is the solenoid switch, component 2 is the spring, and component 3 is the armature.
What should you check on the armature during solenoid switch installation?
Check armature for wear including scoring and deep spots, and replace if necessary.
What lubrication is required when installing the solenoid switch?
Lubricate with grease before installing.
What steps are involved in removing the starter from below?
Drain coolant, disconnect heater hose and unscrew coolant pipe if necessary, then unscrew nuts and remove starter from above.
What reference number is given for the starter removal and installation procedure?
12 41 020 for removing and installing starter.
How do you remove the solenoid switch from the starter?
Remove solenoid switch with spring and disconnect and remove armature.
What should be done with the cooling system during installation?
Pour in coolant and bleed cooling system according to procedure 17 00 039.
What components need to be unscrewed for air collector removal?
Unscrew bracket for air collector.
What steps are required to disconnect the holder?
Unscrew holder and disconnect lines.
What service information reference is provided at the bottom of the page?
See Service Information of Gr. 00.
What is the reference number for replacing the solenoid switch?
12 41 041 for replacing solenoid switch.
What safety caution must be followed regarding the wire between battery and alternator?
Disconnect wire between battery and alternator only when engine is stopped.
What components need to be removed after disconnecting the battery when removing the alternator?
Remove air cleaner and air flow sensor.
Which connections need to be unscrewed on the alternator?
Unscrew connections B + and D +, and disconnect ground wire.
What should not be forgotten during alternator installation?
Don't forget the ground wire (see arrow).
Where must the pulling hook be positioned when checking belt tightness?
This requires pulling hook (2) to be in center of teeth.
Where should the indicator be located when checking belt tension?
Indicator must be located in scale above the green or yellow field.
What is the specified torque for the tensioning wheel nut?
Unscrew nut (1) and turn tensioning wheel (3) with a torque of approx. 7 Nm (5 ft.lbs.) and tighten nuts (1).
What should be done after adjusting the belt tension?
Recheck tightness with the tester, correcting if necessary.
What voltage should be checked on the TCI control unit terminal 1 during Test 3?
Check voltage greater than 10 V on TCI control unit terminal 1 (M 01).
What should you do if the ignition coil check in Test 3 is not okay?
Replace the ignition coil. If casting compound has run out or is missing, also replace the TCI control unit.
Where can you find the procedure for checking ignition coil resistance?
See section 12 13 009 for checking the resistance of primary and secondary coils.
What is the requirement before performing Test 4 on the TCI control unit?
Test 1 through 3 must be completed and show no malfunction.
What engine RPM should be used when cranking the engine for the oscilloscope test?
Crank the engine with starter at approximately 250 rpm.
At what RPM should the engine be operated when checking primary current?
Operate the engine at 1000 ±50 rpm when checking primary current.
What is the acceptable value range for primary current measurement?
The value should be 1.2 to 1.7 A - if not within this range, replace the control unit.
Where should the ammeter be connected for the primary current check?
Connect the ammeter in the power supply lead (terminal 15/green, on plug for engine wire harness).
What should you do if voltage is not okay when checking the wire from ignition coil terminal 1?
Check the wire from ignition coil terminal 1 to control unit for breaks and ground out (M 06).
What oscilloscope pattern should be displayed during the primary current test?
The primary display on oscilloscope should conform with the pattern illustrated - if necessary, replace the control unit.
When is it necessary to check the primary current according to the manual?
Check primary current (M 03) only when the primary oscillograph deviates from the expected pattern.
What additional test reference is mentioned for ignition voltage checking?
In engine test (P 09) check ignition voltage, which is also contained in engine test (P 01).
What are the four main testing requirements listed before starting the brief test?

The four testing requirements are: starting system okay (battery charged, starting motor and ignition lock), good ground connections between engine and body and engine wire harness okay, specified gasoline in tank (octane number, leaded/unleaded, not contaminated), and engine in good operating condition (timing, compression, etc.).
What connector type should be used when connecting to the DME control unit?
A 55-pin connecting lead should be used to connect the universal adaptor on the DME control unit and wire harness.
Why should the tests be carried out in the given order?
Tests are arranged to support each other and therefore should be carried out in the given order.
What is the source of supply mentioned for the universal adaptor?
The source of supply for the universal adaptor is HWB.
What alternative testing method is mentioned at the bottom of the page?
The alternative testing method mentioned is using the BMW Diagnosis Tester.
Which BMW models are covered in this Engine Electrical Equipment section?
Models 325 / 325 e / 325 es / 325 i / M 3 are covered in this section.
What page can I find information about carbon brushes replacement with starter removed and disassembled?
Carbon brushes replacement with starter removed and disassembled can be found on page 12-155.
On what page is the diagnosis plug connection plan located?
The diagnosis plug connection plan is located on page 12-160.
Where can I find on-board diagnosis information?
On-board diagnosis information can be found on page 12-200.
What is the reference number for the carbon brushes replacement procedure?
The reference number for the carbon brushes replacement procedure is 12 41 551.
What is the procedure number for disassembling and assembling the starter?
The procedure number is 12 41 513.
What should you do to the engaging fork guide during installation?
Lubricate the guide for engaging fork with grease.
What components are numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 in the starter disassembly diagram?
The diagram shows numbered components of the starter assembly, with component 5 being specifically called out in the removal instructions for the retainer, shims, and seal.
What should you check on the drive bearing bracket during installation?
Check the bearing sleeve in the drive bearing bracket, lubricating with oil prior to installation.
What tool is recommended for removing burrs from the drive pinion?
Remove burrs with a file.
How should you push back the bearing race during disassembly?
Push back bearing race (1) with a piece of suitable pipe.
What parts should be checked for wear during carbon brush inspection?
Check carbon brushes and commutator for wear, repairing if necessary.
What reference number should you see for carbon brush repair procedures?
See 12 41 551 for carbon brush repair procedures.
What should you use for the drive pinion surface during installation?
Use a new circlip and lubricate bearing surface for drive pinion with grease.
What components should you check on the pinion during installation inspection?
Check pinion for wear (on teeth, bearings, one-way clutch), replacing if necessary.
What is the source of supply reference noted at the bottom of the page?
The source of supply reference is HWB.
What BMW service test unit step should be carried out when checking ignition coil?
Carry out engine test step 09.
What should you observe on the oscillograph when checking ignition coil?
Observe oscillograph - ignition voltage and ignition voltage deviation must agree with nominal values.
What are the terminal numbers for the primary coil when using multimeter test M 06?
Measure resistance of primary coil terminal 1/15.
What are the terminal numbers for the secondary coil resistance measurement?
Measure secondary coil terminal 15/4.
What should you check for on hairline cracks inspection?
Check for hairline cracks and signs of burning.
What should you do if the plug is pressed out during inspection?
Check plug for tight fit - if pressed out, replace ignition coil.
What safety warning is given before working on the ignition system?
Always turn off ignition before working on the ignition system - dangerous high voltage!
Where can you find instructions for working on ignition system?
Refer to page 12-0 for instructions for working on ignition system.
What callout numbers are visible in the ignition coil diagrams?
The diagrams show callout numbers 1, 4, 15, and S marking different terminals and connections on the ignition coil.
On which page can I find information about DME troubleshooting test procedures?
DME troubleshooting test procedures can be found on page 12-111.
What page contains the engine electric layout for M3 models?
The engine electric layout for M3 models is on page 12-106.
Where can I find information about the 55-pin plug connections?
Information about 55-pin plug connections can be found on page 12-107/3.
Which page covers the fuel supply system information?
Fuel supply system information is covered on page 12-114/1.
What chapter section does this index page cover?
This index page covers Chapter 12 - Engine Electrical Equipment.
On which page can I find information about starter troubleshooting?
Starter troubleshooting information can be found on page 12-50.
What page covers the procedure for removing and installing the starter?
The procedure for removing and installing the starter is covered on page 12-51.
Where can I find instructions for replacing the solenoid switch?
Instructions for replacing the solenoid switch can be found on page 12-51.
What page contains information about replacing carbon brushes?
Information about replacing carbon brushes is on page 12-53.
On which page would I find procedures for disassembling and assembling the starter?
Procedures for disassembling and assembling the starter are on page 12-52.
What terminals should be connected when using a BMW service test unit or ohmmeter to check the pulse transmitter?
Connect the BMW service test unit (M 06) or ohmmeter on plug pins terminals 5 and 6 of the plug.
What should be done if the nominal coil resistance value is not reached during checking?
Check plug connection on distributor or, if necessary, replace pulse transmitter coil.
What voltage range should be produced when cranking the engine at 200 to 300 rpm?
Voltage of 1.0 to 2.0 V should be produced.
What tool is needed to remove the pulse transmitter gear?
Knock down dowel pin with an impact mandrel and take off pulse transmitter gear (rotor).
What should be lubricated during installation of the pulse transmitter?
Lubricate connecting rod with grease at opening.
What is distance 'A' referring to in the pulse transmitter installation?
Distance 'A' refers to the pulse transmitter distance that should be checked and corrected by loosening and centering the carrier plate.
What components are numbered 1 through 6 in the distributor plug diagram?
The numbers 1 through 6 indicate the terminal positions on the distributor plug connector for testing the pulse transmitter.
What test equipment is mentioned for connecting to the ignition control unit?
Connect multimeter (M 02) and oscilloscope (M 22) of BMW service test unit on disconnected ignition control unit plug terminals 5 and 6.
What pattern should appear on the oscilloscope screen during testing?
The voltage waveform shown in the graph should appear on screen, displaying a pattern with peaks of 1.0 to 2.0 V.
What is the first step when replacing the pulse transmitter?
Remove distributor as referenced in section 12 11 060, then unscrew vacuum control and let it hang down.
What should be checked between the pulse transmitter and pulse transmitter gear?
Check distance 'A' between pulse transmitter and pulse transmitter gear, adjusting if necessary.
What procedure should be followed after connecting the BMW service test unit for checking the ignition coil?
Carry out engine test step 09. Observe oscillograph - ignition voltage and ignition voltage deviation must agree with nominal values.
What are the multimeter terminals for measuring ignition coil resistance?
Terminal 1/15 for primary coil and terminal 15/4 for secondary coil resistance measurement.
What safety precaution must be observed before working on the ignition system?
Always turn off ignition before working on the ignition system - dangerous high voltage! Refer to page 12-0 for instructions for working on ignition system.
What visual signs indicate that an ignition coil should be replaced?
Check for hairline cracks and signs of burning. Check plug (S) for tight fit - if pressed out, replace ignition coil.
What are the first steps to remove an ignition coil?
Pull off protective cap and ignition lead (terminal 4). Unscrew connections (terminal 1 and 15). Unscrew holder and take off ignition coil.
What should be verified when installing a new ignition coil?
Check new ignition coil for correct code number and color label.
What component is numbered as 15 in the ignition coil removal diagram?
Terminal 15 is one of the electrical connections that must be unscrewed when removing the ignition coil.
What component is numbered as 4 in the ignition coil diagram?
Terminal 4 is the ignition lead connection that must be pulled off along with the protective cap during removal.
What test equipment is required for checking ignition coil operation?
BMW service test unit for oscillograph testing and a multimeter (M 06) for resistance measurements.
What does the oscillograph display show during ignition coil testing?
The oscillograph displays ignition voltage waveforms with time scale markings, showing ignition voltage patterns that must agree with nominal values.
Where can specifications for ignition coil nominal values be found?
See Specifications section and nominal value microfiche as referenced at the bottom of the page.
What is the main component shown in this transistor ignition control unit connection plan?
The main component is the Transistor Ignition Control Unit, with connection plans shown for both the Bosch TCii Control Unit and the Siemens/Telefunken TCii-S Control Unit.
What does terminal 1 connect to on the Bosch TCii Control Unit?
Terminal 1 connects to the ignition coil on the Bosch TCii Control Unit.
Which terminal provides the ground connection on the Bosch control unit?
Terminal 31 provides the ground connection on the Bosch control unit.
What are the three functions of terminal TD on the Siemens/Telefunken control unit?
Terminal TD connects to fuel pump relay, to L-Jetronic control unit, and to tachometer.
What does terminal 15 represent on both control units?
Terminal 15 represents the power supply connection on both the Bosch and Siemens/Telefunken control units.
Which terminals handle the pulse transmitter function?
Terminals A+/B- (terminals 5/6) handle the pulse transmitter function on the Bosch unit, while terminal +/- handles it on the Siemens/Telefunken unit.
What does terminal S connect to on the Siemens/Telefunken control unit?
Terminal S connects to starter terminal 50 on the Siemens/Telefunken control unit.
How many numbered connection points are shown in the bottom circular diagram?
The bottom circular diagram shows 6 numbered connection points, labeled 1 through 6.
What is the terminal designation for the alternator charge indicator on models until 1985?
The terminal designation for the alternator charge indicator is D+.
Which terminal is used for the coolant temperature transmitter on pre-1986 models?
Terminal FT is used for the coolant temperature transmitter on pre-1986 models.
What does terminal 15s provide power for on models until 1985?
Terminal 15s provides power supply with ignition turned on - fuse protection.
On 1986 and later models, what is connected to terminal A?
On 1986 and later models, terminal A is connected to the diagnosis lead for airbag.
What is the difference between terminals 15s and 15u on pre-1986 models?
Terminal 15s provides power supply with ignition turned on with fuse protection, while terminal 15u provides power supply with ignition turned on but without fuse protection.
Which terminal designation is used for the electric fuel pump on models since 1986?
Terminal EP is used for the electric fuel pump on models since 1986.
What function does terminal dyn serve on both model years?
Terminal dyn serves the oil level dynamic function on both model years.
How many terminals are listed for the 1986 and later models connection plan?
20 terminals are listed for the 1986 and later models connection plan.
What is terminal 50 used for on both model years?
Terminal 50 is used for power while starting on both model years.
Which terminal provides oil pressure monitoring on 1986 and later models?
Terminal Öl provides oil pressure monitoring on 1986 and later models.
What is the first step when replacing a cylinder identifying sender?
Take off the cover.
On M20 engines, what should be done with the ignition lead after pulling off the ignition lead shielded plug of cylinder no. 6?
Cut off the ignition lead and cut off the sender on the ignition lead.
What additional step is required for M20 engines when disconnecting the cylinder identifying sender?
Disconnect the plug underneath the diagnosis socket.
What should be measured to check the sender according to the testing procedure?
Measure the resistance of coil between leads 1 and 2.
What leads are referenced for testing the cylinder identifying sender resistance?
Leads 1 and 2.
What type of value is specified for the resistance measurement but requires looking elsewhere for the actual specification?
Nominal value (with an asterisk indicating to see Specifications).
After replacing the sender, what type of connector needs to be installed?
Install a shielded connector.
What reference is provided for installing the shielded connector?
See 12 12 072 in Group 12.
What final step is mentioned for M20 engines after taking off the leads?
Plug on new sender.
What is the procedure code for checking vacuum advance control?
The procedure code is 12 63 075.
What are the initial steps to prepare for vacuum advance control testing?
Take off protective cap, remove advance control relay and pull off plug.
What simulator should be used for the vacuum advance control test?
Connect relay (3) and plug (4) on advance control simulator 12 1 460.
What position should switch 1 be set to on the simulator?
Set switch (1) on simulator to position A.
What test steps should be performed according to the simulator procedures?
Perform test steps A through D according to procedures printed on the simulator.
What does it mean when lamp MV is not on during the test?
If lamp MV is not on, this means the advance control box has vacuum.
What should you do if specified conditions are not found during the vacuum advance test?
Refer to troubleshooting chart for vacuum advance control, if the specified conditions are not found in the test.
What test equipment can be used as an alternative to the BMW simulator?
Connect BMW service test unit or BMW digital tester.
What engine test step should be performed for ignition timing?
Perform engine test step 06 or check ignition timing.
What happens to the ignition timing value when displayed by the simulator?
The ignition timing value displayed will be retarded approximately 20° on crankshaft by the simulator.
What do the resistance measurement points TW and TA represent?
TW = Water temperature and TA = Intake air temperature.
What does lamp 'tp' indicate during the test procedure?
Lamp 'tp' (load signal) will flash throughout the entire test.
What is the first step when removing the alternator?
Unscrew the negative terminal on the battery (in trunk).
What safety precaution must be taken when disconnecting the battery for alternator removal?
Only disconnect leads on battery, alternator and starter when engine is stopped. Also disconnect positive and negative leads when charging battery with a charger.
What component needs to be removed along with the air cleaner?
Take off air cleaner with air flow sensor.
What are the acceptable tester needle positions when checking belt tension?
The tester needle must be in the scale above green or yellow section.
What torque specification is given for tightening the drive belt?
Unscrew nut and turn tensioning wheel with a torque of approx. 7 Nm (5 ft. lbs.). Tighten nut.
What should be done after tightening the drive belt nut?
Recheck tightness with tester, correcting if necessary.
What components need to be unscrewed before removing the alternator?
Unscrew mounting bolts and unscrew leads.
What section reference is given for drive belt tightening during installation?
Tighten drive belt - 12 31 299.
What additional procedure may be required if the alternator was replaced?
If alternator was replaced, check and, if necessary, discharge gas tank - see Group 61, Pos. 61 21 015.
What are the terminal markings visible on the alternator in the bottom image?
The alternator shows D+ and B+ terminal markings.
What does callout number 2 represent in the engine electric layout?
Callout number 2 represents the Engine electric/electronic ground point.
What are the three components shown in the Relay Survey section?
The Relay Survey shows: 1 = DME, 2 = Electric fuel pumps, 3 = Oxygen sensor.
What sensor is shown in the image labeled as 'Coolant temperature sensor (DME) blue Temperature gage'?
The image shows the Coolant temperature sensor (DME) blue for the temperature gage.
What component is labeled as 'Inductive pulse sender' in the bottom left image?
The bottom left image shows the Inductive pulse sender component.
What is Test 6 for the DME system?
Test 6 is for the DME control unit and power supply.
Where can you find the code number and manufacturing date of the DME control unit?
The code number and manufacturing date of the DME control unit can be found in Group 13.
What should you do to supply power to the control unit when checking power supply?
Pull off relay 2 and bridge terminals 87 and 30 with a piece of wire to supply power to the control unit.
What voltage should terminals 85 (-) and 86 (+) have when checking relay 2 activation?
Terminals 85 (-) and 86 (+) should have voltage of approximately 12 V.
What test lead is used with the universal adapter for power supply testing?
A 35-pin test lead is used with the universal adapter for power supply testing.
Which pins should you check voltage on, such as connections 17 (-) and 35 (+)?
You should check voltage of pins, for example on connections 17 (-) and 35 (+).
What should you do if test results indicate the necessity to replace the control unit?
If test results indicate the necessity to replace the control unit, first make the periphery test with an universal adapter.
What is Test 6a for?
Test 6a is for ignition timing.
What should you do if the ignition timing check (P 06) shows 'no'?
If the ignition timing check shows 'no', replace the DME control unit.
What condition must be met regarding car wire harness plugs during testing?
Car wire harness plugs must remain connected during testing.
Where should you check if necessary for ground point and plug connection?
If necessary, check ground point and plug connection near the DME control unit, as shown in the figure.
What is Test 17/18 checking for in the exhaust system and catalytic converter?
Test 17/18 checks the exhaust system and catalytic converter for damage, tight fit and leaks.
What specific components should be inspected during Test 19 - Crankcase Vent?
During Test 19, check hoses for crankcase vent and oil dipstick for tight fit and leaks.
What should you do if the cooling system needs to be filled and bled during Test 20?
If necessary, fill and bleed the cooling system - see Group 17 for detailed procedures.
Where can you find additional service information referenced at the bottom of this page?
Additional service information can be found in Group 00, as referenced at the bottom of the page.
What types of problems should you look for when inspecting the exhaust system?
When inspecting the exhaust system, look for damage, improper fit, and leaks in both the exhaust system and catalytic converter.
What is the test number for checking the crankcase ventilation system?
Test 19 is designated for checking the crankcase vent system.
Which group should you reference for detailed cooling system fill and bleed procedures?
Reference Group 17 for detailed procedures on filling and bleeding the cooling system.
What should be checked for tight fit during the crankcase vent inspection?
During crankcase vent inspection, check both the hoses for crankcase vent and the oil dipstick for tight fit.
What are the two main aspects to check in the cooling system during Test 20?
Check both the coolant level and coolant concentration during Test 20 of the cooling system.
What should you inspect for leaks during Test 19?
During Test 19, inspect both the crankcase vent hoses and oil dipstick area for leaks.
What voltage should be measured on connection terminals 15 and 31 of the TCI control unit during Test 2?
Approximately 12 V should be measured on connection terminals 15 and 31 of the TCI control unit.
What is the first step required before checking the voltage supply for the TCI Control Unit?
Pull off plug on control unit and turn on ignition.
What does terminal 31 represent in both the Bosch and Siemens/Telefunken TCI control units?
Terminal 31 represents Ground in both control unit types.
If the voltage test on terminals 15 and 31 is not okay, what troubleshooting steps should be performed?

Check the routing of terminal 15w wire, including ignition lock connections, wire harness connections for car electric system, engine wire harness plug connections, and TCI control unit connections. The ground wire should be routed to the ground point on air collector (4th cylinder).
What does terminal 15 represent in the TCI control unit connector pinouts?
Terminal 15 represents Power supply in both the Bosch and Siemens/Telefunken control units.
What component is shown in the middle diagram with terminals numbered 1 through 6?
The middle diagram shows the TCI1-S Control Unit (Siemens/Telefunken) with the note that S = ignition timing retard while starting.
What does the 'S' designation mean in the Siemens/Telefunken TCI1-S control unit?
S = ignition timing retard while starting.
What is connected to terminal 1/16 in the Siemens/Telefunken control unit?
Terminal 1/16 is connected to the ignition coil.
Where is the ground point located for the TCI control unit ground wire?
The ground wire is routed to the ground point on air collector (4th cylinder).
What do terminals A+/B- represent in the Bosch TCI control unit?
Terminals A+/B- represent the Pulse transmitter in the Bosch control unit.
What reference should be consulted for more detailed wiring information related to this system?
See car or engine electric system wiring diagram.
What are the four main components shown in the gearbox unit diagram at the top left?
The four main components are: 1 Planet gearbox, 2 Release, 3 Pinion, and 4 Gearbox case.
What should you do with the thrust ring and retainer during disassembly?
Knock back thrust ring (1), pull off retainer (2) forward, remove burrs if applicable, then take off drive pinion.
What lubrication requirement is specified for the pinion bearing surface?
Clean bearing surface for pinion thoroughly and lubricate with grease.
What should you check when examining the drive pinion?
Turn drive pinion against stop. The pinion will be very easy to turn if the one-way clutch is worn.
What components need to be inspected for wear according to the bottom procedures?
Check bearing sleeve and teeth of pinion for wear, and check planet gears for wear.
What is the approximate distance specification mentioned for bearing installation?
Distance A = approx. 1 mm (0.039 in) when lubricating new bearing with grease and pressing in.
What three types of washers are identified in the retainer assembly?
The three washers are: 1 retainer, 2 Metal washer, and 3 Plastic washer.
What tool requirement is specified for bearing removal?
Check bearing sleeve, removing with a suitable puller if necessary.
What components are numbered 4, 5, and 6 in the bearing assembly diagram?
Component 4 is the bearing cover, 5 are washers, and 6 is the bearing sleeve.
What method is recommended for checking the bearing condition?
Check bearing, driving it out with a suitable mandrel if necessary, then lubricate new bearing with grease and press in.
What are the three components identified for 1986 models in the engine electrical layout?
1 Control unit for DME (see Gr. 13), 2 Control unit for idle speed (see Gr. 13), 3 Plug for car electric system, fuel pump relay
What wire colors are specified for the transmission versions plug (item 4)?
Green/yellow - blue/brown, not used for automatics (lean mixture), connected for manuals
What four temperature-related components are identified in the engine bay?
1 Temperature switch 45° C (113° F) for idle speed control, 2 Coolant temperature sensor for DME, 3 Temperature transmitter, 4 Temperature time switch
What is the installation instruction for the twenty pin engine wire harness plug?
The screw-on cap engages in final position
What sensors are identified by plugs B and D in the engine bay?
Plug (gray) for reference mark sensor (B) and plug for speed sensor (D)
Where is the pressure sensor located according to the diagram?
The pressure sensor (see Gr. 13) is shown in the lower right area of the engine bay
What should you always do when working on the electrical system for TCI and DME?

Always disconnect battery or interrupt power supply to ignition control unit and ignition coil when working on the electrical system (charging battery or welding, etc.) - dangerous primary and secondary voltage as well as danger of destroying the ignition system.
What happens if you start the engine after removing the distributor cap or disconnecting wire on ignition coil term. 4?
Never start the engine after removal of distributor cap and/or disconnection of wire on ignition coil term. 4 - pull off plug on ignition control unit.
When should you never disconnect the battery or leads on the alternator and starter?
Never disconnect the battery or leads on the alternator and starter while engine is running.
What type of parts should be installed for TCI and DME systems?
Only install specified original BMW parts.
Which ignition coil terminal should never have a shielded capacitor or test lamp connected?
Never connect a shielded capacitor or test lamp on term. 1 of the ignition coil.
What is the restriction for connecting ignition coil term. 1 to ground or B+?
Never connect wire of ignition coil term. 1 on ground or B+. Consequently the ignition coil term. 1 wire must not be used to prevent engine starting when service installing a burglar alarm system.
What should you do when checking compression for TCI or DME systems?
When checking the compression, pull off plug on control unit for TCI or master relay for fuel injection (relay no. 2) for DME.
What is the minimum shielding requirement for the secondary side of the ignition system?
The secondary side (high voltage side) of the ignition system must be shielded with at least 4 k-ohms, whereby the original distributor rotor with 1 k-ohm shielded resistor must be installed.
What distributor rotor resistance should not be used for radio shielding?
Do not use a 5 k-ohm distributor rotor for the shielding of radio and/or communication equipment.
What ignition systems are covered by these working instructions?
These instructions are for working on Transistorized Coil-Type Ignition (TCI) and Digital Motor Electronics (DME).
What are the potential dangers mentioned when working on the electrical system?
The dangers include dangerous primary and secondary voltage as well as danger of destroying the ignition system.
What is the original distributor rotor shielded resistor value?
The original distributor rotor has a 1 k-ohm shielded resistor.
What is the section number and title for replacing/checking the distributor rotor?
Section 12 11 111 REPLACING / CHECKING DISTRIBUTOR ROTOR.
What safety precaution must be taken before working on the ignition system?
Always turn off ignition before working on dangerous high power ignition systems! Remove distributor cap - 12 11 091.
What should be checked when installing ignition lead plugs?
Make sure plugs fit tight on ignition leads and in distributor cap. Check firing order.
What components are numbered 1-6 in the exploded view diagram?
The exploded view shows numbered components of the distributor assembly, with component 6 appearing to be a cover or cap, and components 1-5 representing internal distributor parts.
What should be inspected when only removing the distributor cap and not replacing it?
Check points and slip ring carbon brushes. Inspect inside for hairline cracks.
What should be checked on protective caps during installation?
Check seal (6) when installing protective caps (1 and 2).
What installation requirement is specified for the distributor rotor?
Installation: Tightening torque - see Specifications.
What checks should be performed on the distributor rotor?
Check resistance in distributor rotor. Check casting compound for cracks and burns.
What part numbers are visible in the service manual images?
How should the distributor cap installation be checked?
Check seal and inspect inside of distributor cap during installation.
What is the first step in the distributor rotor replacement procedure?
Pull off ignition lead plugs.
What are the three main components shown in the arrangement diagram for the distributor?
The three main components are: 12 - Insulator, 13 - Pulse transmitter, and 14 - Carrier plate.
What should be done after finishing the installation of the pulse transmitter?
After finishing installation, adjust ignition timing according to section 12 11 005.
What steps are required to access the vacuum control for replacement?
Take off protective cap and distributor cap, then unscrew and turn distributor for better accessibility, and finally unscrew vacuum control.
What should be applied to the eye of the pull rod during installation?
Lubricate the eye of pull rod with grease during installation.
What must be checked after connecting the pull rod during installation?
Check that pivoting plate moves easily after connecting the pull rod.
What timing adjustment is required after completing the vacuum control installation?
Complete installation and adjust ignition timing according to section 12 11 005.
How should the BMW service test unit be connected for checking?
Connect BMW service test unit according to operating instructions and perform test step '06 Engine'.
What test should be performed if vacuum hose is connected on the intake air manifold?
Perform test step '06 Engine' if vacuum hose is connected on the intake air manifold.
What timing difference should be noted between disconnected and connected vacuum hose?
Note difference in ignition timing between disconnected and connected vacuum hose - 13 to 17° before TDC on crankshaft.
From which direction should the pull rod be disconnected?
Disconnect pull rod from below.
What should be checked regarding the arrangement of carrier plate connections?
Check arrangement of carrier plate connections as shown in the installation instructions.
What is the specific procedure for replacing speed and reference mark sensors?
Unscrew screws of speed and reference mark sensors (D and B) and pull out sensors. For installation, mark new reference mark sensor (B) with a piece of tape.
What components are labeled as B and D in the sensor diagrams?
B is the Reference mark sensor and D is the Speed sensor.
What testing equipment should be connected to check the speed sensor signal?
Connect oscilloscope (M 22/23) on + and - connections of speed sensor. Turn engine with hand after connecting.
What is the correct signal pattern for the speed sensor?
Signal shown in the figure should be displayed. Only the shape is important when evaluating the signal - not the amplitude height.
How should you test the reference mark sensor resistance?
Measure resistance of sensor coil (M 06) on + and - of plug.
What should you do if the oscillograph deviates when checking the reference mark sensor?
If oscillograph deviates, remove sensor and check for dirt (grease, burrs, rust), cleaning if necessary. Check reference mark, replacing pin for flywheel if necessary.
What are the numbered components 1 and 2 in the protective sleeve diagram?
Component 1 is the protective sleeve and component 2 is the clip.
What installation steps are required after removing the protective sleeve and clip?
Coat seals with Molykote paste. Keep grease and dirt off of face surface on sensors.
Which plug belongs to which sensor during installation?
Plug marked with tape belongs to gray plug.
What testing procedure is specified for initial sensor testing?
Disconnect plug. Connect BMW service test unit to operating instructions (M 06/22/23). Use universal test leads.
What should be done to remove the sensors from their holder?
Press plug of sensor head out of holder.
What is the first step before accessing the speed and reference mark sensors?
Unscrew shield.
What procedure should be performed before replacing the solenoid according to section 12 41 041?
Remove starter according to section 12 41 020 and take off cover.
What voltage should be applied when checking the power consumption of activating and holding coils in the solenoid?
12V should be applied when checking power consumption of activating and holding coils in solenoid.
What safety warning is given when unscrewing solenoids 1 and 2?
Don't turn wire connector while tightening - danger of short circuit.
In the solenoid replacement diagram, what does callout number 1 indicate?
Callout number 1 indicates one of the solenoids to be removed.
What components should be checked for ground contact when testing the exciter coil?
Check exciter coil, carbon brush holder and armature coil for ground contact.
What should be done with pin 3 during installation after taking off the solenoid and spring?
Check pin 3 for wear and lubricate with grease.
What tool is mentioned for checking armature for shorted turns?
Standard tester is mentioned for checking armature for shorted turns.
Which cars are noted as not applicable for exciter coil checking?
Cars with permanent magnets (M 3) are not applicable for exciter coil checking.
What three numbered components are shown in the solenoid removal sequence?
The three numbered components are: 1 and 2 (solenoids) and 3 (pin to be disconnected).
What should be disconnected after taking off solenoid 1 and spring 2?
Disconnect pin 3 after taking off solenoid 1 and spring 2.
What reference is provided at the bottom of the page for additional information?
See Specifications is referenced at the bottom of the page for additional information.
What is the part number designation shown for the solenoid replacement procedure?
The part number designation shown is 12 41 041 for replacing solenoid.
What are the resistance values for the 80A and 140A alternator rotor coil break and shorted turn test?
For the 80A alternator, the resistance should be 2.8 ohms ± 10%. For the 140A alternator, the resistance should be 2.65 ohms ± 10%.
How do you check the rotor coil ground contact test on a Bosch alternator?
Hold test leads for resistance tests on slip ring and rotor shaft. The nominal value should display 999 k-ohms.
What is the expected display value for a good rotor coil ground contact test?
The nominal value should be infinity, displayed as 999 k-ohms.
How do you perform the stator coil ground contact test?
Hold test leads for resistance tests on soldering point and stator/coil carrier. The nominal value should equal to display of 999 k-ohms.
What should you check when performing the stator coil break test?
Compare resistance values of leads 1/2, 1/3 and 2/3 with an ohmmeter - they should be the same. Checking for shorted turns can be performed with a standard tester.
How do you test the positive diodes in the alternator?
Hold negative lead on B+ stud and positive lead on one of the positive diode connections. Display with good diodes should show polarity.
What should you do if you find a faulty diode during testing?
Replace entire diode plate in case of a faulty diode - see 12 31 691.
What resistance value should the 90A alternator show during rotor coil testing?
The 90A alternator should show 2.9 ohms ± 10% resistance.
What tool is recommended for checking the Bosch alternator in electric test mode?
Check with a BMW Service Tester.
What resistance specification applies to the 65A alternator?
The 65A alternator should have 3.4 ohms ± 10% resistance.
What is the resistance specification for the 115A alternator rotor coil?
The 115A alternator should show 2.65 ohms ± 10% resistance.
What are the testing requirements before checking the alternator and voltage regulator?
The testing requirements are: correct connections on charged battery, correct connections on alternator and starter, good ground connection between engine and body, and tight drive belt.
What should you do if the indicator lamp stays on continuously?
Remove voltage regulator and check carbon brushes, replacing if necessary (see 12 31 200). Check the distance 'V' for new condition - approximately 12 mm (0.472").
What distance measurement is specified for new carbon brushes?
The distance 'V' for new condition should be approximately 12 mm (0.472").
What installation checks should be performed after alternator service?
Check slip rings for wear, fine grinding and polishing if necessary. Connect BMW service test unit. Start engine and compare test values with nominal values.
What oscillograph pattern indicates a defective alternator with defective power or exciter diode?
The oscillograph shows an irregular wave pattern with varying amplitude, labeled as 'Oscillographs of Defective Alternator: Defective power or exciter diode.'
What does the oscillograph pattern show for a shorted turn of stator coil?
The oscillograph shows a regular wave pattern with consistent amplitude but reduced peaks, indicating a shorted turn of stator coil.
What condition indicates the voltage regulator needs to be replaced?

If the battery charge indicator lamp goes out while engine is running and the regulating voltage is not reached - harmonic wave ratio and oscillograph okay (as shown) - the voltage regulator has to be replaced (see 12 32 000).
What are the positive and negative terminal markings shown in the alternator diagram?
The alternator diagram shows terminals marked as 'B+' (positive) and 'D+' (positive excitation terminal).
Where can you find nominal values for comparison during testing?
See nominal value microfiche for the test values to compare with during engine testing.
What section should be referenced for voltage regulator replacement procedures?
Reference section 12 32 000 for voltage regulator replacement procedures.
What section of the BMW E30 M3 service manual covers troubleshooting engine electrical and DME issues?
Section 12-108 covers troubleshooting engine electric and DME.
What diagnostic system is used for troubleshooting engine electrical and DME problems since the introduction of M 1.1?
BMW Diagnosis Test is used for troubleshooting engine electrical and DME problems since the introduction of M 1.1.
Where can the increment wheel for single-sender Motronic be found?
The increment wheel (1) for single-sender Motronic is recognizable on the increment wheel and is shown in the diagram.
What component is labeled as item 1 in the diagram?
Item 1 in the diagram is the increment wheel for single-sender Motronic.
What type of Motronic system does this increment wheel apply to?
This increment wheel applies to single-sender Motronic systems.
How is the increment wheel identified in the engine bay?
The increment wheel is recognizable on the increment wheel itself for single-sender Motronic systems.
What engine management system version introduced the use of BMW Diagnosis Test?
BMW Diagnosis Test has been used since the introduction of M 1.1.
What is the main focus of this troubleshooting section?
This section focuses on troubleshooting engine electric and DME (Digital Motor Electronics) systems.
What visual method is used to show the increment wheel location?
A black and white photograph with an arrow pointing to the increment wheel (labeled as 1) is used to show its location.
What temperature range defines a cold engine condition for troubleshooting purposes?
A cold engine is defined as oil temperature less than 20°C or 68°F.
If I have a warm engine that's hard to start, which test positions should I check according to the troubleshooting chart?
For a warm engine that's hard to start (symptom 5), check test positions 1, 2, 4, 16, 17, and 18 according to the X marks in the chart.
What components should be tested if the engine has erratic idling during warm-up phase?

For erratic idling during warm-up phase (symptom 6), test the speed sensor/reference mark sensor (position 1), ignition coil (position 2), and oxygen sensor/emission control and EGR system (position 10).
Where can I find additional information about fuel injection troubleshooting?
Refer to 'Troubleshooting Fuel Injection' in Group 13 for other test positions.
What are the testing requirements mentioned for troubleshooting digital motor electronics?

Testing requirements include: engine in perfect running condition (timing, compression, oil, carbon deposits, etc.), starting system in perfect condition (battery voltage, starter, ignition lock, etc.), correct fuel in tank (octane rating, leaded/unleaded, dirt, etc.), and connections and ground points according to wiring diagram.
If the engine has poor acceleration and high fuel consumption, which systems should I check?

For poor acceleration/final output and high fuel consumption (symptoms 13-14), check oxygen sensor/emission control and EGR (position 10), active carbon filter/purge valve (position 11), fuel supply (position 15), intake system (position 16), catalytic converter (position 17), and exhaust system (position 18).
What does test position 6 refer to and in which group can I find more information?
Test position 6 refers to DME control unit/ignition timing. No specific group reference is provided for this test position.
If I have CO/HC readings that are not correct, which components need to be tested?

For incorrect CO/HC readings (symptom 15), test oxygen sensor/emission control and EGR (position 10), fuel supply (position 15), intake system (position 16), catalytic converter (position 17), exhaust system (position 18), and crankcase vent/air hoses (position 19).
Which group contains information about the active carbon filter/purge valve system?
The active carbon filter/purge valve system information can be found in Group 13/16.
What symptom pathway leads to checking the cooling system?
The cooling system (test position 20) should be checked when troubleshooting various engine performance issues, as indicated by the X mark in the troubleshooting chart matrix.
What are the three relays shown in the relay survey for the M20 engine?
The three relays are: 1 Master relay, 2 Fuel pump relay, and 3 Oxygen sensor relay.
What is the reference number shown for the upper image in the relay survey?
The reference number is 30 12 914.
Where is the M20 DME control unit located according to the manual?
The M20 DME control unit is located in the glove box.
What is the reference number for the lower image showing the DME control unit?
The reference number is 30 12 923.
Which relay is labeled as number 1 in the relay survey?
The Master relay is labeled as number 1 in the relay survey.
Which relay is positioned as number 2 in the relay configuration?
The Fuel pump relay is positioned as number 2 in the relay configuration.
What type of control unit is shown in the lower photograph?
A DME (Digital Motor Electronics) control unit is shown in the lower photograph.
Which relay handles oxygen sensor functions in the M20 system?
The Oxygen sensor relay, which is labeled as number 3, handles oxygen sensor functions.
What engine type do these electrical components belong to?
These electrical components belong to the M20 engine.
How are the relays numbered in the relay survey diagram?
The relays are numbered 1, 2, and 3, with arrows pointing to each relay position.
What terminal number is used for the ground connection in the diagnosis plug?
Terminal 31 is used for the ground connection.
Which terminal designation is used for the temperature gauge signal?
Terminal FT is used for the temperature gauge signal.
What is the function of terminal L in the diagnosis plug connections?
Terminal L provides the integrator output for CO adjustments for Engine M 10 B 18, and oxygen sensor signal for Engine M 30 B 34.
What wire colors are used for the service indicator reset connection?
The service indicator reset connection uses white/green wire colors.
Which pin number corresponds to the D+ alternator charge indicator in the diagnosis socket?
Pin 12 corresponds to the D+ alternator charge indicator.
What terminal number is used for the starting pulse for starter?
Terminal 50 is used for the starting pulse for starter.
What wire color is used for Terminal 30 in the diagnosis socket connections?
Terminal 30 uses red wire color.
What is the function of pin 18 in the diagnosis socket?
Pin 18 is the PGSF for DME control unit programming.
Which terminal provides the power supply for ignition?
Terminal 15 provides the power supply for ignition.
What wire colors are used for the TXD data lead connection?
The TXD data lead connection uses white/violet wire colors.
What is the first step when removing the voltage regulator?
Unscrew negative terminal on battery (in trunk).
What should be removed along with the air cleaner?
Take off air cleaner with air flow sensor.
What is the proper installation sequence for mounting the voltage regulator?
Mount regulator at first with one bolt screwed on finger tight, then press alternator to final installed position carefully, install and tighten all bolts.
What should be checked on the spring contacts during voltage regulator work?
