Clean contact surfaces and check tension of spring contacts, correcting if necessary.
How should the voltage regulator bolts be removed?
Unscrew bolts and take off voltage regulator carefully.
What should be inspected on the slip rings?
Check slip rings for wear, fine grinding if necessary.
What should be done with the battery during this procedure?
Remove battery. Check gas discharging tank for battery, discharging if necessary - see 61 21 015.
What reference number should be consulted for battery discharging procedures?
See 61 21 015 for battery discharging procedures.
What is shown in image M 21 12 078?
The voltage regulator installation showing the mounting position and bolt configuration.
What does image M 21 12 080 demonstrate?
The slip rings that should be checked for wear and fine grinding if necessary.
What component needs to be removed for M3 models along with the air cleaner?
Take off air cleaner with air flow sensor. For M3 models, remove intake manifold and air cleaner - see 11 61 050.
What additional step is required for 1986 and later models during starter removal?
Since 1986 Models: Disconnect plugs for reference mark sensor B (gray) and speed sensor D.
What components are labeled D and B in the lower left image?
D and B are the plugs for reference mark sensor B (gray) and speed sensor that need to be disconnected on 1986 and later models.
What should be done with the coolant during starter removal?
Drain coolant. Disconnect heater hoses. Unscrew starter mounting nuts.
What is an alternative method for removing the bottom starter mounting nut?
Bottom nut could also be unscrewed from below for better accessibility.
What must be done during installation regarding coolant?
Pour in coolant and bleed cooling system - see 17 00 039.
What special tool is required for removing the starter nuts?
Unscrew nuts with a starter wrench.
What section should be referenced for bleeding the cooling system?
See 17 00 039 for bleeding the cooling system.
What components need to be unscrewed in addition to disconnecting hoses?
Unscrew support and lines, and unscrew starter mounting nuts.
What is the source of supply for the starter wrench tool?
Source of Supply: HWB
What is the clearance specification for the TDC position transmitter?
The clearance A should be 0.2 to 2.0 mm (0.008 to 0.080 inches).
What safety precaution is given before working on the distributor cap?
Always turn off ignition before working on dangerous high voltage ignition systems!
How do you remove the diagnosis socket from its holder?
Open lid on diagnosis socket, lift clips 1 and 2, and press diagnosis socket out of holder.
What are the wire colors for positions 1, 2, and 3 in the transmitter lead connector?
1 = Black wire, 2 = Shielding, 3 = Yellow wire.
What component should be checked for resistance and insulation?
Check resistance of coil and insulation, maintaining distance of 0.2 to 2.0 mm (0.008 to 0.080 inches) to vibration damper.
What is the correct procedure for removing the fan?
Unscrew fan with left-hand threads, then unscrew fan cowl and lift out together with unscrewed fan.
What connector terminals are labeled in the wiring diagram?
The diagram shows terminals Kl.31, Kl.50, FT, D+, Kl.1, Kl.30, and Kl.15.
How do you access the distributor cap for removal?
Take off retainers, pull off cover, then unscrew screws for distributor cap.
What is the first step in installing the TDC position transmitter?
Lift position transmitter out of clamp, then during installation make sure transmitter fits correctly.
What reference should be consulted for detailed specifications?
See Specifications (as noted with asterisk at bottom of page).
What special threading characteristic does the fan have?
The fan has left-hand threads.
What is the final step shown for the transmitter connector?
Unlock hooks and push round female plugs (1-3) for transmitter lead out of receptacle, then mount wire.
What is the procedure reference number for replacing the diode plate?
The procedure reference number is 12 31 691.
What must be done first when servicing a Bosch alternator diode plate?
Unsolder stator coil on diode plate.
What caution is given regarding heat when working on the diode plate?
Excessive heat from the soldering iron would destroy the diodes.
What are the steps to remove the diode plate after unsoldering the stator coil?
Unscrew screws, then take out diode plate.
What diagram number shows the alternator with the stator coil unsoldered?
Diagram 630 12 178 shows the alternator with the stator coil unsoldered from the diode plate.
What diagram number illustrates the diode plate with screws to be removed?
Diagram 630 12 173 shows the diode plate with arrows pointing to the screws that need to be removed.
What should be checked during installation of the diode plate?
Check condition of insulating sleeves and washers, replacing if necessary.
What diagram number shows the installation view with insulating components?
Diagram 630 12 179 shows the installation view highlighting the insulating sleeves and washers.
What components should be replaced if found to be in poor condition during installation?
The insulating sleeves and washers should be replaced if necessary.
What is the main risk when using excessive heat during the unsoldering process?
Excessive heat from the soldering iron would destroy the diodes.
In what sequence should the diode plate removal be performed?
First unsolder the stator coil on the diode plate, then unscrew the screws, and finally take out the diode plate.
What is the purpose of the holding circuit in the Motronic system?
The holding circuit makes sure that the Motronic master relay remains activated for another 3 sec. after switching off ignition lock terminal 15 and stopping the engine.
Which terminals are used in the Motronic with holding circuit since 12.86?
Terminals 27 and 36 are used in the Motronic with holding circuit since 12.86.
What happens to terminals 27 and 36 in Motronic systems without holding circuit before 12.86?
Terminals 27 and 36 are not used in Motronic systems without holding circuit before 12.86.
How long does the Motronic master relay remain activated after ignition is turned off?
The Motronic master relay remains activated for another 3 seconds after switching off ignition lock terminal 15 and stopping the engine.
What is the module designation shown in both wiring diagrams?
The module designation shown in both wiring diagrams is 1.1.
Which terminal numbers are visible in the Motronic relay connector?
The terminal numbers visible in the Motronic relay connector are 27, 37, and 36.
What date marks the transition to using the holding circuit in Motronic systems?
The date 12.86 marks the transition to using the holding circuit in Motronic systems.
What is the main difference between the two wiring diagrams shown?

The main difference is that the top diagram shows Motronic with holding circuit (since 12.86) where terminals 27 and 36 are used, while the bottom diagram shows Motronic without holding circuit (before 12.86) where terminals 27 and 36 are not used.
Which terminals connect to the positive power sources (15 and 30)?
Terminal 15 connects to the ignition power source and terminal 30 connects to the battery power source.
What page number and section is this diagram from?
This diagram is from page 12-107/4 from the Holding Circuit Wiring Diagram section for M 1.1 Motronic.
What should you check the ignition coil wires for during Test 2?
Check the wires for tight fit and examine the connection plate and ignition lead contacts for traces of burning, cracks and oxidation.
Where can you find the code number for the ignition coil?
The code number of the ignition coil can be found in section 12 13 009.
What two electrical properties should be checked for the ignition coil's primary and secondary coils?
Check resistance (M 06) and inductivity (M 07) of the primary and secondary coils.
What reference section provides the specifications for ignition coil resistance and inductivity testing?
See section 12 13 009 for the resistance and inductivity specifications.
What are the two main checks required for spark plugs in Test 3?
Check spark plugs for tight fit and leaks, and check the insulator for signs of leakage current.
What two spark plug specifications need to be verified during testing?
Check spark plug type and electrode gap, and check resistance.
What component is labeled as number 4 in the diagram?
Number 4 indicates a component in the ignition system assembly, visible in the lower portion of the diagram.
What part number is visible in the diagram for the ignition coil assembly?
The part number 630 12 907 is visible for the upper ignition coil assembly, and 630 12 is shown for the lower component.
What should you look for when checking the spark plug insulator?
Check the insulator for signs of leakage current.
What special tool is required to hold the pulley when removing the alternator 80 A voltage regulator?
Special Tool 12 31 000 is required to hold the pulley when removing the voltage regulator.
What component needs to be removed after taking off the fan during alternator removal?
The voltage regulator (12 32 000) needs to be removed after taking off the fan.
What should you do with the housing sections before unscrewing the bolts?
Mark the housing sections to each other before unscrewing the bolts and pulling the housing sections apart.
What specific terminals need to have their nuts unscrewed when removing the shielded capacitor?
The nuts on the B+ and D+ terminals need to be unscrewed when removing the shielded capacitor.
How is the diode plate removed after unscrewing the capacitor?
The diode plate is removed with the stator coil after unscrewing the shielded capacitor.
What components should be checked during installation according to the manual?
Check the condition of insulating sleeves and washers, replacing if necessary during installation.
What is shown in the diagram labeled 630 12 270?
The arrangement of washers is shown in diagram 630 12 270.
What procedure is described for the bearing cap screws and end plate?
Unscrew the bearing cap screws and take off the end plate.
What is the first step shown for disassembling the diode plate?
The first step is to unscrew the screws for the diode plate.
What alternator type is being serviced in this section?
The 80 A alternator is being serviced in this disassembly/assembly section.
What is the purpose of marking the housing sections?
Marking the housing sections to each other ensures proper alignment when reassembling the alternator components.
What should be done with the pulley nut during voltage regulator removal?
The pulley nut should be unscrewed while holding the pulley with Special Tool 12 31 000.
What chapter number covers Engine Electrical Equipment?
Chapter 12 covers Engine Electrical Equipment.
On which page can I find information about TCI troubleshooting?
TCI troubleshooting information can be found on page 12-20.
What is the procedure code for ignition timing adjustment?
The procedure code for ignition timing adjustment is 12 11 005.
Where can I find instructions for replacing the voltage regulator?
Instructions for voltage regulator replacement can be found on page 12-46, under procedure code 12 32 000.
What page covers the procedure for checking the pulse transmitter in the distributor?
The procedure for checking the pulse transmitter in the distributor is covered on page 12-3, under code 150.
Which procedure covers alternator belt tightening and what is its code?
Alternator belt tightening is covered under procedure code 299 and can be found on page 12-42.
What should you remove first when replacing carbon brushes on the starter?
First unscrew the mounting bolts (1), then remove the dust cap (2).
What components are indicated by callout numbers 3, 4, and 5 in the carbon brush replacement diagram?
Number 3 is the lock washer, number 4 is the shims, and number 5 is the seal.
What is the acceptable range for machine insulation between plates on the commutator?
The machine insulation between plates should be approximately 0.5 to 0.7 mm (0.020 to 0.028") deep.
What voltage should be applied when checking the power input of engaging and holding coils in the solenoid switch?
Apply 12V when checking the power input of engaging and holding coils in the solenoid switch.
What should be checked on the commutator and when might fine grinding be necessary?
Check the commutator for wear, and fine grinding may be necessary if wear is found.
What precaution should be taken when soldering in new carbon brushes?
When soldering in new carbon brushes, make sure that copper leads are not hardened with flowing solder.
What components should be checked for ground contact during starter inspection?
Check the exciter coil, carbon brush holder, and armature coil for ground contact.
How should you install the components during carbon brush replacement?
During installation, take up axial play with the shims (4).
What should be done to remove all carbon brushes from the starter?
Remove the holder and pole housing, then unsolder or cut off all carbon brushes.
What should be checked on the armature after repairing?
Check the armature for shorted turns after repairing.
What type of tester should be used for checking armature shorts?
Use a standard tester to check the armature for shorted turns.
What signal must Terminal 3 have when checking the speed signal for the idle control unit?
Terminal 3 must have 'terminal 1 signal' with the engine running.
Which terminals should I connect the ohmmeter to when checking the idle signal?
Connect ohmmeter (M 06) between terminals 4 and 12.
What should I do if the voltmeter is not displaying at least 9 volts during the idle signal test?
Adjust or replace throttle switch and adjust cable.
How far should I press down the accelerator pedal during the idle signal test?
Press down accelerator pedal several centimeters.
What corrective action should be taken if the voltmeter doesn't show approximately 0 volt when pressing the accelerator?
Adjust or replace throttle switch and adjust cable.
What conclusion can be drawn if both idle signal tests pass successfully?
Idle signal for idle control unit is okay.
What are the two main signal checks performed for the idle control unit?
Speed Signal and Idle Signal checks.
What component is commonly adjusted or replaced when idle signal tests fail?
Throttle switch, and the cable should also be adjusted.
What engine types are covered for DME troubleshooting with the BMW Diagnosing System?
The M 20 B 20 and M 20 B 25 engine types are covered for DME troubleshooting with the BMW Diagnosing System.
What is the idle speed specification for both M 20 B 20 and M 20 B 25 engines?
The idle speed specification is 760 ± 40 rpm for both M 20 B 20 and M 20 B 25 engines.
What CO level percentage is specified for the M 20 B 20 engine?
The CO level for the M 20 B 20 engine is 0.7 ± 0.5% by volume.
How do you initiate DME troubleshooting with the BMW Diagnosing System?
Insert diskette and connect diagnosing unit on the BMW Service Tester, then select 01 DME. If applicable, carry out brief test with brief test only display whether there are faults in the system.
What is the load signal specification range for the M 20 B 20 engine?
The load signal specification for the M 20 B 20 engine is 2.1 to 2.5 ms.
What should you do when exchanging a control unit according to the troubleshooting procedure?
When exchanging a control unit, also send in a print of the identification (test code).
What is the shutoff speed specification for both engine types?
The shutoff speed specification is 6400 ± 40 rpm for both M 20 B 20 and M 20 B 25 engines.
Under what temperature conditions should oil temperature be maintained for proper readings?
Oil temperature should be greater than 60°C (140°F) or coolant temperature greater than 80°C (175°F), with no electric equipment switched on, at idle speed.
What fault memory code should you call for additional troubleshooting help?
Call fault memory code 900. Status lists may also be called as additional help in troubleshooting.
Where can you find additional information for electrical troubleshooting?
Additional information can be found in the Electrical Troubleshooting Manual (E 34).
What is Test Position 16 testing?
Test Position 16 is for testing the CONTROL UNIT.
What should you do if the code number and manufacturing date check fails?
Replace control unit, if necessary.
What are the four main checks to perform on the control unit?
Check code number and manufacturing date, check tightness of control unit plug, check contact of plug connections, and check power supply and ground supply.
What type of test program should be used when checking the control unit?
Check control unit with L-Jetronic test program; not with DME.
What should you check regarding the control unit plug?
Check tightness of control unit plug and check contact of plug connections.
What electrical aspects of the control unit need to be verified?
Check power supply and ground supply.
What type of injection system should the test program be configured for?
L-Jetronic test program, not DME.
What two items should be checked on the control unit itself before checking electrical connections?
Check code number and manufacturing date.
What is the consequence if the control unit fails the initial checks?
Replace control unit, if necessary.
What should you check after loosening the hose straps?
Pull off plug (3) and open fasteners (4...8).
What component should be removed along with the air flow sensor?
Take off upper air cleaner section with air flow sensor.
What should be inspected on the rubber mounts during removal?
Check rubber mounts, replacing if necessary.
What is the critical installation check for the air filter cartridge?
Check installed position of air filter cartridge (arrows face in direction of flow).
What fasteners are used to secure the air flow sensor during installation?
Unscrew screws (9) and take off air flow sensor.
What should be checked between the air cleaner and air flow sensor?
Check gasket between air cleaner and air flow sensor, replacing if necessary.
What post-installation checks are required?
Check code number (1) and manufacturing date (2), check engine idle speed and CO level, and check air flow sensor.
What is shown in the wiring diagram section?
A wiring diagram with terminals numbered 4, 3, 2, 1 is shown for the air flow sensor connections.
What marking is visible on the air filter cartridge in the installation diagram?
The marking 'TOP' is visible on the air filter cartridge to indicate proper orientation.
What should I check if the throttle switch is maladjusted or defective?
Check the throttle switch with BMW service test unit / test step L-Jet. 03. Test values okay?
If the throttle switch wiring is okay but the switch is still faulty, what's the next step?
Adjust or replace throttle switch.
What causes poor central ground, loose contact or wrong plug connections?
Eliminate trouble.
Where can I find information on repairing and adjusting the throttle if it will not close?
Repair and adjust throttle (see Group 13 in Repair Manual).
What should I do if the throttle will not open fully?
Adjust throttle cable (see 35 41 421 in Repair Manual). Adjust throttle (see Group 13 in Repair Manual).
What procedure should I follow if the basic mixture setting is too high?
Adjust engine idle speed and CO (see 13 00 054 in Repair Manual).
How should I address intake system leaks?
Check all air carrying parts for leaks and repair, if necessary.
What's the solution for oil filler cap seal leaks?
Replace oil filler cap.
How do I fix oil dipstick seal leaks?
Oil dipstick must be pressed in tight in guide tube. Replace seal.
How do you remove the air flow sensor after disconnecting the hose?
Pull off plug (1), then loosen nuts (2 through 4) and take off air flow sensor.
What should be checked during installation regarding the seal?
Check seal (1), replacing if necessary.
What components should be checked on the silent mounts during installation?
Unscrew silent mounts (1 through 3) on air flow sensor and check silent mounts, replacing if necessary.
What callout numbers identify the nuts that need to be loosened to remove the air flow sensor?
Callout numbers 2, 3, and 4 identify the nuts that need to be loosened.
What installation checks are required regarding the code number and manufacturing date?
Check code number (1) and manufacturing date (2).
What engine parameters should be verified after installing the air flow sensor?
Check engine idle speed and CO level, and check air flow sensor.
How many silent mounts are there on the air flow sensor?
There are 3 silent mounts on the air flow sensor, numbered 1 through 3.
What is the specification for adjusting the push rod for throttle valve neck of 3rd and 4th cylinders?
Adjust push rod for throttle valve neck of 3rd and 4th cylinders to 97.5 ± 0.4 mm (3.838 ± 0.016").
What distance should the push rod for throttle valve neck of 1st and 2nd cylinders be adjusted to?
Adjust push rod for throttle valve neck of 1st and 2nd cylinders to approximately 100 mm (3.937").
What is the target distance from throttle valve upper edge to throttle valve neck opening?
Adjust distance from throttle valve upper edge to throttle valve neck opening to 21.7 ± 1 mm (0.854 ± 0.039") with the full load stop screw.
How should the full load stop screw be adjusted?
Open throttle valves until valves are parallel to direction of flow. Turn full load stop screw until it bears on the stop of the operating lever.
What tool setup is required for the dial gauge measurement?
Mount dial gauge with holder. Have dial gauge bear with preload on operating lever for 3rd and 4th cylinders.
What is the procedure for shortening the push rod for 1st and 2nd cylinders?
Shorten the push rod for 1st and 2nd cylinders until the dial gauge needle begins to move. Both throttle levers must bear uniformly on the idle stop.
What important warning is given about adjusting push rods?
Do not change the adjustment of push rods for this adjustment. Adjust stop screw in such a manner that any possible slight deviation is distributed uniformly to both sides.
What should be done if the 21.7 ± 1 mm distance cannot be achieved by adjusting the full stop screw?
If distance 21.7 ± 1 mm (0.854 ± 0.039") is not possible on all throttle valves by adjusting the full stop screw, replace pertinent components.
What component is being measured with calipers in diagram 13 54 057?
The diagram shows measurement of the throttle valve linkage adjustment with calipers measuring 97.5 ± 0.4mm for the 3rd and 4th cylinder push rod adjustment.
What is shown in the cross-sectional view diagram 13 54 061?
The diagram shows a cross-sectional view of the throttle valve assembly with the measurement point for the 21.7mm distance from throttle valve upper edge to throttle valve neck opening.
What adjustment is being performed in the photographs labeled 13 54 064 and 13 54 069?
The photographs show the dial gauge setup and procedure for shortening the push rod for 1st and 2nd cylinders until the dial gauge needle begins to move.
What condition must be met for both throttle levers during the push rod adjustment?
Both throttle levers must bear uniformly on the idle stop during the push rod adjustment procedure.
What does the temperature sensor for coolant measure and how does it send this information?
The temperature sensor measures the engine temperature and sends this information to the control unit as a resistance value. The resistance value drops with rising temperature (NTC).
What are the three main components of the coolant temperature sensor shown in the diagram?
The three main components are: 1 = Plug connection, 2 = Housing, and 3 = NTC resistor.
How do you remove the coolant temperature sensor?
Pull off plug (1), then unscrew temperature sensor.
What checks should be performed during installation of a replacement sensor?
Check code number (1), replace seal (2), note that FD = Manufacturing date, and fill and bleed cooling system (Group 17).
What tool is needed to check the temperature sensor and what is its part number?
A Jetronic test lead 61 1 440 is needed to check the temperature sensor.
How should you check the nominal value of the temperature sensor?
Connect Jetronic test lead 61 1 440 and check nominal value with an ohmmeter.
What procedure is recommended to check the entire temperature range of the sensor?
To check the entire temperature range, remove temperature sensor, place it in a water bath heated to testing temperature and check resistance with an ohmmeter.
What does 'FD' marking on the temperature sensor indicate?
FD indicates the Manufacturing date of the temperature sensor.
What additional system work is required after installing a new temperature sensor?
After installation, you must fill and bleed the cooling system according to Group 17 procedures.
What part number is associated with the temperature sensor removal and installation procedure?
The procedure is identified as 13 62 531 for removing and installing/checking temperature sensor for coolant.
What procedure number covers removing and installing the air flow sensor?
Procedure 13 62 000 covers removing and installing the air flow sensor.
What are the first three steps for removing the air flow sensor?
First loosen hose clamp (1), then unscrew nuts (2), and finally pull off plug (3).
What callout numbers are shown in the top diagram of the air flow sensor removal?
The top diagram shows callout numbers 1, 2, 3, and 4, indicating the hose clamp, nuts, plug, and code number respectively.
How many rubber mounts need to be unscrewed on the air flow sensor?
Three rubber mounts (1...3) need to be unscrewed on the air flow sensor.
What should be done with the rubber mounts during installation?
Check rubber mounts, replacing if necessary during installation.
What diagnostics should be checked after installing the air flow sensor?
Check code number (1) and manufacturing date (2), check engine idle speed and idle speed CO level, and check air flow sensor.
What reference is provided for specifications and nominal values?
See Specifications + Nom. Value Microfiche for detailed specifications and nominal values.
What is the final step in the air flow sensor removal procedure?
Pull air flow sensor out of air cleaner housing and remove.
What model years does this air flow sensor procedure apply to?
This procedure applies until Model '85.
What components are labeled as 1 and 2 in the bottom installation diagram?
In the bottom installation diagram, component 1 appears to be the code number location and component 2 appears to be the manufacturing date location.
What should the resistance be between throttle valve switch connections 2 and 18 with a closed throttle valve?
There should be approximately 0 ohm between connections 2 and 18 with a closed throttle valve.
What resistance should be measured between connections 3 and 18 with a wide open throttle valve?
There should be approximately 0 ohm between connections 3 and 18 with a wide open throttle valve.
How do you remove the throttle valve switch according to the removal procedure?
Pull off multiple-pin plug (3), unscrew screws (1), then take off throttle valve switch (2).
What brand name is visible on the throttle valve switch component?
BOSCH is visible on the throttle valve switch component, with 'made in Germany' text below it.
What is the first step in the throttle valve switch adjustment procedure?
There must be approx. 0 ohm between connections 2 and 18 with a closed throttle valve, then adjust by loosening screws (1) and turning the throttle valve switch.
What should happen to the resistance immediately after opening the throttle valve during adjustment?
The resistance should rise immediately to ∞ ohms after opening the throttle valve during adjustment.
What should the resistance drop back to when releasing the throttle valve after adjustment?
Resistance must drop again to approximately 0 ohm when releasing the throttle valve.
What installation check is mentioned for the throttle valve switch?
Check code number (1) and adjust throttle valve switch - see 13 63 544.
Which section should be referenced for throttle valve switch adjustment specifications?
See section 13 63 544 for throttle valve switch adjustment specifications.
What multimeter designation is referenced for testing procedures?
Quoted multimeter steps (for example, M 01) refer to the BMW SERVICE TEST.
Which terminals should you connect the voltmeter between when checking voltage supply to the idle control unit?
Connect voltmeter (M 01) between terminal 2 and car ground.
What voltage reading should the voltmeter display when testing between terminal 2 and ground with ignition on?
Voltmeter displaying at least 9 volts?
If there's no voltage between terminal 2 and ground, what should you check?
Check green/yellow wire for breaks according to wiring diagram with ohmmeter (M 06). Eliminate breaks.
What indicates that the voltage supply and ground of the idle control unit are functioning properly?
Voltage supply and ground of idle control unit okay!
What is the first step when removing throttle valve necks?
Unscrew capped nuts (1) on all four throttle valve necks.
Which hose straps need to be loosened during throttle valve neck removal?
Loosen hose straps (2 ... 4).
What should be checked during installation of throttle valve necks?
Check O-rings (6), replacing if necessary. Replace hose (7) between manifold and crankcase.
What components need to be disconnected after loosening the hose straps?
Disconnect throttle cable (5). Take off air intake manifold and cut off hose between manifold and crankcase (cannot be pulled off).
What type of nuts are used to secure the throttle valve necks?
Torx nuts (1) are used on all throttle valve necks.
What should be done with the plug on the throttle valve switch?
Pull off plug on throttle valve switch.
Which component is identified as item 8 in the diagram?
Item 8 is the plug plate on fuel injectors.
What vacuum hose needs to be removed during the procedure?
Pull off vacuum hose for the fuel pressure regulator.
What bolts need to be unscrewed when lifting off the injection pipe?
Unscrew bolts (9 and 10) and lift off injection pipe with fuel injectors.
What safety precaution is mentioned regarding needle bearings?
Do not lean on needle bearings. Keep dirt off of bearings and don't damage the shaft.
What should be checked when separating throttle valve necks?
Check O-ring of connecting pipe, replacing if necessary.
What section is this diagnostic procedure from?
This is from Section 13 - 804, which covers checking periphery for warm-up speed, specifically the coolant temperature switch.
What are the first steps to test the coolant temperature switch?
Connect voltmeter (M 01) between terminal 2 and terminal 6, then turn on ignition. The voltmeter should display approximately 0 volt with a coolant temperature of ≤ 30° C (86° F).
What should the voltmeter reading be when coolant temperature is above 48° C (118° F)?
The voltmeter should display at least 9 volts with a coolant temperature of > 48° C (118° F).
What diagnostic tool is specified for checking the white wire connection?
Use ohmmeter (M 06) on the "white wire" plug connection of temperature sensor and car ground.
What resistance reading indicates a problem with the temperature sensor at low coolant temperature?
If the ohmmeter displays at least 100 k-ohms with a coolant temperature of ≤ 30° C (86° F), there is no connection problem.
What should you check if the white wire connection test fails?
Check the white wire of temperature sensor for breaks, eliminate breaks, check contact pins of temperature sensor for tight fit and good contact, and verify wire and contact pins are okay.
What is the expected ohmmeter reading at higher coolant temperatures?
The ohmmeter should display approximately "0" ohm with a coolant temperature of > 48° C (118° F).
What is the corrective action if the temperature sensor fails testing?
Replace temperature sensor and check code number.
What are the two main temperature thresholds used in this diagnostic procedure?
The procedure uses ≤ 30° C (86° F) for cold coolant temperature and > 48° C (118° F) for warm coolant temperature testing.
What are the two temperature switches being covered in procedures 12 63 051 and 12 63 060?
The 0°C (32°F) temperature switch and the 45°C (113°F) temperature switch.
What should you do after installing the 45°C temperature switch?
Fill and bleed the cooling system according to Group 17.
What tool is specified for checking the temperature switch resistance?
An ohmmeter (M 06) is used to check the temperature switch resistance.
What resistance reading should the ohmmeter display when testing the temperature switch at temperatures below -8°C?
The ohmmeter must display approximately 0 ohm for temperatures less than -8°C (+ 18°F).
What resistance reading indicates proper operation for temperatures above 4°C on the first temperature switch?
The ohmmeter must display approximately ∞ ohms for temperatures greater than 4°C (39°F).
In the wiring diagrams, what do callout numbers 1 and 2 represent?
Callout number 1 indicates the electrical connector and callout number 2 indicates the temperature switch body.
What should be checked during installation of both temperature switches?
Check the code number (1) and switching temperature (2) during installation.
What resistance should be displayed when the 45°C temperature switch is tested above 48°C?
The ohmmeter should display approximately ∞ ohms for temperatures above 48°C (118°F).
What is the first step in removing either temperature switch?
Pull off the electrical plug (1) from the temperature switch.
Where can additional specifications for these temperature switches be found?
Additional specifications can be found in the Specifications section, as indicated by the asterisk notation.
What voltage should the voltmeter display when checking the speed signal for the idle control unit?
The voltmeter should display at least 9 volts when checking the speed signal for the idle control unit.
Which terminals should be connected when testing the speed signal for the idle control unit?
Connect voltmeter (M 01) between terminals 3 and 4 when testing the speed signal for the idle control unit.
What ohmmeter reading should you get between terminal 3 and socket 13 of the diagnosis socket?
The ohmmeter should display approximately 0 ohm between terminal 3 and socket 13 of the diagnosis socket.
What should you do if there are breaks in the green wire during speed signal testing?
You should eliminate the breaks in the green wire if they are found during speed signal testing.
Which terminals are used for the idle signal test on the idle control unit?
Connect voltmeter (M 01) between terminals 4 and 12 for the idle signal test on the idle control unit.
What voltage should the voltmeter show briefly when testing the idle signal?
The voltmeter should display at least 9 volts briefly when testing the idle signal with ignition turned on and then off.
What should you do if the idle signal test fails at the throttle switch step?
If the test fails, you should adjust or replace the throttle switch and adjust the cable.
What voltage reading indicates a proper idle signal when pressing the accelerator pedal?
The voltmeter should display approximately 0 volt when pressing down the accelerator pedal several centimeters during the idle signal test.
What is the first step in checking the idle signal for the idle control unit?
The first step is to connect voltmeter (M 01) between terminals 4 and 12, then turn on ignition.
What should you check if the idle signal voltage test fails initially?
If the initial test fails, you should pull off the multiple-pin plug on the throttle switch and connect voltmeter (M 01) on center pin contact of plug receptacle and ground.
When should you provide power supply to the wiring diagram during idle signal testing?
You should provide power supply to the wiring diagram if the voltage test at the throttle switch plug receptacle fails to show at least 9 volts briefly.
What does a successful speed signal test indicate about the idle control unit?
If the speed signal test passes (voltmeter shows at least 9 volts), it indicates that the speed signal for the idle control unit is okay.
What are the steps to remove the cold start valve?
Pull off plug (1), disconnect fuel line (2), unscrew screws, and take off cold start valve.
How do you check the cold start valve after installation?
Unscrew cold start valve on intake manifold while keeping the fuel line connected.
What specific procedure applies to L-Jetronic E30 engines when checking the cold start valve?
Unscrew cold start valve on intake manifold, fuel line remains connected, pull off fuel pump relay (1), bridge terminals 87b and 30 with Special Tool 61 3 050, and fuel pump runs.
What tool is required for bridging terminals 87b and 30 on L-Jetronic E30 engines?
Special Tool 61 3 050.
What terminals should be bridged on the fuel pump relay for L-Jetronic E30 checking?
Terminals 87b and 30 should be bridged with Special Tool 61 3 050.
What leak test procedure is specified for the cold start valve?
Check permissible leak rate.
How should the cold start valve be positioned when checking fuel flow rate and spray angle?
Hold cold start valve in measuring glass 13 3 020.
How should the Jetronic test lead be connected for flow rate testing?
Plug Jetronic test lead 61 1 440 on cold start valve and connect with B+ and B-.
Where can specifications for fuel flow rate and spray angle be found?
See Specifications.
What component is indicated by callout number 2 in the cold start valve removal diagram?
The fuel line that needs to be disconnected during removal.
What is the procedure for checking periphery for air conditioner speed?
Connect voltmeter (M 01) between terminal 4 and terminal 9, turn on ignition, turn on air conditioner, and check if voltmeter displays at least 9 volts.
What should you do if the voltmeter reads less than 9 volts during the air conditioner speed check?
Check the blue/white wire for breaks with ohmmeter (M 06) and eliminate any breaks found.
What is the minimum voltage reading required during the air conditioner periphery speed check?
At least 9 volts.
What wire color should be checked if the voltage reading is insufficient?
Blue/white wire.
What is the important note regarding drive range gears with automatic transmission?
After selecting a drive range gears with automatic transmission, always only the nominal idle speed (700 ± 50 rpm) is regulated (preferred circuit).
What is the nominal idle speed specification mentioned in the important note?
What type of circuit is referenced in the automatic transmission idle speed regulation?
Preferred circuit.
What should be done after identifying breaks in the blue/white wire?
Eliminate breaks.
What is the nominal idle speed for cars with automatic transmission after selecting a drive range?
The nominal idle speed is 700 ± 50 rpm and is always regulated after selecting a drive range on cars with automatic transmission.
Which terminals should the voltmeter be connected between when testing the preferred circuit?
The voltmeter (M 01) should be connected between terminal 4 and terminal 7.
What position should the automatic transmission selector lever be in during the preferred circuit test?
The selector lever of the automatic transmission should be moved to 'N' (neutral).
What is the minimum voltage reading required during the preferred circuit test?
The voltmeter should be displaying at least 9 volts.
If the voltmeter reads less than 9 volts on a car with automatic transmission, what should be checked?
Check the blue/brown wire for breaks with an ohmmeter (M 06), eliminate breaks, and check or replace the selector lever switch.
What diagnostic procedure applies to cars with manual transmission in the preferred circuit test?
Connect voltmeter (M 01) between terminal 4 and terminal 7, turn on ignition, and verify the voltmeter displays at least 9 volts.
If a car with manual transmission shows no voltage during the test, what wire should be checked?
Eliminate breaks in the blue/yellow wire from terminal 7 to terminal 2.
What tool is specified for checking wire breaks in the blue/brown wire?
An ohmmeter (M 06) is specified for checking breaks in the blue/brown wire.
What is the main difference between the automatic and manual transmission testing procedures?

For automatic transmission, the selector lever must be moved to 'N' and if voltage is insufficient, check the blue/brown wire and selector lever switch. For manual transmission, check the blue/yellow wire from terminal 7 to terminal 2 if voltage is insufficient.
What component should be checked or replaced if breaks are found in the blue/brown wire on automatic transmission cars?
The selector lever switch should be checked or replaced.
What is the significance of the 'Important!' note regarding idle speed regulation?
It emphasizes that after selecting a drive range on cars with automatic transmission, the nominal idle speed of 700 ± 50 rpm is always regulated, which is a critical operational characteristic.
What is the first step when removing the fuel pressure regulator?
Disconnect fuel hose (1).
What should you do after unscrewing the bolts to remove the fuel pressure regulator?
Pull fuel pressure regulator out of injection pipe and pull off vacuum hose (2).
What should be checked during installation of the fuel pressure regulator?
Check seal (1), replacing if necessary.
What special tools are needed for checking between the feed pipe and hose?
Install Special Tools 13 3 060 and 13 3 064 between feed pipe and hose.
What procedure should be followed with the fuel pump relay?
Pull off fuel pump relay (1), bridge terminals 87 and 30 with Special Tool 61 3 050, press the button, fuel pump runs, then check fuel injection pressure.
What does callout number 2 indicate in the fuel pressure regulator removal diagram?
The vacuum hose that needs to be pulled off during removal.
What should be done to the engine compartment wall trim during this procedure?
Remove trim on engine compartment wall.
What code numbers are visible on the fuel pressure regulator installation diagram?
Check code number (1) and manufacturing date (2).
Where can you find fuel injection pressure specifications?
See Specifications and Nominal Value Microfiche.
What is the first test to perform when checking the coolant temperature switch for warm-up speed periphery?
Connect voltmeter (M 01) between terminal 2 and terminal 6, turn on ignition, and check if the voltmeter displays approximately 0 volt with coolant temperature of less than 30°C (86°F).
What should the voltmeter reading be when testing the coolant temperature switch with coolant temperature below 30°C?
The voltmeter should display approximately 0 volt with coolant temperature of less than 30°C (86°F).
If the initial voltage test passes, what is the next step in checking the coolant temperature switch?
Connect voltmeter (M 01) between terminal 2 and terminal 6, turn on ignition, and verify the voltmeter displays at least 9 volts with coolant temperature of greater than 48°C (118°F).
What ohmmeter test should be performed on the white wire plug connection?

Connect ohmmeter (M 06) on the white wire plug connection of the 45°C (113°F) temperature switch and car ground. The ohmmeter should display at least 100 k-ohms with coolant temperature of less than 30°C (86°F).
What resistance reading indicates a good 45°C temperature switch when the coolant is below 30°C?
The ohmmeter should display at least 100 k-ohms with coolant temperature of less than 30°C (86°F).
What is the final ohmmeter test in this diagnostic sequence?

Connect ohmmeter (M 06) on the white wire plug connection of 45°C (113°F) temperature switch and car ground. The ohmmeter should display approximately 0 ohm with coolant temperature of greater than 48°C (118°F).
What should you do if the 45°C temperature switch fails any of the tests?
Replace 45°C (113°F) temperature switch and check code number.
What tools are referenced for testing the coolant temperature switch?
Voltmeter (M 01) and ohmmeter (M 06) are referenced for testing the coolant temperature switch.
What temperature thresholds are critical for this coolant temperature switch diagnosis?
The critical temperature thresholds are less than 30°C (86°F) for the cold test conditions, 45°C (113°F) for the temperature switch rating, and greater than 48°C (118°F) for the warm test conditions.
What page number contains information about engine idle speed and CO level adjustment?
Engine idle speed and CO level adjustment information is found on page 13-700a.
What is the page reference for fuel injector removal and installation?
Fuel injector removal and installation information is on page 13-781.
On which page would I find information about throttle valve necks removal and installation?
Throttle valve necks removal and installation is covered on page 13-730.
What section number covers the fuel system procedures?
Section 13 covers the fuel system procedures.
Where can I find the air flow sensor removal and installation procedure?
The air flow sensor removal and installation procedure is found on page 13-760.
What should I check first if the fuel pump is not running?
Check if the pump fuse is okay. If the fuse is not okay, replace the pump fuse.
How do I check the power supply to the fuel pump?
Pull off plug on fuel pump, connect voltmeter (M 1) between wires in plug, start engine. Voltmeter should show battery voltage.
What should I do if the fuel pump has good power supply but still isn't working?
Replace fuel pump.
How do I test the brown wire ground connection?
Connect ohmmeter (M 06) between brown wire on disconnected plug and ground. Ohmmeter should show approx. 0 ohm.
What should the resistance value be when checking the brown wire ground?
Ohmmeter should show approx. 0 ohm.
How do I check the green/violet wire voltage?
Pull off plug on control relay, connect ohmmeter (M 06) between conn. 87a on disconnected control relay plug and green/violet wire on disconnected pump plug. Ohmmeter should show approx. 0 ohm.
What should I do if the brown wire ground check shows the resistance value is not okay?
Repair wire.
What should I do if the green/violet wire voltage check shows the resistance value is not okay?
Repair wire.
What connector should I use to check the green/violet wire voltage?
Connect between conn. 87a on disconnected control relay plug and green/violet wire on disconnected pump plug.
What type of meter is specified for checking the ground wire resistance?
Ohmmeter (M 06).
What should you do with terminals 87 and 30 when working on the fuel pump relay?
Bridge terminals 87 and 30 with Special Tool 61 3 050 to make the fuel pump run.
What components are shown in the diagram with reference 28 13 053?
The diagram shows the cold start valve assembly with callouts for (1) the electrical connection and (2) the fuel line connection.
What should be checked during installation of the cold start valve?
Check the code number (1) and replace the seal (2).
What verification step should be performed after cold start valve installation?
Unscrew the cold start valve on intake manifold and confirm that the fuel line remains connected.
What type of test is performed to check the cold start valve operation?
A leak test is performed to check the permissible leak rate.
What equipment is needed to check fuel flow rate and spray angle?
Hold the cold start valve in measuring glass 13 3 020 and plug Jetronic test lead 61 1 440 on cold start valve and connect with B+ and B-.
What parameters should be checked during the fuel flow rate and spray angle test?
Check the fuel flow rate and spray angle according to specifications.
Where can you find the specific values for leak rate and fuel flow specifications?
See Specifications section for the specific values and acceptance criteria.
What components are labeled as KL 87 and KL 30 in the fuel pump relay diagram?
KL 87 and KL 30 are terminal designations on the fuel pump relay that need to be bridged with special tool 61 3 050.
What is the function of part number 61 3 050 mentioned in the procedure?
It is a special tool used to bridge terminals 87 and 30 on the fuel pump relay to make the fuel pump run during testing.
What are the main categories of fuel injection troubleshooting symptoms listed?

The main categories are: 1) Cold engine does not start (oil temp ≤ 20°C/68°F), 2) Engine starts but stops again, 3) Cold engine hard to start (oil temp ≤ 20°C/68°F), 4) Warm engine does not start (oil temp ≤ 60°C/140°F), 5) Warm engine hard to start (oil temp ≤ 60°C/140°F), 6) Erratic idling during warm-up phase, 7) Idle speed not correct.
What conditions must be met for proper fuel injection testing according to the requirements?

Testing requirements include: Engine in perfect running condition (timing, compression, oil/carbon deposits, etc.), starting system in perfect condition (battery voltage, starter, ignition lock, etc.), correct fuel in tank (octane rating, leaded/unleaded, dirt, etc.), and connections and plugs correct according to wiring diagram.
What is the job number for the fuel injector test position?
The job number for the fuel injector test position is 13 64 501.
Which symptoms would lead you to check the cold start valve?
You would check the cold start valve (job no. 13 64 030) for symptoms including cold engine does not start, engine starts but stops again, cold engine hard to start, and warm engine does not start.
What component should be tested if the engine has poor acceleration and final power output issues?

For poor acceleration and final power output issues, you should test the fuel pressure (injection pressure) with job number 13 51 200, fuel pressure regulator with job number 13 51 200, fuel injector with job number 13 64 501, and control unit (DME or L-Jetronic) with job number 13 61 000.
Which test positions are checked for misfiring at constant engine speed?

For misfiring at constant engine speed, you should check fuel injector (position 6, job no. 13 64 501), throttle switch (position 12, job no. 13 63 544), throttle housing (position 14, job no. 13 54 051), throttle positioner (position 15, job no. 13 54 130), and control unit DME or L-Jetronic (position 16, job no. 13 61 000).
What is the job number for testing the oxygen sensor?
The oxygen sensor testing is referenced as Group 11, but no specific job number is provided on this page.
If the engine has incorrect CO/HC values, which components should be tested?

For incorrect CO/HC values, you should test the fuel injector (job no. 13 64 501), control unit DME or L-Jetronic (job no. 13 61 000), air flow sensor (job no. 13 62 000), electric idle control valve (job no. 13 41 000), control unit for idle speed regulation (job no. 13 41 010), and oxygen sensor (Group 11).
What symptoms would indicate a problem with the temperature time switch?

The temperature time switch (job no. 13 62 050) should be checked for symptoms including cold engine does not start, engine starts but stops again, cold engine hard to start, warm engine does not start, and warm engine hard to start.
Where can additional application information be found for this troubleshooting section?
Additional application information can be found on the next page, as indicated by the note 'See application information on next page' in the troubleshooting fuel injection section.
What are the steps to remove the pressure sensor?
Pull off plug (1), unscrew screw (2), and remove pressure sensor.
What does FD stand for on the pressure sensor?
FD = Manufacturing date.
What callout numbers are shown in the top pressure sensor diagram?
The diagram shows callout numbers 1 and 2, where 1 indicates the plug connection and 2 indicates the screw.
What should be checked during installation of the pressure sensor?
Check code number (1).
What resistance should be measured at atmospheric pressure of ≤ 860 mbar?
There will be resistance of approximately 0 ohms between plug connections (1 and 2).
Which plug connections are used for resistance testing of the pressure sensor?
Plug connections 1 and 2.
What are the two atmospheric pressure ranges specified for checking the pressure sensor?
≤ 860 mbar and ≥ 930 mbar.
What diagram numbers are associated with the pressure sensor images?
How does the resistance reading change based on atmospheric pressure conditions?
At low pressure (≤ 860 mbar) the resistance is approximately 0 ohms, while at high pressure (≥ 930 mbar) the resistance is approximately infinite ohms between the same plug connections.
What should you check during installation of the control unit?
Check code number (1) and manufacturing date (2).
What is the first step in removing the control unit?
Open glove box and pull off pins (1) of both retaining straps.
What should you do after opening the glove box?
Unscrew trim panel.
How do you remove the control unit after accessing it?
Push back retainer (1) and pull off plug (2). Unscrew four mounting bolts and take off control unit.
Where should you look for information about plug connections?
See wiring diagram for plug connections.
What callout number indicates the retainer that needs to be pushed back?
Callout number (1) indicates the retainer that needs to be pushed back.
What callout number shows the plug that needs to be pulled off?
Callout number (2) shows the plug that needs to be pulled off.
What reference number is associated with the trim panel removal step?
Reference number 28 15 207 is associated with the trim panel removal step.
What is the first step when removing a fuel injector?
Unscrew screws on injection pipe.
What two components need to be pulled off during fuel injector removal?
Pull off plug on throttle valve switch (1) and pull off plug plate (2) on fuel injectors.
How do you lift the fuel injectors out of their guides?
Push up injection pipe (3) until fuel injectors are lifted out of guides on throttle valve necks.
What component is labeled as item 4 in the fuel injector removal procedure?
The retainer that needs to be lifted out to take off the fuel injector.
What does the code number check involve during installation?
Check code number (2) - FD = Manufacturing date.
What lubricant should be used to coat the O-rings during installation?
Only coat O-rings with vaseline or SAE 90 gear lube for installation.
What color marking should be checked during installation?
Check color of plug receptacle (5) or fuel injector guard (4).
What reference number identifies this procedure in the manual?
13 64 501 - Removing and Installing One Fuel Injector.
Which multimeter setting should I use to test the air temperature switch terminals?
Use voltmeter setting M01 to test between terminal 4 and terminal 10.
What voltage reading indicates a faulty air temperature switch at cold temperatures?
If the voltmeter displays at least 9 volts with an air temperature of < -8°C (< 18°F), the switch is faulty.
Do all E30 models have an air temperature switch?
No, cars with manual transmission do not have an air temperature switch.
How are the wire plugs connected on the air temperature switch?
Wire plugs for air temperature switch are connected with each other.
What ohmmeter reading indicates a good air temperature sensor at cold temperatures?
The ohmmeter should display approximately 0 ohm with an air temperature of < -8°C (< 18°F).
What should I do if the ohmmeter shows 0 ohms on both plug connections of the air temperature sensor?
Replace the air temperature sensor.
What voltage reading indicates the air temperature sensor is okay at warm temperatures?
The voltmeter should display approximately 0 volt with an air temperature of > +4°C (39°F).
What resistance reading should I expect from a good air temperature sensor at warm temperatures?
The ohmmeter should display at least 100 k-ohms with an air temperature of > +4°C (39°F).
How do I test the air temperature sensor resistance?
Connect ohmmeter (M06) on both plug connections of air temperature sensor after pulling off both wire plugs.
When can I conclude that the air temperature sensor is okay?
Air temperature sensor is okay when it shows approximately 0 volt at warm temperatures (> +4°C/39°F) during the voltage test.
What voltage should the voltmeter display when testing the air temperature switch at temperatures below -8°C (18°F)?
The voltmeter should display at least 9 volts when the air temperature is below -8°C (18°F).
What should you do if the voltmeter shows less than 9 volts during the initial air temperature switch test?
Connect ohmmeter M 06 between terminal 2 and terminal 10, then pull off both wire plugs on the air temperature switch and connect.
What ohm reading indicates a faulty air temperature switch when testing with M 06 at approximately 0 ohms?
If the ohmmeter displays approximately 0 ohms with an air temperature below -8°C (18°F), replace the air temperature switch.
What voltage should be displayed when testing the air temperature switch at temperatures above +4°C (39°F)?
The voltmeter should display approximately 0 volt when the air temperature is above +4°C (39°F).
What resistance reading should the ohmmeter show for a properly functioning air temperature switch at temperatures above +4°C?
The ohmmeter should display at least 100 k-ohms with an air temperature above +4°C (39°F).
What is the final determination if the voltmeter reads approximately 0 volt at temperatures above +4°C?
The air temperature switch is okay.
Which terminals should be tested first when diagnosing the air temperature switch?
Terminal 4 and terminal 10 should be tested first using voltmeter M 01.
What action should be taken if wire breaks are suspected during testing?
Eliminate wire breaks by pulling off both wire plugs on the air temperature switch and connecting them.
What multimeter should be used for resistance measurements on the air temperature switch?
Use ohmmeter M 06 for resistance measurements on the air temperature switch.
At what temperature threshold does the air temperature switch behavior change according to the test procedure?
The air temperature switch behavior changes at the threshold between -8°C (18°F) and +4°C (39°F).
What should you do with the wire plugs before performing ohmmeter testing?
Pull off both wire plugs on the air temperature switch before connecting the ohmmeter for testing.
What resistance should be measured between connections 3 and 18 with the throttle wide open?
There must be approximately 0 ohm between connections 3 and 18 with the throttle wide open.
How do you remove the throttle switch from the housing?
Remove throttle housing 13 54 030, unscrew screw (1), and take off throttle switch (2).
How is the throttle switch adjusted after loosening screw (1)?
Adjust by loosening screw (1) and turning the throttle switch. Open the throttle after making adjustment - the resistance value should rise immediately to ∞-ohms.
What should happen to the resistance value when the throttle valve is released during adjustment?
When releasing the throttle valve, the resistance must drop to approximately 0 ohm.
What part number is associated with adjusting the throttle switch?
The part number for adjusting the throttle switch is 13 63 544.
What component is shown in callout number 2 in the throttle switch removal diagram?
Callout number 2 indicates the throttle switch that needs to be removed.
What is the first step when checking the throttle switch?
Check that there should be approximately 0 ohm between connections 2 and 18 with the throttle closed.
What reference number is used for the throttle housing that needs to be removed?
The throttle housing reference number is 13 54 030.
What should be checked after installing the throttle switch?
Check code number (1) and adjust throttle switch 13 63 544 after installation.
What is Test Position 10 for in the BMW E30 M3 fuel system diagnostics?
Test Position 10 is for the coolant temperature sensor diagnostics.
What should I check first when diagnosing coolant temperature sensor issues?
Check code number, then check for tight fit and good contact of plug connections and correct level of coolant (see Gr. 17 for air bubbles).
What should I do if the coolant temperature sensor code number check fails?
Replace coolant temperature sensor and repair plug contact.
How do I test the coolant temperature sensor resistance values?
Check resistance values, and if necessary, heat to testing temperature in a water bath.
What should I do if the coolant temperature sensor resistance values are incorrect?
Replace coolant temperature sensor.
Where can I find coolant system air bubble information referenced in this test?
See Gr. 17 (air bubbles).
Where can I find the specifications for coolant temperature sensor testing?
See Specifications section, as indicated by the asterisk footnote.
Where can I find the wiring diagram for the coolant temperature sensor circuit?
See Wiring Diagram section, as indicated by the double asterisk footnote.
What are the main diagnostic steps for coolant temperature sensor troubleshooting?
1) Check code number and plug connections/coolant level, 2) Check resistance values (heat in water bath if necessary), 3) Check wires.
What color wire is plug 1 in the control unit plug connections?
Plug 1 is Black.
What does plug connection A represent when 1 + 0?
A) 1 + 0 = unleaded prem. grade US.
What does plug connection C represent when 1 + 1?
C) 1 + 1 = leaded prem. grade ECE.
What does E represent in the plug connections list?
E) State of plug connections.
In the state of plug connections, what does 0 mean?
0 = disconnected.
What symptom indicates a fuel pump control relay issue?
Fuel pump running only during starting procedures.
How do you check the power supply of the control relay?
Pull off plug on control relay and connect voltmeter (M 01) between conn. 30 on disconnected control relay plug and ground. Voltmeter must display battery voltage.
What should you do if the voltage value is not okay when checking connection 30?
Provide power supply (see wiring diagram).
Which connection should you test after conn. 30 when checking the control relay?
Connect voltmeter (M 01) between conn. 15 on disconnected control relay socket and ground, then turn on ignition.
What voltage reading should you get when testing conn. 50 with the engine started?
Voltmeter should display battery voltage when the engine is started.
How do you check the ground connection of the control relay?
Connect ohmmeter (M 06) between conn. 31 on disconnected control relay plug and ground. Ohmmeter should display approx. 0 ohm.
What should you do if the resistance value is not okay when checking the ground connection?
Repair wire. Electric ground (see wiring diagram).
How do you check the speed signal for the control relay?
Connect voltmeter (M 02) between conn. 1 on disconnected control relay plug and ground. Voltmeter should display voltage.
What should you check if no voltage is displayed during the speed signal test?
Check ignition system. Ignition system okay?
What is the final step if all voltage and resistance tests pass?
Replace control relay.
What should you do with the injection tube after unscrewing the bolts?
Push up injection tube until fuel injectors have cleared guide in the intake manifold.
What two items need to be removed after pulling off the plug?
Lift out retainer (2) and remove fuel injector.
What does callout number 1 indicate in the fuel injector diagram?
The plug connection that needs to be pulled off.
What does callout number 2 represent in the installation diagram?
The retainer that must be lifted out during fuel injector removal.
What should you check on the O-rings during installation?
Check O-rings (1), replacing if necessary.
What does the code number (2) on the fuel injector indicate?
The code number should be checked, and FD indicates the manufacturing date.
What should you inspect regarding the plastic washer during installation?
Check location of plastic washer (3).
What two color-coded items should be checked during fuel injector installation?
Check color of plug receptacle (5) or fuel injector guard (4).
Where can additional specifications for fuel injector replacement be found?
See Specifications section 13 64 025.
What does 'FD' represent on the fuel injector diagram?
FD represents the manufacturing date marking on the fuel injector.
Which terminals should be connected with a voltmeter for testing cars with automatic transmission?
Terminal 4 and terminal 7
What is the minimum voltage reading that should be displayed when testing the automatic transmission selector lever circuit?
At least 9 volts
Which selector positions should be tested for cars with automatic transmission?
"N" or "P" positions
For manual transmission cars, what is the minimum voltage reading required between terminals 4 and 7?
At least 9 volts
What wire colors should be checked for breaks in manual transmission vehicles?
Green/yellow wire from terminal 7 to terminal 2
What tool is specified for measuring voltage in the preferred circuit test?
Voltmeter (M 01)
What should be done if breaks are found in the blue/yellow wire for automatic transmission cars?
Eliminate breaks and check or replace selector lever switch
What is the BMW part number for the throttle valve housing shown in the diagram?
The throttle valve housing part number is 13 54 055.
How much should the idle stop screw be turned when loosening nut (2)?
Turn the idle stop screw (1) about 1/10th of a turn in the direction of the arrow, then tighten nut (2) again.
What components are indicated by callout numbers 3, 4, and 5 in the throttle valve housing diagram?
Number 3 indicates the gasket, number 4 indicates the retainer, and number 5 indicates O-rings.
What is the proper axial clearance specification for the throttle valve?
The axial clearance should be 0.2 mm (0.008") with a feeler gage blade (1) fitting easily on both left and right sides between the throttle valve and housing.
What special tools are mentioned for the throttle valve adjustment procedure?
Dial gage 00 2 510 (with extension 3) and Special Tool 00 2 500 are mentioned for mounting on the throttle valve neck.
What temperature conditions are specified for throttle valve adjustment?
Component temperature should be approximately 20° C (68° F) during adjustment.
How much should the throttle screws be loosened during installation?
Screw in throttle screws carefully until they fit tight and then loosen 1 and 1/2 turns again.
What is the specified adjustment range for the throttle valve lower edge?
Adjust the throttle valve lower edge to 0.1 + 0.05 mm (0.004" + 0.002") with idle stop screw (1) approximately 1/10th of a turn.
When are throttle valve neck basic adjustments necessary according to the note?
Throttle valve neck basic adjustments are only necessary after replacing parts, in case of a loose clamping screw or erroneous adjustment.
What should be done to secure the idle stop screw after adjustment?
Lock idle stop screw (1) and secure with paint after adjustment is complete.
How should the spring be preloaded during installation?
Preload spring (8) by about 1/2 turn during installation, and preload spring (5) with about 1/2 a turn.
What check should be performed to verify proper throttle valve operation?
Check whether throttle valve moves easily at operating temperature with closed throttle valve and at room temperature of about 20° C (68° F).
What is the procedure number for replacing fuel injectors?
The procedure number is 13 64 501 for replacing fuel injectors.
How many mounting bolts need to be unscrewed from the injection pipe?
Four mounting bolts (1) need to be unscrewed from the injection pipe.
What should be done with the injection pipe after unscrewing the mounting bolts?
Push up injection pipe until fuel injectors are lifted out of the guide on the intake manifold.
Which components need to be disconnected according to the upper right image?
Disconnect plug (2), coolant temperature sensor plug (3), and DME temperature sensor plug (4).
What should be checked on the O-rings during installation?
Check O-rings (1), replacing when necessary. Check code number (2), check position of plastic washer (3), and check color of plug receptacle (5) or injector guard (4).
How many mounting bolts need to be unscrewed in the lower procedure?
Unscrew mounting bolts (5...8), which indicates four bolts numbered 5 through 8.
What should be done after pushing up the injection pipe in the lower procedure?
Push up injection pipe until fuel injectors are lifted out of the guide on the intake manifold, then remove fuel injectors separately.
What is shown in callout number 1 in the fuel injector removal image?
Callout number 1 indicates the plug that needs to be pulled off the fuel injector.
What does the holder (1) refer to in the new plug plate procedure?
The holder (1) needs to be unscrewed when replacing fuel injectors with new plug plate.
What reference is provided for additional specifications?
The page references 'See Specifications' for additional technical details.
What is the first step in removing the throttle switch?
Pull off multiple pin plug (3).
How many screws need to be unscrewed during throttle switch removal?
Unscrew screws (1).
What does callout number 3 identify in the throttle switch diagram?
Callout number 3 identifies the multiple pin plug that needs to be pulled off.
What adjustment procedure is required after throttle switch installation?
Adjust throttle switch 13 63 544.
What manufacturer made the throttle switch shown in the diagram?
BOSCH made in Germany.
What is the part number visible on the Bosch throttle switch?
What reference number is shown for the throttle switch installation procedure?
13 63 551 for removing and installing throttle switch.
What section should be referenced for specifications during installation?
See Specifications as indicated by the asterisk note at the bottom of the page.
What resistance reading indicates the throttle switch is in the wide open position?
With the throttle wide open there should be approximately 0 ohm between connections 3 and 18.
What do the abbreviations LL and VL stand for in the throttle switch testing?
LL stands for Idle and VL stands for Full load.
How do you adjust the throttle switch according to the procedure shown?
Adjust by loosening screws (1) and turning the throttle switch. There should be approximately 0 ohm between connections 2 and 18 with the throttle closed.
What resistance value should you see when releasing the throttle back to idle after adjustment?
When releasing the throttle the resistance should drop back to approximately 0 ohm.
What component is identified by part number 13 63 544?
Part number 13 63 544 identifies the throttle switch that is being adjusted.
What component callout number 1 indicates in the adjustment photograph?
Callout number 1 indicates the screws that need to be loosened to adjust the throttle switch.
What is the part number shown at the bottom of the throttle switch component diagram?
The part number shown at the bottom of the throttle switch component diagram is 30 13 631.
What connections are used to check the full load position of the throttle switch?
Connections 3 and 18 are used to check the full load (VL) position of the throttle switch.
What is the expected resistance reading that indicates infinite ohms during throttle switch testing?
Infinity ohms (∞ ohms) is the expected resistance reading when the throttle is opened after adjustment, indicating the switch has properly transitioned.
What photo reference number is shown for the throttle switch adjustment procedure?
Photo reference number 30 13 440 is shown for the throttle switch adjustment procedure.
What does the temperature time switch regulate?
The temperature time switch regulates the open time of the cold start valve in accordance with the coolant temperature.
What are the open time and switching-off temperature values stamped on the hexagon?
The open time (e.g. 8 sec.) and switching-off temperature (e.g. + 35° C = 95° F) are stamped on the hexagon.
How do you remove the temperature time switch?
Pull off plug (1), then unscrew temperature time switch.
What should you check when installing the temperature time switch?
Check code number (1). Replace seal (2). FD = Manufacturing date. Fill and bleed cooling system (Group 17). Tighten to torque.
What tool is needed for checking the temperature time switch?
Connect Jetronic test lead 61 1 440.
How do you check the temperature time switch resistance?
Check nominal value with an ohmmeter. To check the entire temperature range, remove temperature sensor, place in water bath heated to testing temperature and check resistance with an ohmmeter.
What does 'FD' represent on the temperature time switch?
FD = Manufacturing date.
What system needs to be filled and bled after installing the temperature time switch?
Fill and bleed cooling system (Group 17).
What should you do if the voltmeter shows less than 9 volts when checking between terminals 4 and 9?
Check the blue/white wire for breaks with ohmmeter (M 06) and eliminate any breaks found.
Which terminals should be connected with a voltmeter for the second air conditioner speed check?
Connect voltmeter (M 01) between terminal 4 and terminal 11.
What wire should be checked if the second air conditioner speed test fails?
Check the blue/black wire for breaks with ohmmeter (M 06) and eliminate breaks.
What is the minimum voltage reading required for proper air conditioner operation?
At least 9 volts must be displayed on the voltmeter.
What tool is specified for measuring voltage in the air conditioner speed check?
Voltmeter (M 01) is specified for measuring voltage.
What tool is used to check for wire breaks?
Ohmmeter (M 06) is used to check for breaks in the wires.
When should the solenoid cut in during the air conditioner speed test?
The voltmeter should display at least 9 volts after the solenoid has cut in during the second test.
What is the important note regarding drive range selection for cars with automatic transmission?
After selecting a drive range (cars with automatic transmission) always only the nominal speed (750 ± 50 rpm) is regulated (preferred circuit).
What are the two wire colors mentioned in the air conditioner speed checking procedure?
Blue/white wire and blue/black wire are the two wire colors mentioned.
What should be done if breaks are found in the wires during the air conditioner speed check?
Eliminate the breaks found in the wires.
What is the regulated nominal speed mentioned in the important note?
The nominal speed is 750 ± 50 rpm.
What is the normal operating voltage range for the power supply to the control unit?
10 to 15 V for normal operation, and 6 to 15 V during starting.
What voltage jumps are associated with the oxygen sensor signal?
0.7 volt voltage jumps.
What percentage of leaning occurs throughout the working range when applied ground is present?
Approximately 1% leaning throughout the entire working range of the control unit.
What is the function of pin 22 on the L-Jetronic control unit?
Integrator voltage outlet for diagnosis socket, Plug socket 5.
What signal does pin 6 carry and where does it go?
Load signal ti to knock protection relay.
What is the function of pin 328 according to the control unit code table?
It is connected via running-up safety relay/signal for fuel consumption display (economy control).
What should the resistance be between terminals 2 and 1 or 2 and 3 on the idle speed control valve?
The nominal resistance between terminals 2 and 1 or between 2 and 3 should be approximately 20 ohms each.
What are the first steps for removing the idle speed control valve?
First unscrew the capped nuts on all four throttle valve necks, then unscrew the mounting nut and loosen hose straps 2 through 4.
How should the air intake manifold be removed during idle speed control valve service?
Disconnect the throttle cable first, then take off the air intake manifold while cutting off the hose between the manifold and crankcase, as it cannot be pulled off.
What components are identified by callout numbers 1 through 7 in the removal diagram?
The diagram shows numbered components 1 through 7 indicating various parts of the throttle body and idle speed control valve assembly during the removal process.
What is the proper procedure for the dynamic test of the idle speed control valve?

Remove the idle speed control valve but keep the plug connected, open or close the rotary piston completely, turn on ignition, and verify the rotary piston moves into and remains in a position of approximately 50% of the cross-section opening.
Where should the hose be replaced during installation?
Replace hose 7 between the manifold and crankcase during installation.
What is the final step shown in the bottom diagram for valve removal?
Pull off plug 1, disconnect hoses 2 and 3, and disconnect the retaining strap.
What electrical test should be performed between which terminals?
Measure resistance between terminals 1 and 3, and also measure resistance between terminals 2 and 1 or 2 and 3.
What position should the rotary piston achieve during the dynamic test?
The rotary piston should move into and remain in a position of approximately 50% of the cross-section opening during the dynamic test.
What component cannot be pulled off and must be cut during removal?
The hose between the manifold and crankcase cannot be pulled off and must be cut off during removal.
What are the two main fuel pressure problems covered in this troubleshooting section?
Fuel Pressure Too High and Fuel Pressure Too Low.
What should I check first if the fuel pressure is too high?
Check if the vacuum hose to or on the pressure regulator is leaking or bent.
If the vacuum hose to the pressure regulator is okay but fuel pressure is still too high, what's the next step?
Check fuel return line routing and flow, then if that's okay, the pressure regulator is defective and should be replaced - see 13 51 200 in Group 13.
What's the first thing to check when diagnosing fuel pressure too low?
Check fuel feed line routing and flow.
If the fuel feed line is okay but pressure is still low, what should I check next?
Check flow in fuel filter.
What should I inspect on the fuel intake if the fuel filter flow is okay?
Check filter screen on fuel intake, cleaning if necessary - see 16 12 000 in Group 16.
What's the final step if all other checks pass for low fuel pressure?
Check pressure regulator, replacing if necessary - see 13 51 200 in Group 13.
Where can I find the procedure for replacing the pressure regulator?
See 13 51 200 in Group 13.
What reference code should I use for fuel intake filter screen cleaning?
16 12 000 in Group 16.
What additional information is available at the bottom of this page?
See Specifications and See Wiring Diagram are referenced at the bottom of the page.
How do you perform a mechanical air flow sensor test?
Detach intake hose on air flow sensor. Move sensor plate with finger. Sensor plate must move easily over entire range.
What BMW service test unit step is used to check the electric air flow sensor?
Use BMW service test unit / test step L-Jet. 04 to check air flow sensor test values.
What should you check if one or more fuel injectors are defective?
Start engine and check needle movement of fuel injectors with fingers. The needle movement must be felt.
Which test step is used to check fuel injector activation?
Check activation of fuel injectors with BMW service test unit/test step L-Jet. 02.
What test step is used to check fuel injector wires and coil?
