What should be checked during installation after unscrewing the heat shield?
Check for sufficient space between tank and heat shield during installation.
What component should be bolted on during installation according to the procedure?
Also bolt on holder for oxygen sensor plug during installation.
What is the proper torque specification for tightening the threaded sleeve?
Tighten threaded sleeve with Special Tool 26 1 040 after finishing installation to the specified tightening torque.
What steps are required for cars with manual transmission and vibration damper on output flange?
Support transmission, unscrew transmission suspension, and lower transmission for cars with manual transmission and vibration damper on output flange.
What component needs to be unscrewed from the transmission according to the final step?
Unscrew propeller shaft on transmission as the final step in the procedure.
What is the section number for replacing the joint disc for the rear propeller shaft?
Section 26 11 051 covers replacing the joint disc for the rear propeller shaft on all wheel drive vehicles.
What tool numbers are specified for loosening the threaded sleeve?
Special Tool 26 1 060 or 26 1 040 is used to loosen the threaded sleeve several turns.
What must be done before beginning the joint disc replacement procedure?
Remove exhaust assembly 18 00 020 and unscrew heat shields before starting the replacement procedure.
What important caution is given about propeller shafts?
Propeller shafts are balanced in assembled state and may only be replaced as such. Never disconnect propeller shafts on slide.
What should you avoid doing when letting the propeller shaft rest during the procedure?
Don't let propeller shaft rest on fuel tank connecting line.
How should the joint disc be installed according to the instructions?
Install joint disc so that arrows face flange arms, then tighten to specified torque.
What is the critical safety rule about tightening nuts or bolts on the flange end?
Only tighten nuts or bolts on flange end whenever possible by design, to avoid tension in joint disc.
What component reference number is shown for the special tool in the second image?
Reference number 26 1 040 is shown for the special tool used in the threaded sleeve procedure.
What should be done after finishing the installation of the threaded sleeve?
Tighten threaded sleeve with Special Tool 26 1 060 or 26 1 040 after finishing installation to specified tightening torque.
What is the first step in the installation sequence for replacing stop nuts?
Replace stop nuts and tighten to specified torque, following the important rule to only tighten nuts or bolts on flange end when possible.
What action is required for the propeller shaft on the power divider?
Unscrew propeller shaft on power divider, then push propeller shaft together and pull out of centering pin on power divider.
Where can the specific tightening torque values be found?
The tightening torque values are referenced with asterisks and can be found in the Specifications section.
How much should you turn the vibration damper when unscrewing the propeller shaft on transmission?
Turn vibration damper 60° and place on rubber coupling.
What important safety note is mentioned about the propeller shaft?
The propeller shaft was balanced in assembled state and may only be replaced as such. Do not disconnect propeller shaft on slide.
What caution is given about where to let the propeller shaft rest?
Don't let propeller shaft rest on fuel tank connecting line.
When installing the coupling, which direction should the arrows face?
Install coupling that arrows face flange arms.
What is the specified tightening torque for the coupling installation?
The tightening torque is marked with an asterisk, indicating it should be referenced in the specifications section.
What important rule applies when turning nuts and bolts on flange side?
Only turn nuts and bolts on flange side whenever permitted by design, to avoid stress in the coupling.
How far forward should you preload the center mount during installation?
Preload center mount forward by distance A = 4 to 6 mm (0.157 to 0.236 inches).
What diagram numbers are shown for the propeller shaft removal and center mount procedures?
What is the procedure section number for removing and installing the front propeller shaft on all wheel drive vehicles?
The procedure section number is 26 20 000 for removing and installing the front propeller shaft on all wheel drive vehicles.
What critical warning is given about operating the car after propeller shaft removal?
Never operate the car on its own engine power after removal of the propeller shaft, as this would damage the central lock in the transfer box.
How many bolts need to be removed during the propeller shaft removal procedure?
All six bolts need to be removed during the propeller shaft removal procedure.
What should be done with the stop nuts during installation?
Replace the stop nuts during installation and tighten to the specified torque.
What is the first step shown for removing the propeller shaft?
Push back the propeller shaft and remove the joint disc with centering disc.
Where should the centering disc be mounted during installation?
Mount the centering disc on the flange of the propeller shaft during installation.
What should be checked and potentially replaced during installation according to the seal inspection step?
Check the seal and replace if necessary during installation.
What installation instruction is given regarding the joint disc and flange arms?
Install the joint disc so that arrows face flange arms during installation.
What should be done with the gap and seal during the final installation step?
Check gap and seal, replacing if necessary, and slide cap on to transfer box after finishing installation.
What action is shown for removing the propeller shaft and cap from the transfer box?
Pull propeller shaft and cap off of transfer box as shown in the procedure.
Where can additional information be found according to the reference at the bottom of the page?
Additional information can be found in the Specifications section as referenced at the bottom of the page.
What is the part number for removing the exhaust assembly?
What should you do when tightening the threaded sleeve during installation?
Tighten threaded sleeve with Special Tool 26 1 060 or 26 1 040 after finishing installation. Tightening torque is referenced to specifications.
How should propeller shafts be handled when removing them?

Push propeller shaft together and pull out of centering pin on transfer box. Remove propeller shaft. Propeller shafts are balanced in assembled state and may only be replaced as such. Never disconnect propeller shafts on slide.
What important design consideration is mentioned for nuts and bolts on the flange?
Only turn nuts or bolts on flange and whenever possible by design, to avoid torsion in the joint coupling.
What should be replaced during installation according to the stop nuts section?
Replace stop nuts. Tightening torque is referenced to specifications.
What does the diagram in the bottom right corner illustrate?
A technical drawing showing the center joint assembly with lubrication points.
What inspection should be performed on the center during installation?
Check center, lubricating with Molykote Longterm 2 if necessary. Replace a damaged center.
What is the procedure number for replacing the joint disc for the front propeller shaft on all wheel drive vehicles?
The procedure number is 26 20 051.
How many bolts need to be removed when replacing the joint disc for the front propeller shaft?
Remove all six bolts.
What important instruction is given regarding the tightening torque when installing the stop nuts?
Replace stop nuts and apply the tightening torque. It's marked as 'Important!' that you only turn nuts on flange end whenever possible by design, to avoid tension in joint disc.
What should be done with the propeller shaft before removing the joint disc?
Push back propeller shaft, then remove joint disc with centering disc.
What direction should the joint disc arrows face during installation?
Install joint disc so that arrows face flange arms.
What should be done with the cap on the power divider after finishing installation?
Slide cap on to power divider after finishing installation.
What image numbers are shown for the joint disc replacement procedure?
Why is it important to only turn nuts on the flange end when possible?
To avoid tension in the joint disc, as noted in the important instruction.
What component is used together with the joint disc during installation?
The centering disc is used together with the joint disc and must be mounted on the flange of the propeller shaft.
Which mufflers need to be removed according to the procedure?
Remove and install primary and final mufflers 18 12 000.
What additional step is required for models since 1983?
Since 1983 Models: Unscrew connector.
What part number corresponds to the oxygen sensor plug holder?
Part number 30 26 021 corresponds to the bolt on holder for oxygen sensor plug.
What component is shown in image 30 26 023?
Image 30 26 023 shows the process of unscrewing the propeller shaft on transmission.
What component needs to be unscrewed in both removal and installation procedures?
The heat shield needs to be unscrewed in both removal and installation procedures.
What special tool is required to unscrew the threaded sleeve during propeller shaft removal?
Special Tool 26 1 040 is required to unscrew the threaded sleeve.
What important warning is given about the propeller shaft during disassembly?
The propeller shaft was balanced in assembled state and must not be turned in slide. You should punch mark an unmarked propeller shaft.
What lubricant should be used during installation and where?
Molykote Longterm 2** should be used to lubricate the slide during installation.
In what sequence should the components be assembled during installation according to the numbered callouts?
Slide on threaded sleeve (1), washer (2) and rubber ring (3), then assemble propeller shaft ensuring punch marks are aligned.
What is the significance of universal joints being mounted in one plane?
Propeller shaft sections are mounted to have universal joints in one plane. If slide had been taken apart without punch marking, only wrong installation by 180° is possible because of balancing.
How should the center mount complete with grooved ball bearing be removed?
Pull off center mount complete with grooved ball bearing as shown in the diagram.
What procedure is shown for installing the grooved ball bearing?
Press grooved ball bearing into center mount as illustrated in the installation diagram.
What final installation steps are required for the dust guard and center mount?
Slide on dust guard (1), then press on center mount with Special Tool 24 1 050.
What reference sources are noted at the bottom of the page for additional information?
The page references 'See Specifications' and lists 'Source: HWB' for additional information.
What could cause drumming noise from 60 km/h (35 mph) on?

Possible causes include propeller shaft not aligned precisely or installed with stress - axial compensator, center damaged, runout on centering pin/transmission/final drive flanges, centering error due to worn flange bores, excessive propeller shaft imbalance with balance plate missing, or universal joints worn or seized.
How do you correct propeller shaft alignment issues causing drumming noise?
Align propeller shaft or check movement of axial compensator, lubricating slide with Molykote Longterm 2 and tightening screw-on bushing to correct torque if necessary.
What part number is used to replace a damaged center?
Replace center - 26 11 501
How should you check for runout on centering pin and flanges?
Check centering pin and flanges for runout with dial gage - see Specifications; offset or replace final drive flange.
What causes center mount noise while driving?
Center mount not perpendicular to propeller shaft with no or insufficient preload, or center mount grooved ball bearing not okay.
What is the correct preload specification for the center mount?
Preload center mount 4 to 6 mm (0.157 to 0.236") in forward direction at right angle to propeller shaft.
What part number is needed to replace the center mount grooved ball bearing?
Replace grooved ball bearing - 26 12 001
What section reference is given for propeller shaft balancing procedures?
Balance or replace propeller shaft - see 26 11 000
What should you do if universal joints are worn or seized?
Check clearance and movement, replacing propeller shaft if necessary.
What correction is needed for centering error due to worn flange bores?
Replace transmission or final drive flange.
What special tool is required to remove the spring strut assembly?
Special Tool 31 3 000 is required to remove the spring strut assembly and take up spring strut in a vise.
What important note is given when a correction mount is used?
If a correction mount (see Group 32) is used, install a new mount with the same code.
What special tool is needed to set up the mount for spring compression?
Special Tool 31 3 116 should be set up on the mount for spring compression.
Which special tool is used specifically for All Wheel Drive Cars when setting up the mount?
For All Wheel Drive Cars, Special Tool 31 3 117 is used to set up on the mount.
What is the procedure for removing the guide sleeve and special tool compressor?
Remove washer (2), screw in guide sleeve 31 3 115 entire length of threads, then release and remove special tool compressor.
In what order are the components installed when lifting off the mount?
The installed order is: 1 Self-locking nut, 2 Washer with small diameter, 3 Mount, 4 Seal, 5 Washer with large diameter, 6 Cap.
What important safety note is given when using the spring compressor?
Pins must fit in openings when compressing the coil spring with Special Tool 31 3 111.
How should the self-locking nut be removed from the strut mount?
Pull off cap and unscrew self-locking nut with Special Tool 31 3 170.
What is the installation procedure for the self-locking nut?
Replace self-locking nut and tighten to specified torque.
Which direction should the internal curved surface of the seal face?
The internal curved surface of seal (4) faces the mount.
What special tools are required to replace the lockplate and lock during installation?
Special Tools 00 5 500 and 33 4 050 are required to replace the lockplate and lock.
What should be done with the tie rod joint during installation?
Keep grease off of pin and out of bore, replace the self-locking nut, and apply the specified tightening torque.
What special tool is needed to press off the guide joint?
Special Tool 31 2 160 is used to unscrew the nut and press off the guide joint.
What are the three main disconnections required when working on the spring strut?
Disconnect the brake pad wear indicator plug, disconnect the ground wire, and disconnect wires and brake hose on spring strut holders.
What happens to the brake line when the brake caliper is unscrewed and suspended?
The brake line remains connected when the brake caliper is unscrewed and suspended from the body on a piece of wire.
What lubrication instruction is given for the output shaft installation?
Lubricate splines of output shaft lightly with oil and pull in output shaft with Special Tools 33 2 112, 33 2 114 and 33 4 038.
What should be done when installing the guide joint according to the safety note?
Keep grease out of bore and off of pin, apply tightening torque, and lock the nut with a cotter pin.
What preliminary steps are required before removing the front spring strut assembly?
Remove the front wheel (see Group 36) and remove the ABS pulse transmitter (see Gr. 61).
How should the lockplate be handled during the strut assembly procedure?
Lift out the lockplate with a screwdriver and unscrew the collar nut during removal, then apply tightening torque during installation.
What reference information is provided for additional specifications?
See Specifications of Groups 31 and 34 for removal procedures, and see Specifications of Groups 31 and 32 for installation procedures.
What is the BMW part number for replacing bearings for drive pinion with the front axle final drive removed?
The part number is 31 52 510.
Should you replace just one bearing or both bearings when servicing the drive pinion?
Always replace both bearings according to the manual instructions.
What component is indicated by callout number 3 in the drive pinion assembly diagram?
Callout number 3 indicates the tapered roller bearing.
What should you inspect on the flange when replacing the shaft seal bearing surface?
You should check if the shaft seal bearing surface on the flange is scored seriously, and replace the flange if it is damaged.
What important note is given about the surfaces marked 'A' in the drive pinion bearing replacement?
Surfaces A are finish machined and you must be careful not to damage them during the procedure.
What components are indicated by callout numbers 9 and 10 in the assembly?
Callout number 9 indicates the shaft seal and callout number 10 indicates the case.
How should the lockplate be lifted out during disassembly?
Lift out the lockplate with a screwdriver.
What cross-reference is provided for removing the drive set from the front axle final drive?
The cross-reference is 31 52 505 for removing the drive set from the front axle final drive.
What are the part numbers for replacing the constant velocity joints?
Part number 31 60 020 for replacing one constant velocity joint (outer) and part number 31 60 021 for replacing one constant velocity joint (inner) of output shaft.
What should be removed first when servicing the constant velocity joints?
Remove front output shaft 31 60 000.
What type of hammer should be used to drive the joint off the shaft?
Use a plastic hammer to drive the joint off the shaft.
How should the splines of the shaft and joint be prepared before reassembly?
Clean and remove grease on splines of shaft and joint, then coat splines of shaft completely with Loctite No. 270.
What is the first step shown for removing the constant velocity joint?
Loosen both hose clamps and pull dust cover off of joint.
How much grease should be added to the outer constant velocity joint?
Add about half of the grease in a 80 gr. tube for the outer constant velocity joint.
What technique is used to remove the joint from the shaft after spreading the circlip?
Spread open circlip and drive joint off of the shaft with a plastic hammer.
What amount of grease should be added to the inner joint during reassembly?
Add grease of 70 gr. tube in joint for the inner joint.
What should be done to the outer joint during reassembly regarding grease?
Add remaining amount of grease in joint for the outer joint.
What diagram number shows the process of loosening hose clamps and removing the dust cover?
Diagram 30 31 595 shows loosening both hose clamps and pulling dust cover off of joint.
What diagram illustrates the circlip spreading technique?
Diagram 30 31 596 shows spreading open the circlip and driving the joint off the shaft with a plastic hammer.
What special tool is required to mount the front axle final drive in an assembly stand?
Special Tool 31 5 000 is required to mount the front axle final drive in an assembly stand.
What is the procedure section number for removing and installing the drive set?
The procedure section number is 31 52 505 for removing and installing the drive set.
What should be measured and noted during installation?
The thickness of shim (A) should be measured and noted during installation.
What component should be replaced during installation according to the instructions?
The seal (1) should be replaced during installation.
What bolt size is specified for removing the drive set?
Two M 8 x 30 bolts are specified for removing the drive set.
What is the first step shown in the procedure for working on the drive set?
The first step is to unscrew bolts, and the tightening torque for installation is specified with an asterisk reference.
What important alignment requirement is specified for installation?
The flat surfaces of the drive set faces must be flat surface on the case during installation.
What are the three main procedural steps shown in the diagrams?
The three steps are: mounting the drive in assembly stand with special tool, unscrewing bolts, and pulling the drive set out using M 8 x 30 bolts.
What component is labeled as (A) in the top diagram?
Component (A) is a shim whose thickness must be measured and noted during installation.
What diagram reference numbers are shown for the three procedural steps?
The diagram reference numbers are 30 31 507 for unscrewing bolts, 30 31 508 for pulling the drive set, and 30 31 511 for the shim measurement.
What is the correct installed order for the mount assembly components?
The installed order is: 1. Self-locking nut, 2. Washer with small diameter, 3. Mount, 4. Insulator, 5. Washer with large diameter, 6. Cap.
How should the insulator be positioned when installing the mount?
The inside curved surface of insulator (4) faces the mount.
What should be done with the spring strut tube when pulling out the shock absorber?
Remove old oil from spring strut tube (2). Fill new shock absorber with engine oil prior to installing. Engine oil will carry off heat from shock absorber to the spring strut tube.
What is the minimum piston rod diameter for single-pipe gas pressure cartridges that should not be installed with oil?
At least 33 mm (1.259") diameter piston rod. These cartridges may not be installed with oil.
What should you check when installing the upper spring retainer?
Check upper and lower rubber rings, replacing if necessary. Ends of coil spring must rest on shoulders in lower and upper spring retainers.
How should shock absorbers be stored to prevent damage?
Only store shock absorbers standing upright. If shock absorbers are stored laying down with their piston rods run in, this could cause rattling or knocking noise when used in car again.
What special tool is required to unscrew the screwed-on ring?
Special Tool 31 3 150 or 31 3 180.
What should be checked on the protective tube and rubber damper?
Check protective tube and rubber damper or rubber bellows, replacing if necessary.
What components are identified by callouts 1 and 2 in the shock absorber removal diagram?
Callout 1 indicates the shock absorber being pulled out, and callout 2 indicates the spring strut tube.
What special installation requirement applies to M 3 with EDC?
Install bolts (1) with a bolt cement. Tightening torque: See Specifications.
Where can you find the tightening torque specification for installation?
See Specifications section. For operating fluids, see Operating Fluids section. Source of Supply: HWB.
What procedure section is 31 33 100 covering?
Section 31 33 100 covers removing and installing/replacing left or right front spring strut coil spring.
What is the first step when removing the coil spring?
Remove spring strut mount 31 33 001, then remove upper spring retainer with rubber ring and coil spring.
What critical rule must be followed when installing pairs of springs?
Only install pairs of springs on one axle with same BMW number (1) on end of spring and same color code (2), either with or without a red paint stripe.
How do you determine the correct spare part number for a spring with red color code?
For a spring with red color code, find the number on the spring (e.g. 1 125 332), add 1 to get the part number (1 125 333).
What should be done with the protective tube and rubber damper during installation?
Check protective tube and rubber damper, replacing if necessary.
What is the thickness specification for the upper rubber ring installation?
Install upper rubber ring with thickness (A) = 9 mm (0.354") for coil springs with red color code.
How should the ends of the coil spring be positioned during installation?
Ends of coil spring must rest on shoulders in lower and upper spring retainers.
What part number calculation applies to springs without red color code?
For springs without red color code, find the number on spring (e.g. 1 125 332), add 2 to get part number (1 125 334).
What components should be inspected during installation according to the upper right instruction?
Check upper and lower rubber rings, replacing if necessary.
What reference should be consulted for cross-referencing springs and vehicle types?
Refer to spare part microfiche for cross reference of springs and vehicle types as well as applicable special equipment (air conditioner, sport suspension, etc.) and introduction dates.
What special tool is required to attach to the engine when replacing the front axle carrier?
Special Tool 00 0 200 is required to attach to the engine and support the bar on bolts of side panels.
Which groups should be referenced for removing the splash guard, front wheels, and air cleaner?
Remove splash guard - see Group 51, remove front wheels - see Group 36, and remove air cleaner - see Group 13.
What special tool is used to press off tie rods and what is the tool number?
Special Tool 32 2 070 is used to press off tie rods.
What should be done with the hydraulic lines during removal?
Unscrew hydraulic lines and insert plugs in openings to prevent contamination.
What important instruction is given about the steering spindle bolt during installation?
The slot of steering spindle faces mark of cap, and bolt must be in locking groove of steering shaft.
What special tool number is used to press off control arms?
Special Tool 31 2 160 is used to press off control arms.
What should be kept out of the bore and off the pin during installation of tie rods?
Keep grease out of bore and off of pin during installation.
What type of nuts should be replaced during installation?
Replace self-locking nuts during installation.
What should be done with control arm brackets nuts after installation?
Lock nuts with cotter pins after installation.
What needs to be replaced when reinstalling the hydraulic lines?
Replace gaskets when reinstalling the hydraulic lines.
What should be done after drawing off hydraulic fluid from the tank?
Fill power steering after completing the installation - see Group 32.
What special tool is required for all wheel drive cars when replacing front spring strut shock absorber?
Special Tool 31 3 117 must be set up on mount for all wheel drive cars.
What is the important requirement when replacing shock absorbers?

Always replace shock absorbers with ones having same code K. To know whether shock absorbers have to be replaced, check shock absorbers with a 'Shock Tester' or removed in an absorber testing machine.
Where can you find information about cars with Electronic Absorber Control (EDC)?
Refer to information in Group 37.
What special tool is used to compress the coil spring and what is the important note about it?
Special Tool 31 3 111 is used to compress coil spring. Important note: Pins must fit in openings.
How do you remove the spring strut assembly?
Remove spring strut assembly - see 31 31 000. Take up spring strut in a vise with Special Tool 31 3 000.
What tool is shown in diagram 31 3 170 and what is its purpose?
Special Tool 31 3 170 is shown for lifting off cap and unscrewing self-locking nut, counterholding the piston rod.
What should be done during installation regarding the self-locking nut?
Replace self-locking nut and apply tightening torque (see specifications).
What special tool is referenced as 31 3 116 and what should be done with it?
Special Tool 31 3 116 should be set up on mount.
What components should be removed according to tool 31 3 115?
Take off washer (2). Screw in Special Tool 31 3 115 entire length of threads. Release and take off special tool compressor.
What service information reference is provided for additional shock absorber information?
Also refer to Service Information 37 02 83 (177).
What visual components are shown in the spring assembly diagram labeled 31 3 115?
The diagram shows the coil spring, strut assembly components, and the special tool compressor setup with washer (2) that needs to be removed.
What page number contains information about the front wheel suspension layout drawing?
Page 31-1 contains the front wheel suspension layout drawing.
On which page can I find procedures for replacing the front axle carrier?
Front axle carrier replacement procedures can be found on page 31-4.
Where can I find information about checking rubber mounts for control arms?
Information about checking rubber mounts for control arms is located on page 31-8.
What section number covers the drive flange for front axle replacement for all wheel drive models?
Section 31 21 121 covers the drive flange for front axle replacement for all wheel drive models, found on page 31-9.
Which page contains procedures for spring strut removal and installation for all wheel drive vehicles?
Page 31-11.1 contains procedures for spring strut removal and installation for all wheel drive vehicles.
What is the section number for shock absorber replacement for front spring strut?
Section 31 32 001 covers shock absorber replacement for front spring strut, found on page 31-13.
What should be done to the tapped bores before installation?
The tapped bores should be cleaned before installation.
What type of compound should be used when installing bolts?
Always replace and install bolts with a bolt cement and apply the tightening torque.
What must be done to both control arms during the procedure?
Unscrew both control arms.
How should the control arms be positioned during installation?
Mount control arms in installed position, so that rubber parts of tapered joints are not turned wrong.
What type of nuts should be replaced on the control arms?
Replace self-locking nuts on the control arms.
Which components need to be unscrewed for engine and steering gear removal?
Unscrew engine mounts and steering gear.
What type of nuts should be replaced for the engine mounts and steering gear?
Replace self-locking nuts for the engine mounts and steering gear.
What is the first step shown in the procedure?
Unscrew left and right stabilizer mounts.
What critical warning is given about the tapered joints during control arm installation?
The rubber parts of tapered joints must not be turned wrong during installation.
What procedure is referenced in section 36 10 300?
Remove and install front wheels.
What tool should be used to check front wheel alignment after installation?
Optical tester 32 00.
How should the pin be loosened when removing components?
Loosen pin by applying knocks with a plastic hammer.
What should be done with the control arm brackets during the procedure?
Disconnect left and right control arm brackets.
What components need to be unscrewed on both left and right sides of the stabilizer?
Thrust rods on left and right sides of stabilizer.
What type of nuts should be used when installing left and right nuts?
Use lock nut (1) and washer (2) instead of standard polystop nut.
What preparation is required for the pins and bores before installation?
Pins and bores cleaned to remove grease.
What should be replaced when unscrewing the steering gear on the front axle carrier?
Replace self-locking nuts.
Where are the mounting points located for the front axle carrier?
Mounting points are at the rear bores of front axle carrier.
What specific engine configuration has different instructions for disconnecting the engine damper?
Four Cylinder Engines have specific instructions to disconnect engine damper on front axle carrier.
What reference should be consulted for additional specifications related to Group 32?
See Specifications of Gr. 32.
What is emphasized as important when dealing with tightening torques throughout the procedure?
Tightening torque is marked as important for multiple installation steps.
What HWB part number should be used for the new grease cap with cement?
What special tools are needed to pull off the bearing unit according to the procedure?
Special Tools 31 2 101/102/104 are required to pull off the bearing unit.
What important warning is given about a pulled off bearing unit?
A pulled off bearing unit must not be reused.
What should always be done with grease caps during this procedure?
Always replace grease caps and install new grease cap with cement.
What special tool is used to break the collar nut with a cross chisel?
Special Tool 11 2 180 is used to break the collar nut with a cross chisel.
What special tool numbers are mentioned for the M3 bearing installation?
Special Tool 31 2 080 for M3, and for installation, Special Tools 31 2 102/105/106 are mentioned.
What special tools are needed to bend the dust guard back and pull off the bearing inner race?
Special Tool 00 7 500 and Special Tool 33 1 309 are needed for this operation.
What important note is given about removing the guard after pulling off the bearing unit?
Remove the guard if the inside bearing inner race remains on the stub axle after pulling off the bearing unit.
What must not be reused according to the bearing unit installation notes?
The bearing unit must not be reused once it has been pulled off.
What special tools are required to dip the new shaft seal in gear lube and drive it against the stop?
Special Tools 31 5 020 and 00 5 500 are required to dip the new shaft seal in gear lube and drive it against the stop.
What tool is needed to mount the flange and tighten the collar nut?
Special Tool 00 2 000 is needed to mount the flange and tighten the collar nut in steps until the specified friction torque is reached.
What should be done if the friction torque is exceeded during the tightening process?
If the friction torque is exceeded, replace the bushing and repeat the adjusting procedures.
What three adjustments are necessary because of new bearings after installing the lockplate?
Because of new bearings, it is necessary to adjust: a) ring gear/pinion block distance, b) backlash of ring gear, and c) tooth contact pattern.
Where can you find information about the front axle final drive adjustments mentioned in this procedure?
See adjustments on front axle final drive for the specific procedures.
What component identification number is shown for the shaft seal installation tool in the first diagram?
The component identification number 30 31 510 is shown in the first diagram for the shaft seal installation procedure.
What is the purpose of turning the assembly uniformly during the collar nut tightening procedure?
The assembly should be turned uniformly with Special Tool 00 2 000 while tightening until the specified friction torque is reached.
What component identification number appears in the third diagram showing the lockplate installation?
Component identification number 30 31 506 appears in the third diagram showing the lockplate installation.
What is emphasized as important when installing the new lockplate?
It is important that because of new bearings, several adjustments are necessary including ring gear/pinion block distance, backlash of ring gear, and tooth contact pattern.
Where are the specifications for the friction torque referenced in this procedure?
The specifications for the friction torque are referenced at the bottom of the page with an asterisk noting 'See Specifications'.
What component identification number is shown in the second diagram for the collar nut tightening procedure?
Component identification number 30 31 505 is shown in the second diagram for the collar nut tightening procedure.
What procedure is being described in section 31 10 000?
Removing and installing front axle assembly.
Which cars require steering wheel removal according to the SRS note?
Only cars with SRS require steering wheel removal, and you should see Group 32 for the procedure.
What should be checked after front axle installation?
Check front wheel alignment with an optical tester after installation, referencing Group 32.

What should I do if the car body keeps swinging long after passing over rough road surfaces?
This indicates weak shock absorber efficiency. Replace the shock absorbers and refer to the Troubleshooting Shock Absorbers section for detailed procedures.
What causes the body to wipe or oscillate when passing over successive rough road surfaces?
Shock absorber efficiency weak. See the Troubleshooting Shock Absorbers section for diagnostic procedures.
If the car body rises when accelerating, what is the likely cause and correction?
The cause is weak shock absorber efficiency. The correction is to replace the shock absorbers, and you should see the Troubleshooting Shock Absorbers section.
What does it mean when wheels are jumping even on normal road surfaces?
This symptom indicates shock absorber efficiency weak. Replace the shock absorbers and refer to Troubleshooting Shock Absorbers for additional guidance.
How should I address a car that breaks out when braking?
Replace the shock absorbers, as this condition is caused by weak shock absorber efficiency. See Troubleshooting Shock Absorbers section for detailed procedures.
What causes breaking out or skidding in curves due to poor track holding?
Shock absorber efficiency weak. See the Troubleshooting Shock Absorbers section for diagnostic and repair procedures.
What section should I reference for detailed shock absorber troubleshooting?
All the front axle troubleshooting conditions reference the Troubleshooting Shock Absorbers section for additional diagnostic procedures.
What symptom indicates poor shock absorber performance during normal driving conditions?
Wheels jumping even on normal road surfaces indicates weak shock absorber efficiency and requires shock absorber replacement.
If I'm experiencing multiple symptoms like body movement and poor handling, what is the likely root cause?

All the symptoms listed (long after-swinging, wiping over rough roads, body rising when accelerating, wheel jumping, breaking out when braking, and skidding in curves) are caused by weak shock absorber efficiency.

What should I check if I hear grinding noise in curves from the front axle?

What are the possible causes of vibration in the front axle?
Vibration can be caused by wheels unbalanced, wheel rim lateral/radial runout, tire lateral runout, or defective output shaft.
How do I fix steering wheel shake caused by insufficient shock absorber effect?
Replace shock absorbers.
What causes rattling noise from the front axle?

Tighten threaded ring (inspect threads).

How do I address oil loss from the front axle?
Check for radial oil seal leak, plugged vent, or incorrect oil grade. Replace radial oil seal, clean vent, or replace front axle final drive oil as needed.
What causes acceleration or deceleration noise from the front axle?
Excessive or insufficient backlash causes acceleration or deceleration noise. The correction is to adjust backlash.

What happens to the tooth contact pattern when loads are applied to the differential?

Loads will displace the tooth contact pattern slightly more toward the outside. Moving the ring gear will mainly change the backlash and also the tooth contact pattern in longitudinal direction of the teeth.

What effect does moving the drive pinion have on the tooth contact pattern adjustments?

What is the procedure number for removing and installing rear shock absorbers?
The procedure number is 33 52 000 for removing and installing rear shock absorbers.
What important safety warning is given about storing shock absorbers?
Always store shock absorbers standing upright. If shock absorbers are stored laying down with their piston rods run in, they will cause knocking noise when used in car.
What is the recommended remedy for shock absorbers with run out piston rods?
Store shock absorbers with run out piston rods standing upright at room temperature for at least 24 hours.
What caution is given about the shock absorber during removal?
Shock absorber acts as a retaining strap. Do not remove the support or lift the car, to avoid damage on constant velocity joints.
What should be done with the car loading when tightening shock absorbers during installation?
Tighten shock absorbers with car loaded down to normal position to the specified tightening torque.
Which group should be referenced for cars with ride level control?
See Group 37 for cars with ride level control.
What additional steps are required for Touring Models during shock absorber removal?
For Touring Models: Remove side backrest (see Gr. 52), Remove seat belt reels (see Gr. 72), and Unscrew centering shell on wheel house.
What component should be replaced during shock absorber installation according to the important note?
Replace gasket (1) during shock absorber installation.
What type of nut should be replaced during installation?
Replace self-locking nut during installation to the specified tightening torque.
What should be done with the trunk trim panel during this procedure?
Remove trunk trim panel partially - see Group 51.
What should be done to support the semi-trailing arm during shock absorber removal?
Support semi-trailing arm or have road wheel rest on floor, then unscrew shock absorber on semi-trailing arm.
What could cause a loud change knock in the rear axle?
A loud change knock can be caused by excessive backlash, output shaft faulty, or play in propeller shaft slide.
How do I fix excessive backlash that's causing a load change knock?
Adjust backlash - see 33 12 551.
What should I do if the output shaft is faulty and causing noise?
Replace output shaft - see 33 21 000.
What causes traction or compression noise in the rear axle?
Traction or compression noise is caused by backlash that is excessive or insufficient.
What are the possible causes of drumming noise from the rear axle?
Drumming can be caused by propeller shaft issues or rubber mounts on rear axle carrier faulty.
What should I check if there's rattling noise from the rear axle?
Check for shock absorbers installed loose, upper or lower shock absorber rubber ring faulty, rubber mounts on rear axle carrier faulty, or shock absorbers faulty or worn.
What causes grinding noise only when driving in curves?
Grinding noise only when driving in curves is caused by wheel bearings faulty.
How do I fix faulty wheel bearings that cause grinding in curves?
Replace wheel bearings - see 33 41 141.
What should be removed first when working on the trailing arm assembly?
Remove rear wheel - 36 10 300.
What brake system maintenance is required when removing the parking brake lever?
Draw off brake fluid in tank with a syringe reserved exclusively for brake fluids. Remove filter screen sleeve.
What must be done to the brake system during installation after removing the parking brake lever?
Add brake fluid and bleed brakes.
What should be operated before removing the output shaft if necessary?
Operate parking brake.
What is the procedure for disconnecting the brake line during installation?
Disconnect brake line. Installation: Tightening torque*.
What important step is mentioned when unscrewing the trailing arm on rear axle carrier?
First guide in brake bolt for inner bracket. Important! Tighten bolts with car in normal position*.
What components are shown being removed in the support trailing arm procedure?
Unscrew shock absorber and lower trailing arm.
What special positioning requirement is noted when tightening bolts?
Tighten bolts with car in normal position.
What output shaft procedure reference is mentioned if necessary during removal?
If necessary, remove output shaft 33 21 000.
What is the procedure number for replacing the rubber mount for the final drive?
The procedure number is 33 17 001.
What special tool is required for pressing out and pulling in the rubber mount?
Special Tool 33 2 120 is required for both pressing out and pulling in the rubber mount.
What should you do before removing the rubber mount mounting bolt?
Pull off wires on speed pulse transmitter before removing the rubber mount mounting bolt.
What type of nuts should be replaced during installation of the rubber mount?
Replace self-locking nuts during installation.
What important check must be performed after installing the rubber mount?
Check the installed position of the rubber mount to ensure it is properly positioned.
What condition might indicate the rubber mount is eccentric?
If the rubber mount is eccentric, make sure the special tool is applied correctly.
What are the initial steps for replacing the rubber mount?
Loosen nuts on rear axle carrier and support the final drive.
What should be done with the tightening torque during installation?
Apply the tightening torque as specified (marked with asterisk indicating reference to specifications).
What does the bottom image show in relation to the final drive?
The bottom image shows the lower final drive assembly and the installed position of the rubber mount.
Where can additional specifications for this procedure be found?

What safety consideration is noted regarding the special tool application?
The note emphasizes that if the rubber mount is eccentric, make sure the special tool is applied correctly to avoid improper installation.
What part number is being replaced in the dust cover replacement procedure?
Output shaft 33 21 000 is being removed during the dust cover replacement procedure.
What important caution is given about the thicker output shafts and joints for the BMW M3?
Don't mix up the thicker output shafts and joints for the BMW 325 i, as they are different from the M3 components.
What are the numbered components shown in the circlip removal diagram?
Component 1 is the sealing cover, component 2 is the circlip, and component 3 is the cap and dust cover assembly.
Where must the ball hub rest when pressing the output shaft out of the constant velocity joint?
The ball hub must rest on counterpressure plate (P) when pressing the output shaft out.
What special tool is required for pressing on the joint and cap while holding the output shaft?
Special Tool 33 2 100 is required for pressing on the joint and cap while holding the output shaft.
What type of Loctite should be used on the splines and what caution is given?
Coat splines with Loctite No. 270, but keep Loctite out of ball surfaces.
What should be done if the joint has to be disassembled when it's dirty?
If the joint has to be disassembled when dirty, first electrically inscribe position of ball hub, ball cage and joint to each other face, as absolute cleanliness is important during assembly work.
How should the dust cover be protected during installation?
Be careful not to damage new dust covers and protect them from the sharp edges on the splined shaft with a suitable sleeve.
What should be done to the splines of the joint before reassembly?
Clean splines of joint to remove grease before coating them with Loctite No. 270.
What components should be packed with grease during reassembly?
Pack joint and dust cover with grease, and clean sealing surfaces for dust cover to remove grease.
How should the large diameter end of the dust cover be treated during installation?
Coat large diameter end of dust cover with an adhesive and mount with new clamps.
What should be used to seal and install the sealing cover?
Seal and install sealing cover with Curil.
What specific procedure is described for the rear axle final drive with constant velocity joint?
Unscrew propeller shaft on rear axle final drive.
What are the installation steps for the constant velocity joint?
Check gasket, replacing if necessary. Replace stop nuts. Apply tightening torque.
Why is the constant velocity joint not encapsulated according to the manual?
The constant velocity joint is not encapsulated. It must be protected against dirt with a transporting cap or something similar.
What important maintenance check is required for the constant velocity joint?
Check grease filling.
How should the constant velocity joint be protected during handling?
Protect the joint against dirt with a transporting cap or something similar.
What is the page number and section reference for this information?
Page 33-1.1 from Section 33 covering the rear axle.
What type of joint is being serviced in this procedure?
A constant velocity joint on the rear axle final drive.
What fastening procedure is specified during installation?
Apply tightening torque as specified.
What critical warning is given about the constant velocity joint's design?
The constant velocity joint is not encapsulated and must be protected against dirt contamination.
What section reference is given for removing the wheel when working on the output shaft?
Group 36 is referenced for wheel removal procedures.
What should be done to the bearing surface of the nut during installation?
The bearing surface of the nut should be lubricated with oil during installation.
What special tool is used to press off the output shaft?
Special Tool 33 2 110 is used to press off the output shaft.
Which special tools have been replaced and what are their current replacements?
Spindle 33 2 111 and bridge 33 2 112 are replaced by 33 2 116, and Special Tool 33 2 113 is replaced by 33 2 117 and wheel bolts are used.
What should be done with the lockplate during installation?
The lockplate should be replaced during installation.
What special tool number is shown in the bottom image for pulling the output shaft?
Special Tool 33 2 110 is shown in the bottom image for pulling the output shaft.
What additional components are needed when using Special Tool 33 2 110 to pull the output shaft?
Bridge 33 2 116 and nut 33 2 115 are needed when using Special Tool 33 2 110.
How should the spindle 33 2 114 be positioned when pulling the output shaft?
The spindle 33 2 114 should be screwed in completely when pulling the output shaft.
What drive-in method is referenced for the lockplate installation?
Drive in lockplate with Special Tools 33 4 050 and 00 5 000 is referenced for installation.
What is the procedure code for replacing the shaft seal for drive flange?
The procedure code is 33 11 151.
What special tool is needed to pull out the shaft seal?
Special Tool 00 5 010 is needed to pull out the shaft seal, used in conjunction with a pressure piece.
How should the output shaft be supported during removal?
Unscrew the output shaft on drive flange and suspend it on a piece of wire.
What tool is used to press off the drive flange with tire irons?
The image shows tire irons being used to press off the drive flange, as indicated in the middle left photograph.
When should the drive flange be replaced?
Replace the drive flange with a seriously scored bearing surface.
What is the purpose of the wire snap ring mentioned in the installation procedure?
Prior to installation of drive flange, place wire snap ring (1) in groove of differential case so that both ends of wire snap ring are recessed in groove to prevent lateral bending of ring.
How should the drive flange be pressed in during installation?
Press in drive flange by hand and turn slightly until wire snap ring is heard to engage.
What should be done with stretched wire snap rings?
Replace stretched wire snap rings.

What wheels need to be removed and installed during this brake force regulator check?
Remove and install front wheel 36 10 300 and remove and install rear wheel 36 10 320.
Where is the second high pressure meter connected?
Connect second high pressure meter in rear wheel brake bleeder screw.
How many times should the brake pedal be operated during this test?
Operate brake pedal firmly at least 5 times.
What pressure should both high pressure meters display up to 25 bar?
Up to a pressure of 25 bar (355 psi) both high pressure meters should display the same value.
What do the letters A, B, and C represent on the pressure diagram?
A = Inlet pressure, B = Outlet pressure, C = Switching over pressure.
What are the example pressure values given for Pressure I at the inlet and outlet?
Inlet pressure (front axle pressure): 40 bar (569 psi), Outlet pressure (rear axle pressure): 31.8 bar (452 psi).
What should you do if measured values deviate from specified values?
If measured values deviate from specified values, replace the brake force regulator.
How should the brake pedal be held during the pressure test?
Hold brake pedal pressed down with a pedal prop.
What is recommended if multiple measurements are needed?
If necessary, take mean value from three measurements.

What voltage measurement is being tested in this step?
Voltage between wires 1 and 10
What should be done before testing the solenoid pressure build-up/drop/hold?
Turn on ignition, run engine, and check that battery is charged.
What could cause high switching on power during this test?
Due to high switching on power, it may be necessary to repeat the test step with engine running.
What are the job position codes referenced for this troubleshooting?

Only the pressure building-up and pressure holding phases (2 A) can be checked in 325 iX cars because of the changed activation times in the control unit.
Where will irregular values be displayed in 325 iX cars?
Irregular values will be displayed on adapter B in switch position (5 A).
What are the two main procedures covered in section 34-19?
The two main procedures are 34 41 000 REMOVING AND INSTALLING PARKING BRAKE LEVER and 34 41 100 REMOVING AND INSTALLING PARKING BRAKE CABLE.
How do you remove the rubber cap from the parking brake lever?
Take off rubber cap (1) by pulling up clamp at front and lifting out at rear.
What is the first step when removing the parking brake cable?

Unscrew nuts (2) on parking brake cables.

Unscrew bolt, then disconnect consols by pushing back and remove.
Where do you disconnect the parking brake cable in the installation procedure?
Disconnect parking brake cable on semi-trailing arm.

What should be inspected before performing a brake test on the test stand?
Inspect condition and treads of tires and also check/correct tire inflation pressure prior to testing the brakes.
What is the maximum time that cars with four wheel drive (325 iX) can be tested on a brake test dynamometer?
Cars with four driven wheels (325 iX) must not be tested on a brake test dynamometer longer than 60 seconds or faster than 7.5 km/h (4.5 mph) to avoid damaging the central lock.
What is the maximum pressure drop allowed after 2 minutes during the high pressure leak test?
The maximum pressure drop after 2 minutes is 8%.
What range of pressure should be used for the low pressure brake test?
The low pressure test should use a pressure range of 2 to 5 bar (28 to 71 psi).
How long should you wait between brake tests if testing needs to be repeated?
If testing has to be repeated, wait at least 30 minutes to allow the brakes to cool down.
What must be done with the engine during the high pressure leak test?
The high pressure leak test must be performed with the engine stopped.
What should be done after completing the low pressure brake test?
Bleed brake calipers and wheel brake cylinders after finishing the test.
What is shown in diagram 30.34.001?
Diagram 30.34.001 shows the brake test setup with a pressure gauge and brake pedal application.
What roller speed corresponds to 50 rpm wheel speed according to the conversion chart?
According to the conversion chart, 50 rpm wheel speed corresponds to 12.5 km/h roller speed.
What condition must the brakes be in before testing?
The brakes should have operating temperature, meaning brake discs/drums should be warm and dry by driving the car several times.
What should you do if pressure drops considerably during the low pressure test?
If pressure drops considerably, inspect all rubber parts.
How long should the low pressure test be maintained?
The pressure should remain constant during a 5 minute test, and the car and tester must remain still since movement would cause incorrect test results.
What is the air pressure required to press out the piston and what force does this equate to?
10 bar (140 psi) air pressure is equal to a force of about 1250 N (275 lbs.).
How should the seal be removed from the cylinder bore?
Remove seal carefully with a plastic needle.
What cleaning procedure should be followed for cylinder bores and parts?
Clean cylinder bores and parts with alcohol and dry with compressed air.
What should you do first when installing the piston?
First pull rubber guard on to piston. Don't cant piston.
What should be placed in the caliper recess to protect the piston?
Place a liner (hard wood, hard felt or similar material) in caliper recess to protect the piston.
What inspection should be performed on pistons and flange surfaces?
Inspect pistons and flange surfaces thoroughly for damage.
What is specifically not approved regarding cylinder bores and pistons?
Machining of cylinder bores and pistons is not approved.
How should the brake pad be positioned before inserting the spring?
Push brake pad toward outside completely before inserting spring.
What component should be checked and possibly replaced from the repair kit?
Check dowel sleeves (5), replacing with dowel sleeves from repair kit if necessary.
What tool should be used to press in the piston during assembly?
Press in piston with a piece of hard wood.
How should the rubber guard be positioned over the cylinder bore?
Pull rubber guard over edge of cylinder bore and secure with a clamping ring.

This is an index or table of contents page for the Brakes section.
What is the basis of a braking action according to this ABS system description?
The basis of a braking action is the friction between the tires and road surface.
What happens to the frictional force when a wheel is locked with 100% slip?
When a wheel is locked with 100% slip, the frictional force will normally be lower than when a wheel is rolling.
What does the ABS control range represent in the diagram?
The ABS control range is shown as the shaded area where the transmitted braking force reaches its maximum value, which is also where ABS operates to prevent wheel lock.
What do the letters A through G represent in the diagram legend?
A = ABS operating range, B = Braking and lateral force, C = Braking force, D = Lateral force, E = Rolling wheel, F = Slip, G = Locked wheel.
How does ABS control brake pressure to maintain optimal frictional force?
The ABS must control the brake pressure in the wheel brake cylinder so that the slip remains in the shaded area, because here the highest frictional force is available.
What factors affect the amount of slip and frictional force according to the manual?

The amount of slip and frictional force depend chiefly on the tires (type, treads, rubber composition), the road surface (material, surface condition, wet, ice), the road speed and the slip angle of the wheel.
How does ABS detect and respond to frictional conditions?

The ABS detects the frictional conditions between the tires and road surface prevailing at the moment. It automatically adjusts to each change in road surface/tire relation and makes use of the highest coefficient of friction, without the vehicle slips or skids because of wheel lock.
What benefit does ABS provide for lateral cornering force and steering stability?

ABS ensures there will be sufficient lateral cornering force to guarantee steering and directional stability by maintaining the slip in the optimal range where both braking and lateral forces are available.
What is the procedure number for removing and installing front brake pads?
The procedure number is 34 11 000 for removing and installing front brake pads.
What should you do first when removing front brake pads?
Remove front wheels (see procedure 36 10 300) and pull off brake pad wear indicator plug on left side.
What important note is given about the locking bolt when removing brake calipers?
Replace the locking bolt and counterhold on guide pin during installation, then tighten to torque specification.
What does callout number 5 indicate in the brake pad wear indicator diagram?
Callout number 5 indicates the brake pad wear indicator that should be driven out carefully and checked when reusing.
What special tool is required when removing front brake calipers?
A syringe which is used exclusively with brake fluid to draw off brake fluid.
What should you check regarding pad thickness during installation?
Check pads and pad thickness, then push back brake pistons completely.
What critical warning is given about the dust cover during brake work?
Be careful not to damage dust cover on brake piston when assembling. Check dust cover and check installed position of springs.
How many caliper mounting bolts need to be unscrewed according to the procedure?
One caliper mounting bolt needs to be unscrewed, with tightening torque specified for installation.
What should be done after pulling off the caliper toward the rear?
Make sure of correct location of brake pad wear indicator wires with tab of dust cap, and prevent rubbing of the wires on the wheel rim.
Where can you find the bleeding procedure for the brakes?
The bleeding procedure can be found in section 34 00 046/047.
What does callout number 4 show in the bottom left image?
Callout number 4 shows the springs whose installed position should be checked during the installation process.
What ABS system is shown in this wiring diagram?
ABS system 325 iX
When was the ABS system 325 iX introduced?
Introduced gradually since 8/87
What component is identified as number 360 in the wiring diagram?
Electronic control unit
What does component 361 represent in this ABS system?
Hydraulic control unit
What are the signal sender components numbered 362, 364, 366, and 368?
362 is signal sender front left, 364 is signal sender front right, 366 is signal sender rear left, and 368 is signal sender rear right
What does KL61 represent in the diagram legend?

What component is labeled as 375 in the acceleration system?
Acceleration sender

d is Valve - front left, e is Valve - front right, and f is Valve - rear left
What should I do before pulling off a plug and measuring resistance in test step 05?
Turn off ignition before pulling off a plug and measuring resistance.
What are the initial steps to test voltage between wires 1 and 10?
Turn on ignition, run engine, and ensure battery is charged before checking.
Where should I check the ground connections for wires 10, 20, and 34?
Check ground connection below instrument panel on left side for all three ground wires.
What should I check for wire 14/return delivery pump ground?
Check ground connection on battery console, check ground connection on return delivery pump, and check flow in ground wire and multiple pin plug on wire harness.
What job position number applies to checking ground wire connections?
Job position 61 11 530 applies to checking ground wire 10, 20, and 34 connections.
What should I do if there is a power flow break in the wire harness?
Replace wire harness if there is power flow break.
What job position covers replacing the electronic relay?
Job position 34 52 510 covers replacing the electronic relay.
What happens if the motor relay only switches at intervals without the pump motor running?
The voltage will briefly drop excessively due to the high switching on power at the feed wires from the battery. Repeat test with engine running and see test steps 04, 06, and 07.
What is the remedy for overvoltage protector issues?
Replace electronic relay. Note that there is no overvoltage protection relay since 1989 models.
What should I do for fault simulation in the test cycle?
Replace control unit and watch the above mentioned points.
What are the procedure numbers for removing and installing the front and rear ABS pulse speed sensors?
The front pulse speed sensor procedure is 61 12 510 and the rear pulse speed sensor procedure is 61 12 520.
What should you do first when removing either the front or rear ABS pulse speed sensor?
Turn off ignition and unscrew the socket head bolt.
What lubricant should be used on the pulse sensor and housing during installation?
Molykote Longterm 2 should be used to lubricate the pulse sensor and housing prior to installation.
Can the distance between the pulse sensor and pulse wheel be adjusted?
No, the distance between pulse sensor and pulse wheel is given by design and cannot be adjusted.
What inspection should be performed on the pulse wheel during installation?
It is necessary to visually inspect the pulse wheel for dirt or damage.
For the rear ABS pulse sensor, what component must be removed first?
Remove rear wheel 36 10 300.
What ABS reference number should be checked when replacing the front pulse sensor?
Check ABS - see 34 50 000.
What important warning is given regarding the rear pulse sensor rubber grommet?
Don't damage the rubber grommet.
Can the front ABS pulse wheel be replaced separately?
No, the front pulse wheel can only be replaced together with the bearing assembly, and you should see Replacing Wheel Hub - 31 21 180.
What should you do to access the front pulse sensor wiring?
Disconnect plug in engine compartment, push wires down, and lift out wires.
What components need to be removed to access the rear pulse sensor?
Remove rear seat cushion 52 20 010, disconnect pulse sensor plug, pull out rubber grommet and wires, then remove pulse sensor.
What is the maximum distance the parking brake should be effective for driving from the parking lot to workplace?
Max. 400 meters (1300 feet) with the parking brake applied (pull up lever until resistance is felt and then one further catch) before adjusting the parking brake.
How many teeth should the parking brake lever be pulled up by when the parking brake needs to be adjusted?
The parking brake needs to be adjusted when the parking brake lever can be pulled up by more than 8 teeth.
What are the first three steps for adjusting the parking brake?
1. Lift out front clamp, 2. Pull off rubber cap (1), 3. Disconnect rear clamp.
How many adjusting bolts need to be unscrewed and what is shown in step 2?
Two adjusting bolts (2) need to be unscrewed, as shown in the diagram labeled as step 2.
What should you do with the rear wheels during the parking brake adjustment procedure?
Unscrew one wheel bolt on each rear wheel and remove. Turn wheels so that each tapped bore is approx. 30° behind the perpendicular on top.
How do you adjust the parking brake shoes and prevent the brake disc from turning?
Turn adjusting nut (1) with a screwdriver to move out the parking brake shoe and prevent the brake disc from turning. Then loosen adjusting nut by 3 or 4 threads.
What indicates that basic clearance will be adjusted automatically on the drums?
Basic clearance will be adjusted automatically, which is indicated by a clicking noise on the rear wheels when operating the brake pedal several times.
How do you perform the brake cable adjustment?
Pull up parking brake lever by 5 teeth and adjust adjusting nuts (2) enough that left and right rear wheels can just be turned and both uniformly.
What should you check after releasing the parking brake lever?
Release parking brake lever and check whether wheels can be turned easily. The indicator lamp should go out when the parking brake is released with the ignition on.
What is the proper tightening specification mentioned for installation?
Tightening torque is specified (with an asterisk reference), though the specific value references the Specifications section.
What causes the force required for operating the parking brake to increase?

The force required for operating will increase proportionally due to limited wear since the parking brake will not be needed during normal car operation, which consequently reduces the friction torque caused by corrosion of brake drums or contamination of linings.
How can you check the function of automatic slack control?
Function of automatic slack control can be checked through a wheel bolt bore by operating the brake pedal several times and listening for the clicking noise that indicates basic clearance adjustment.
What is test step 08 checking on the ABS system?
Test step 08 is checking the ABS return delivery pump, specifically testing voltage between wires 1 and 10, and front left/right and rear left/right connections.
What conditions should be met when testing the ABS return delivery pump?
The ignition should be turned on, engine running, and battery charged (check).
What should you do if there's high switching on power during the ABS test?
Due to high switching on power, possibly repeat test step with engine running. Refer to test steps 05, 06 and 07.
What conventional brake system components need to be checked for proper ABS operation?
The conventional brake system must be okay: bled properly, brake line connections tight, brake pads okay, master and wheel cylinders okay.
What should you observe about the wheels during ABS testing?
Watch uniformity of wheels on one axle and observe relation between wheel reading.
What is the corrective action if brake lines are mixed up on the hydraulic unit?
Replace hydraulic unit. The job position reference is 34 51 520.
What restriction applies to performing this test step on 325 iX cars?

This test step may not be performed on a dynamometer for 325 iX cars, since the total loading time for the central lock in the transfer box must not exceed 60 seconds at a wheel speed of max. 7.5 km/h (4.5 mph).
What reference should you consult for brake test dynamometer information on 325 iX cars?
Refer to brake test dynamometer in 34 00 009.
What group does this ABS return delivery pump test belong to?
This test belongs to Group 34.
What are the potential causes if the ABS return delivery pump test fails?

Potential causes include high switching on power issues, improperly bled brake system, loose brake line connections, worn brake pads, faulty master or wheel cylinders, wheel uniformity problems, or brake lines mixed up on hydraulic unit.
What special tool is required to turn the retainer springs 90 degrees when working on parking brake shoes?
Special Tool 34 4 000 is required to turn the retainer springs 90 degrees and disconnect them.
What procedure is referenced for removing and installing parking brake lever?
The procedure references section 34 41 000 for removing and installing the parking brake lever.
How should the brake shoes be spread apart when removing them?
Spread brake shoes apart at bottom and lift off from above.
What are the three phases for breaking in parking brake shoes after replacement?
Phase 1: 5 full stop braking actions from 50 km/h (30 mph). Phase 2: Let brakes cool down. Phase 3: 5 additional braking actions from 50 km/h (30 mph).
What lubricant should be applied to sliding surfaces and pins during installation?
Give sliding surfaces and pins a thin coat of Molykote G paste.
What part number is referenced for the parking brake cable procedure?
Part number 34 41 100 is referenced for removing and installing parking brake cable for rear disc brakes.
How should the parking brake cable be removed from the swinging arm?
Disconnect parking brake cable on swinging arm and pull parking brake cable out of protective tube.
What components are labeled as A, B, and C in the spreader diagram?
In the spreader diagram, A shows the pin area, B indicates a pin to be pressed out, and C shows another part of the spreader mechanism.
What should be done with the return spring during installation?
Check return spring, replacing it if necessary during installation.
What is the proper installation position for the cable holder?
During installation, the cable holder must rest on protective tube.
What adjustment procedure is mentioned after installing parking brake components?
Adjust parking brake 34 10 014 is referenced after installation procedures.
What should be done to remove the spreader components?
Pull off part A toward rear, press out pin B, and pull out part C.
What brake service procedure is covered in section 34 31 000?
Removing and installing brake master cylinder.
What is the first step when removing the brake master cylinder?
Draw off brake fluid in tank with a syringe used exclusively with brake fluids.
Which brake lines need to be disconnected during removal?
Brake lines 2 and 3 need to be disconnected.
What bolts must be unscrewed to remove the tank?
Mounting bolts 4 and 5 must be unscrewed to pull off the tank.
What should be checked during installation of the rubber ring?
Check rubber ring (7). If sealing is not perfect, the building up of vacuum will be impaired.
What bleeding procedure reference is given for installation?
Bleed brakes 34 00 046.
How does the tandem brake master cylinder operate when the brake pedal is pressed?
Operating the brake pedal will move pistons 1 and 4 forward. Primary cups 2 and 5 slide over compensation bores 3 and 6, creating equal pressure in chambers A and B.
What happens if a brake circuit fails in the dual circuit system?

If a brake circuit fails, the brake pedal travel will increase considerably. If the second brake circuit fails, the pressure building up in chamber A will act on piston 1 to move piston 4 in the pressureless chamber B against the tandem brake master cylinder housing and restore function of the first brake circuit.
What components are served by Chamber A and Chamber B in the dual circuit system?
Chamber A serves right and left front. Chamber B serves right and left rear.
What should be checked on the rubber seal and connections during installation?
Check rubber seal and connections.
What happens if the first circuit fails according to the description?
If the first circuit fails, piston 1 will be pressed against spring cap 7 in pressureless chamber A and the second brake circuit will function normally via chamber B.
What seats need to be removed according to the instructions?
Remove both front seats 52 10 000 and remove rear seat cushion 52 20 010.
What should be disconnected along with the seat removal?
Disconnect both plugs for the rear pulse sensors.
How should the carpets and trim panels be handled during disassembly?
Detach carpets and trim panels as required, then lay back left and right wires toward front.
Where is the instrument panel trim removed from?
Remove instrument panel trim at bottom left.
What is the proper sequence for disconnecting the multiple pin plug on the control unit?
First engage left side of plug and then press right side into clamp.
How do you remove the indicator lamp from the instrument cluster?
Pull indicator lamp with bulb holder out of instrument cluster.
What needs to be done with the fuse box?
Remove fuse box and push wire harness into passenger compartment.
What ground connection needs to be disconnected on the body?
Disconnect ground lead on body.
Which numbered plugs need to be pulled off?
Pull off plugs (1 and 2).
What electronic component needs to be removed that is numbered 3?
Pull off electronic relay (3).
What diagram reference numbers are shown for the seat removal step?
Diagram reference number 30 34 105 is shown for the seat removal step.
What diagram reference number corresponds to the fuse box removal?
Diagram reference number 30 34 110 corresponds to the fuse box removal step.
What is the component number for the ABS lamp?
The ABS lamp is component number 371.
What does component 360 represent in the ABS wiring diagram?
Component 360 is the Electronic control unit.
What are the component numbers for the signal sensors at the front wheels?
The front wheel signal sensors are components 362 (front left) and 364 (front right).
What does KL61 terminal represent in this ABS system?
KL61 terminal represents the battery charge control.
What is the function of component 361?
Component 361 is the Hydraulic control unit.
What does component 370 represent?
Component 370 is the Electronic relay.
What is the function of the BS switch according to the legend?
The BS switch is the Brake light switch.
What connector numbers are shown for the signal sensor connections?
The signal sensor connections are numbered 363, 365, 367, and 369.
What is the procedure number for replacing the brake booster?
The procedure number for replacing the brake booster is 34 33 000.
What should be checked between the tandem brake master cylinder and brake booster during installation?
Check rubber ring (7) between tandem brake master cylinder and brake booster, and replace if necessary.
How do you replace the check valve for the brake booster?
Detach vacuum hose on check valve (1), then for installation replace clamp if necessary.
What component is indicated by callout number 7 in the brake booster replacement procedure?
Callout number 7 indicates the rubber ring between the tandem brake master cylinder and brake booster.
How do you disconnect the vacuum hose on the brake booster?
Disconnect vacuum hose on brake booster, and for installation replace clamp if necessary.
What should you do with the clamp when installing the vacuum hose on the check valve?
Replace clamp if necessary during installation.
How should the check valve be positioned during installation?
Arrow or black side faces intake manifold, and replace clamp if necessary.
What component is indicated by callout number 1 in the check valve replacement procedure?
Callout number 1 indicates the check valve for the brake booster.
Where can you find the tightening torque specification for the brake booster installation?
The tightening torque specification is referenced with an asterisk and notes 'See Specifications' at the bottom of the page.
What is required when loosening clamps to remove the check valve?
Loosen clamps and take off check valve, then for installation ensure arrow or black side faces intake manifold and replace clamp if necessary.
What test step covers the dynamic speed sensor test?
Test Step 03 covers the Dynamic speed sensor test for speed sensors (DF).
Which speed sensors are tested in the dynamic speed sensor test?
The front left, front right, rear left, and rear right speed sensors are tested.
What should I check if the cycle time is less than the specified value?
If cycle time is less than specified value, the wheel turns too fast. Check for excessive clearance between speed sensor and pulse wheel, and verify the speed sensor is not loose or dirty.
What does it mean when the cycle time is greater than the specified value?
When cycle time is greater than specified value, it means the wheel turns too slow.
What visual inspection should be performed on the speed sensor?
Check for excessive clearance between speed sensor and pulse wheel, verify the speed sensor is not loose or dirty, and check the installation.
What are the job position numbers for replacing the speed sensor?
The job position numbers are 61 12 510 and 61 12 520 for speed sensor replacement.
What should I do if wheel rotation is not uniform enough?
Check pulse wheel teeth for condition and dirt, check clearance between speed sensor and pulse wheel, and replace the pulse wheel if necessary.
How do I check the wheel arrangement with a gage?
Check arrangement of wheel with gage and hold the opposite wheel on rear axle during the check.
What job position covers pulse wheel replacement?
Job position 61 12 510 / 520 covers pulse wheel replacement.
What group does this dynamic speed sensor test belong to?
This dynamic speed sensor test belongs to Group 34.
What is the procedure section number for removing and installing the brake force regulator?
The procedure section number is 34 34 100.
What type of syringe should be used when drawing off brake fluid from the tank?
A syringe used exclusively with brake fluids should be used.
Which brake lines need to be disconnected during brake force regulator removal?
Lines 1 and 2 need to be disconnected.
What must be done after installing the brake force regulator?
The system must be bled according to procedure 34 00 046.
