What components are visible in the top diagram showing the brake force regulator removal?
The diagram shows the brake force regulator with numbered callouts 1 and 2 indicating the brake lines that need to be disconnected.
What should be removed along with the brake force regulator?
Remove the clamp and brake force regulator.
What codes should be checked when replacing a brake force regulator?
Check the calendar day/year number, reduction (e.g. 0.45), and switching over pressure codes.
What do the numbered callouts 1, 2, and 3 represent in the brake force regulator diagram?
Callout 1 indicates the calendar day/year number, callout 2 shows the reduction value (e.g. 0.45), and callout 3 indicates the switching over pressure.
What is an example of the reduction value that might be found on a brake force regulator?
An example reduction value is 0.45.
Where can the tightening torque specification be found for this procedure?
The tightening torque specification is referenced to the Specifications section, as indicated by the asterisk and note at the bottom of the page.
What diagram reference number is shown for the brake force regulator removal procedure?
The diagram reference number is 30 34 081.
What is the diagram reference number for the brake force regulator code checking illustration?
The diagram reference number is 30 34 083.
What special tool is required for adjusting the acceleration pick-up for ABS?
Special Tool 34 5 150 is required for adjusting the acceleration pick-up.
What are the requirements for the car position when adjusting the acceleration pick-up?
The car must be parked on level ground (workshop floor), including trunk empty, fuel tank full (or equal weight in trunk), and tire inflation pressure correct.
What is the normal value for ohmmeter resistance when testing the acceleration pick-up?
The normal value is less than 1 k ohm.
What should be done if the measured actual value is smaller than the nominal value?
Install the shim on mounting point (1).
What is the tightening torque specification for the shear-off screws?
The tightening torque is 6 to 8 Nm (4.5 to 5.5 ft.lbs.).
What is the nominal distance 'A' value in the table?
The nominal distance 'A' value is 26.5 mm.
What is the permissible switching tolerance of acceleration pick-up in the car?
The permissible switching tolerance is 33.0 mm.
What are the actual value measurements provided in the example?
The actual value is 35.6 mm (1.401''), maximum value is 33.0 mm (1.299''), and minimum shim thickness is 2.6 mm (0.102'').
What is the alternative actual value measurement given?
The alternative actual value is 35.6 mm (1.401''), minimum value is 26.5 mm (1.043''), and maximum shim thickness is 9.1 mm (0.358'').
How many wedges and shims can be used maximum on one mounting bolt?
A maximum of one wedge and three shims (= 1 mm / 0.039'') may be used on one mounting bolt to correct the switching point of the acceleration pick-up in the car.
What is the part number and thickness range of the wedge?
The wedge, Part No. 34 51 1 156 827, is equal to 4.9 to 5.3 mm (0.193 to 0.209'').
What section number covers the procedure for checking brake discs for runout and difference in thickness?
Section 34 21 530 covers rear brake discs - remove and install, and section 879 covers rear brake discs - check runout and difference in thickness.
Which section would I reference for bleeding the ABS brakes?
Section 34 00 047 covers Brakes - bleed (ABS).
What is the section number for removing and installing the brake booster?
Section 34 33 000 covers Brake booster and tandem brake master cylinder - remove and install, and section 34 33 000 covers Brake booster - replace.
Where can I find information about adjusting the parking brake?
Section 34 10 010 covers Parking brake - adjust.
What section covers the procedure for replacing brake pipes?
Section 34 32 361 covers Brake pipes - replace.
Which section would I use for checking high and low pressure brake tests?
Section 34 00 519 covers Brakes - check (high and low pressure tests).
What important safety precaution must be followed before removing or installing the ABS control unit?
Always turn off ignition before removing or installing control unit.
What are the two numbered components shown in the second diagram for replacing the ABS control unit?
Component 1 is the clamp that needs to be pushed back, and component 2 is the multiple pin plug that needs to be pulled out to the right.
How do you disconnect the multiple pin plug from the ABS control unit?
Push back clamp (1) and pull out multiple pin plug (2) to the right, and then disengage it to the left.
What should you check for correct connection when replacing the ABS control unit?
The multiple pin plug has a tab on the left side, for which the control unit must have an opening.
What is the correct installation sequence for the ABS control unit plug?
First engage left side of plug and then press right side into clamp.
What components are numbered 7 and 8 in the hydraulic unit removal diagram?
Component 7 is the cover that needs to be unscrewed, and component 8 is one of the bolts that needs to be unscrewed.
What precaution should be taken when pulling off the multiple pin plug on the hydraulic unit?
Pull off multiple pin plug on hydraulic unit carefully (plastic pins) and loosen wire straps.
What must be done with the battery connections when replacing the ABS wire harness?
Disconnect battery ground lead, disconnect lead on battery positive terminal and lay back to left side in engine compartment, and disconnect battery ground lead in the trunk.
Where should the positive terminal cable be disconnected in the engine compartment?
Disconnect cable on positive terminal, in engine compartment on rear panel.
What should be done with the headlight covers during ABS wire harness replacement?
Remove left and right headlight covers and disconnect both plugs for pulse sensors in engine compartment.
What is the final step shown for the wire harness routing?
Pull out right wire to left side of engine compartment.
What critical requirement is emphasized about using the correct ABS control unit?
Only use a control unit with the correct code number, and this information can be found in the Specifications section.
What torque specification is required for the stop screw when installing it?
The stop screw (18) should be tightened with a torque of 5 to 8 Nm (3.7 to 5.9 ft. lbs.).
What type of ring should be used when installing the stop screw?
A new aluminum ring (16) should be used when screwing in the stop screw (18).
What lubricant should be applied to the secondary cup during installation?
The secondary cup (12) should be coated with silicone grease before installation.
What components are identified by callout numbers 10, 11, and 12 in the brake assembly diagram?
Number 10 is the push rod piston, number 11 is the stop washer, and number 12 is the secondary cup.
How should the push rod piston be handled when it comes back?
Let the push rod piston (10) come back carefully and push on the stop washer (11).
What special requirement must be met for the circlip installation?
The circlip must have perfect seat in groove of cylinder bore, and a new seal (15) should be installed before mounting on the brake booster.
What is the proper technique for installing the assembly sleeve over the secondary cup?
Let the short stepped section of assembly sleeve protrude and slide it over secondary cup (12), while holding the cup with two fingers.
What should be done to the plastic bushing before installation on the push rod piston?
Give the plastic bushing (13) a light coat of silicone grease and push it on push rod piston in cylinder bore.
What is the adjustment specification for the brake light switch contact distance?
The contact button will be visible by distance A = 5 to 6 mm (0.197 to 0.236 inches) when the brake pedal is released.
How should the long sleeve pipe be inserted during assembly?
Push in the long sleeve pipe carefully up to point of resistance when adjusting secondary cup flush with long sleeve pipe.
What components need to be removed when pulling back the short sleeve section?
Hold the long sleeve pipe and pull back the short sleeve section, then remove the complete assembly sleeve.
What hardware is used to adjust the brake light switch?
The brake light switch is adjusted with nut (1) and lock nut (2) that work with the brake pedal released.
What is the procedure number for replacing the relay on the hydraulic unit for ABS?
The procedure number is 61 31 570.
What is the first step when replacing the relay on the hydraulic unit for ABS?
Unscrew screw (1) and pull off cover.
What two types of relays can be pulled out according to the procedure?
You can pull out motor relay (2) or valve relay (3).
What are the callout numbers 2 and 3 identifying in the relay compartment?
Callout number 2 identifies the motor relay and callout number 3 identifies the valve relay.
What is the procedure number for replacing the indicator lamp for ABS?
The procedure number is 62 99 080.
What is the first step when replacing the ABS indicator lamp?
Remove instrument panel trim at bottom left.
What component needs to be removed before accessing the ABS indicator lamp?
The instrument panel trim at bottom left needs to be removed first.
What component is being accessed when the cover is pulled off in the ABS relay replacement procedure?
The relay compartment containing the motor relay and valve relay is being accessed.
What procedure numbers are shown for removing and installing rear brake pads and calipers?
Procedure 34 21 200 covers removing and installing rear brake pads, while procedure 34 21 745 covers removing and installing the rear brake caliper.
What is the first step when removing rear brake pads?
Remove rear wheels and press off plastic caps (1).
What should you pull off on the right side after removing the plastic caps?
Pull off brake pad wear indicator plug.
How many guide bolts need to be unscrewed when removing brake pads?
Two guide bolts (2) need to be unscrewed.
What should be checked during installation of the guide bolts?
Check condition of guide bolts and threads, replacing guide bolts if necessary, and apply proper tightening torque.
What is step 3 in the brake pad removal process?
Press out clip (3) and pull off caliper toward rear.
Where is the inner brake pad located?
The inner brake pad is located in piston (4) with a spring.
What must be done during installation after removing the brake pads?
Push back pistons completely.
What tool is specified for drawing off brake fluid during caliper removal?
Draw off brake fluid with a syringe which is used exclusively with brake fluids.
What brake system maintenance is required after caliper installation?
Bleed brakes - see procedure 34 00 046/047.
What important warning is given about the brake pad wear indicator wire?
Check routing and securing of wire for brake pad wear indicator, check for secure holding with tab of dust cap, and avoid rubbing of wire on wheel rim which must always be avoided.
What should be done on the right side when unscrewing bolts during caliper removal?
Pull off brake pad wear indicator plug and pull off caliper toward rear.
What is the title of this brake system diagram?
BRAKE LINE ROUTING LAYOUT - E 30
How many brake disc assemblies are shown in this routing diagram?
Four brake disc assemblies are shown - one at each wheel position.
What type of lines are used to show the brake line connections in this diagram?
Dashed lines are used to show the brake line routing connections between components.
Where is the main brake component (master cylinder/ABS unit) positioned in this layout?
The main brake component is positioned centrally in the diagram, with brake lines routing out to all four wheels.
What additional component is shown with dotted lines connected to the left front brake assembly?
There appears to be an additional brake component connected with dotted lines to the left front brake assembly, likely representing a brake sensor or ABS component.
How are the brake lines routed from the central component to the wheels?
The brake lines route from the central component outward to each of the four wheel positions using dashed lines to indicate the connection paths.
What do the circular components at each corner of the diagram represent?
The circular components at each corner represent the brake disc and caliper assemblies at each wheel position.
What are the possible causes of seized pistons in the brake caliper?
The possible causes are: a) Caliper recesses dirty, caps damaged, b) Brake disc not aligned with caliper, c) Corrosion of pistons in calipers or wheel cylinders.
How do you correct seized pistons in the brake caliper?
Remove and install, repair or replace calipers. Check caliper installation. Remove and install, repair or replace calipers or wheel cylinders.
What causes a pulsating effect on the brake pedal?
The causes are: a) Wheel bearing play excessive, b) Brake disc not aligned with caliper, c) Brake disc runout, d) Excessive thickness difference within braking surface.
What should I check if there's excessive wheel bearing play causing brake pedal pulsation?
Replace wheel bearings.
How do I fix brake disc runout that's causing pedal pulsation?
Check brake discs for runout, replacing if necessary.
What are the potential causes of insufficient parking brake effect?

The causes are: a) Parking brake shoes splattered with oil, b) Excessive dead travel between brake shoes and brake drums, c) Excessive dead travel in cables, d) Cables maladjusted, e) Corroded transmitting elements.
How do you correct oil-splattered parking brake shoes?
Replace brake liners and eliminate cause.
What's the correction for excessive dead travel between brake shoes and drums?
Adjust parking brake.
How do I address corroded transmitting elements in the parking brake system?
Remove and install parking brake and spreader locks; check cables, replacing if necessary.
What should I do about excessive thickness difference within the braking surface?
Measure brake disc thickness and grind or replace discs.
What causes brake pedal travel to be excessive even though brakes have been bled and adjusted?
This can be caused by a damaged primary cup in the master cylinder, separating cups on floating piston or tandem brake master cylinder leak, or a leak in the brake system.
How do I fix excessive brake pedal travel after bleeding and adjustment?
Overhaul or replace the brake master cylinder, or check the brake system for leaks depending on the specific cause identified.
What causes uneven brake pad wear?
Uneven pad wear can be caused by wrong type of brake pads, dirty or damaged caliper recesses/caps, corrosion in calipers or wheel cylinders, or swollen rubber rings for piston control.
What's the correction for uneven brake pad wear?
Replace brake pads with correct type, remove and install/repair or replace calipers or wheel cylinders as needed.
What causes brake pads to wear at an angle?

Angled brake pad wear can be caused by excessive wheel bearing play, brake disc not aligned with caliper, corrosion in calipers or wheel cylinders, angular brake disc wear, pads worn less than minimum thickness, insufficient spring force, or damaged guide bolts.
How do I correct brake pads that are wearing at an angle?

Replace wheel bearings, check caliper installation, remove and install/repair or replace calipers or wheel cylinders, grind or replace brake discs, replace brake pads, replace springs, or replace guide bolts depending on the specific cause.
What are the possible causes if brake fluid is overheated?
According to the troubleshooting chart, overheated brake fluid can be due to vapor lock from excessive water content in brake fluid or excessive brake loads.
What should I check if the brake disc is not aligned with the caliper?
Check caliper installation and ensure proper alignment between the brake disc and caliper assembly.
What components might need replacement if there's corrosion in the brake system?
If there's corrosion in calipers or wheel cylinders, you may need to remove and install, repair, or replace the calipers or wheel cylinders.
How do you remove the acceleration pick-up plug?
Pull off plug (1). Remove shear-off screws (only drilling out is approved).
What adjustment is required during installation of the acceleration pick-up?
Adjust acceleration pick-up.
What test lead should be connected when checking the acceleration pick-up for ABS?
Connect Jetronic test lead 61 1 440 on acceleration pick-up.
What ohmmeter model is specified for testing the acceleration pick-up?
Connect ohmmeter (M 06) of BMW service tester.
What is the nominal resistance value for the acceleration pick-up switch?
Less than 1 k-ohm.
What connections should be measured when checking the switch with wire and plug?
Measure resistance between connections (1 and 16).
What is the nominal resistance value when measuring between connections 1 and 16?
Less than 1 k-ohm.
What must be turned off while measuring resistance?
Ignition must be turned off while measuring.
What callout number indicates the acceleration pick-up plug in both procedures?
Callout number 1 indicates the acceleration pick-up plug in both the removal/installation and checking procedures.
What universal adapter is mentioned for connecting to the ABS control unit wire harness?
Connect universal adapter on wire harness from ABS control unit, with a source reference to HWB.
What should I check first when troubleshooting ABS speed sensors?
Turn off ignition for single tests, control unit not connected. Check the front left plug connection with a visual inspection.
What resistance reading indicates a faulty speed sensor?
If the DF reading is greater than 999 k-ohms, then the DF reading is lower and there's a fault in the wire harness. Normal readings should be less than 1 ohm.
Which wires should I check for the front left speed sensor?
Check flow in wires 4 and 6 (325iX): bridge front left plug on wire harness side. DF reading should then be less than 1 ohm.
What are the job position codes for front speed sensor testing?
Front left speed sensor testing is referenced as job position 61 11 530 and 61 12 510.
How do I test the rear right speed sensor wiring?
Check flow in wires 24 and 26: bridge rear right plug on wire harness side. DF reading should then be less than 1 ohm; if higher, there's a fault in wire harness.
What should I do if speed sensor resistance to ground reading remains less than 999 k-ohms?
If reading remains less than 999 k-ohms, there is a fault in wire harness. Also refer to test step 03 when testing speed sensors.
What connections should I bridge on the electronic relay plug for speed sensor testing?
Bridge connections 30a and 86 on electronic relay plug when testing speed sensors.
What does a safety lamp reading greater than 80 ohms indicate?
Reading greater than 80 ohms indicates ABS indicator lamp faulty or poor contact. Check or replace lamp and check connections on lamp and terminal 15.
What should I check if the safety lamp reading is less than 10 ohms?
If reading is less than 10 ohms, check wires 1 and 29 for ground out.
What's the job position code for safety lamp testing?
Safety lamp testing is referenced as job position 62 99 080.
What is the boiling point range for brake fluid from drum brake to disc brake applications?
The boiling point ranges from +240°C (464°F) to +160°C to 180°C (320°F to 356°F).
What is the maximum charging pressure allowed when bleeding brakes?
Charging pressure must not exceed 2 bar (28 psi).
What should you do to prevent paint damage when bleeding brakes?
Keep brake fluid off of painted car parts as the paint finish would be damaged.
What is the proper procedure for bleeding front wheel brakes?
Connect bleeder hose with bottle on bleeder screw, unscrew bleeder screw, and tighten bleeder screw when escaping brake fluid is without air bubbles.
How many times should you operate the brake pedal when bleeding brakes with ABS?
Release brake pedal and operate 12 times against stop.
What additional step is required when bleeding brakes with ABS that differs from standard brake bleeding?
Do not use air flushing and press and hold brake pedal down.
What is the bleeding sequence for rear wheel brakes on disc brake systems?
Begin at rear right, then repeat bleeding on rear left, front right and front left.
Why does brake fluid take on moisture and what effect does this have?
Brake fluid is hygroscopic and consequently takes on moisture in the air through the vent hole in brake fluid tank, which affects the boiling point.
What should be done with bleeder valves after completing the bleeding procedure?
Hold brake pedal in down position, shut bleeder valves, then release brake pedal.
What component is shown with callout number 30 34 028 in the bleeding brake procedure?
The image shows the bleeder screw connection point on the brake caliper.
What is the first step in removing and installing brake shoes of the rear wheel?
Remove rear wheel and unscrew bolt.
How do you remove the brake drum according to the procedure shown?
Remove brake drum by loosening parking brake cables and unscrewing automatic slack control enough that brake drum can be pulled off.
What angle should you turn the return springs when pushing them in?
Push in return springs and turn 90°.
What components should be disconnected at the front when removing brake shoes?
Disconnect bottom return spring at front, pull brake shoes out of wheel brake cylinder, disconnect top return spring at front, and remove front brake shoes with automatic slack control.
What important installation requirement is specified for brake shoe replacement?
Always replace all four brake shoes and use same make. Also replace return springs and thermo clip when replacing brake shoes.
What should you do with the parking brake cable during this procedure?
Disconnect parking brake cable and remove rear brake shoes.
What are the thread specifications for the automatic slack control adjusting pinion?
Adjusting pinion on left side has right-hand threads (R) and left-hand threads (L) on right side.
What must engage properly in the thermo clip arrangement?
Thermo clip must engage (arrow). Note bends of return springs.
What maintenance should be performed on the adjusting pinion?
Unscrew adjusting pinion, check function and movement of automatic slack control. If applicable, clean and give threads of push rod a light coat of grease.
What reference is provided for additional brake shoe installation information?
Replace brake shoes by reversing. See Service Information of Group 34.
What components are visible in the brake drum assembly diagram?
The diagram shows the brake drum with brake shoes, return springs, wheel brake cylinder, and automatic slack control mechanism.
What section number covers the removing and installing of brake shoes procedure?
Section 34 21 530 covers removing and installing brake shoes of rear wheel.
What safety precaution must be taken before pulling off a plug and measuring resistance in the dynamic voltage test?
Turn off ignition before pulling off a plug and measuring resistance.
What should be checked for voltage drop in the dynamic voltage test between wires 1 and 10?
Battery connection (+ and -), term. 15 and from ignition lock to electronic relay connection, from relay to control unit wire 1.
What three steps should be taken when the valve relay home contact voltage drop test fails?

1. Replace valve relay. 2. Ground connection has excessive transition resistance or break. 3. Check flow in following wires: wire 8 from ground to hydraulic unit plug, from hydraulic unit wire 8 to wire 87a, flow from wire 4 to valve relay term. 30, from wire 4 to multiple pin plug (control unit) wire 32.
What should be checked when the motor relay operating contact voltage drop test fails?

1. Replace motor relay. 2. Check ground terminals of pump motor for tight fit and transmission resistance. 3. Check flow in following wires: from term. B + to plug hydraulic unit wire 12, from multiple pin plug (control unit) wire 14 to hydraulic unit plug, from wire 9 in hydraulic unit to motor relay term. 30 and positive terminal on pump motor. 4. Pump motor faulty: replace hydraulic unit.
What wire should be checked from the multiple pin plug to the hydraulic unit plug for the safety circuit lamp diode test?
Wire 29 from multiple pin plug (control unit) to hydraulic unit plug for break and voltage drop.
What should be done if there is a diode test between wires 7 and 4 (M 09) on 1988 models?
Replace hydraulic unit. Diode now in valve relay since 1988 models / replace valve relay. Measure on valve relay between pins 30 and L1.
What is the remedy for excessive voltage drop or break in wires?
Replace wire harness.
What is the first step when removing the rear brake disc?
Remove and install rear wheel. Unscrew bolts (1).
How should the caliper be positioned after pulling it toward the rear?
Pull off caliper toward rear and suspend with a piece of wire. Brake line remains connected.
What is the important rule about replacing brake discs on an axle?
Always replace both brake discs of one axle, even if only one disc has to be replaced.
What parking brake adjustment procedure should be followed after replacing brake discs?
Adjust parking brake 34 10 014.
How many phases are there in the breaking in procedure for parking brake after replacing brake discs?
The car must be broken in in 3 phases.
What is the speed and number of braking actions required in Phase 1 of the brake break-in procedure?
Phase 1: 5 full stop braking actions from 50 km/h (30 mph).
What should be done between Phase 1 and Phase 3 of the brake break-in procedure?
Phase 2: Let brakes cool down.
How many points should be measured when checking brake disc thickness difference?
Measure difference in thickness within braking surface at about 8 points with a micrometer.
What tool is specified for measuring brake disc runout and thickness difference?
Mount dial gauge holder and check lateral runout of brake disc with dial gauge for runout, and use a micrometer for thickness difference.
What should be installed after machining brake discs to minimum thickness?
After machining to minimum thickness, install only one more set of brake pads.
What cross-reference is provided for brake disc replacement procedures?
Always replace both brake discs of one axle, even if only one brake disc has to be replaced. See also SI Group 34.
What could cause the brakes to pull to one side?

The causes include tire inflation pressure incorrect, uneven tire tread wear, oil on pads/liners, pad/liner type not as specified, caliper recesses dirty, guide bolts dirty or damaged, rear wheel alignment maladjusted, corrosion in calipers or wheel cylinders, shock absorbers without action, pad of one caliper worn, or pad glazed.
How do I correct brakes that are pulling to one side due to dirty calipers?
Remove, clean and install calipers.
What are the symptoms of brakes getting excessively hot while driving?
The brakes become excessively hot during normal driving conditions.
What should I check if the compensation bore in master cylinder is clogged?
Check or replace master cylinder.
What causes insufficient braking effect despite great force on the pedal with normal brake pedal travel?
The cause is brake pads oil splattered or burnt; wrong type of brake pads.
How do I fix brake booster malfunctions when engine vacuum is insufficient?
Check power brake system - check engine (valves, cylinder head, gasket, etc.).
What could cause the parking brake lever not to release fully?
This can be caused by a cross spring broken or the parking brake lever mechanism being faulty.
What's the correction for glazed brake pads?
Replace brake pads and check calipers.
What causes short brake pedal travel with insufficient braking effect?
The cause is brake booster malfunctions with engine vacuum insufficient.
How do I fix a brake system with one brake circuit failed due to leaks or damage?
Check brake system for leaks.
What is being tested in test step 06?
Control unit/simulation - front wheels, specifically testing voltage between wires 1 and 10 for left and right pressure solenoids during build-up, drop, and hold phases.
What should I do if the solenoid pressure build-up, drop, or hold phases fail during testing?
Turn on ignition, run engine, and ensure battery is charged. Due to high switching on power, possibly repeat test with engine running. Replace control unit and repeat test step.
What are the job position codes for replacing the control unit and hydraulic unit?
Control unit replacement is job position 34 52 510, and hydraulic unit replacement is job position 34 51 520.
What additional troubleshooting step should I take if valves in test steps 08, 09 and 10 do not switch or pump does not run?
Replace the hydraulic unit (job position 34 51 520).
Why might the pressure building-up and pressure holding phases only be checkable on 325 iX cars?

Only the pressure building-up and pressure holding phases (2 A) can be checked in 325 iX cars because of the changed activation times in the control unit. Irregular values will be displayed on adapter B in switch position (5 A).
When might it be necessary to repeat this test step?
It might be necessary to repeat this test step to reach the nominal values due to the high switching-on power and short switching phase.
What section of the manual am I looking at?
This is page 34-40 from Group 34 (Brakes section) of the service manual.
What preliminary steps are required before testing the solenoid voltages?
Turn on ignition, run engine, and ensure battery is charged (check).
What is the recommended approach when high switching power might affect test results?
Due to high switching on power, possibly repeat test with engine running, and replace control unit and repeat test step if needed.
Which specific wires are being tested for voltage in this control unit simulation test?
Voltage between wires 1 and 10 is being tested for both left and right pressure solenoids.
How many mercury switches are in the acceleration pick-up for the BMW 325 iX?
There are two mercury switches, one each for forward and reverse drive, which are installed in longitudinal direction of car at an angle to the horizontal.
What resistance value indicates closed contact in the horizontal position for the mercury switches?
The series connected mercury switches provide closed contact in horizontal position with resistance less than 1 k-ohm.
What resistance value will cause the contact to open when the car experiences negative acceleration?
Negative acceleration (braking) of the car or inclination of the acceleration transmitter will displace the mercury filling and cause the contact to open with resistance greater than 2.5 M-ohms.
What percentage of braking deceleration is necessary to open the contact?
Braking deceleration of 35 to 45% is necessary to open the contact because the glass tube is inclined in such a manner.
How can the braking deceleration value for forward drive be simulated?

The braking deceleration value for forward drive can be simulated by inclining the acceleration pick-up from 19.5 to 24° (with Special Tool 34 5 150 this is equal to 26.5 to 33.0 mm (1.043 to 1.299")).
Does the switching point for reverse drive require adjustment?
No, the switching point for reverse drive does not have to be adjusted.
What makes the BMW 325 iX unique in terms of drive system features?
BMW 325 iX (all wheel drive) is the first standard production car to have permanent all wheel drive with constantly switched central and rear axle locks and also a continuously effective ABS.
What is the primary duty of the acceleration pick-up in the BMW 325 iX?

The acceleration pick-up performs the duty of providing information on road condition (higher or lower traction) so that all three systems can be effective simultaneously in the BMW 325 iX (all wheel drive).
How does the ABS control unit use the acceleration pick-up information?
The ABS control unit will decide between various data fields depending on the switch condition (open or closed mercury switches), and consequently consider the traction condition of a street or road.
What happens when an open switch condition is detected for longer than 20 seconds?

If an open switch condition (resistance greater than 2.5 M-ohms) is reported to the ABS control unit over a period of time longer than 20 seconds, the ABS switches off and reports this to the driver with a warning lamp in the instrument cluster.
What tool is mentioned for simulating the braking deceleration value?
Special Tool 34 5 150 is mentioned for simulating the braking deceleration value, which corresponds to inclining the acceleration pick-up from 19.5 to 24°.
What systems need to work simultaneously in the BMW 325 iX according to this page?

All three systems - permanent all wheel drive with constantly switched central and rear axle locks and continuously effective ABS - need to be effective simultaneously, requiring a sensor to provide road condition information.
What are the initial steps to perform when testing the hydraulic unit pressure drop?
Turn on ignition, run engine, and check that battery is charged.
What should you do if high switching on power is detected during the test?
Due to high switching on power, possibly repeat test step with engine running. Refer to test steps 05, 06 and 07.
What is the recommended action if nominal values are not reached in this test?
Replace hydraulic unit.
Which cars have a restriction for this test step regarding dynamometer testing?
325 iX cars - this test step may not be performed on a dynamometer for 325 iX cars.
What is the maximum loading time restriction for the central lock in the transfer box?
The total loading time for the central lock in the transfer box must not exceed 60 seconds at a wheel speed of max. 7.5 km/h (4.5 mph).
What brake system component is being overhauled in procedure 34 31 012?
The brake master cylinder is being overhauled.
Are replacement parts available for brake master cylinders with a recessed stop pin?
No, replacement parts are not available for brake master cylinders with a recessed stop pin (ABS).
What should be applied to the cylinder bore before reassembly?
Give the cylinder bore a very thin coat of ATE brake cylinder paste.
How should the intermediate piston be removed from the cylinder housing?
Knock out the intermediate piston by knocking the housing on a piece of wood lightly.
What cleaning method is recommended for the cylinder housing and other parts?
Clean the cylinder housing and other parts not contained in the repair kit with alcohol and dry with compressed air.
What components are included in the repair kit according to the Important note?

The repair kit includes: spring (1), support (2), primary cup (3), fill-in washer (4), intermediate piston (5), separating cup (6), long sleeve (7), spring (8), screw (9), push rod piston (10), stop washer (11), secondary cup (12), plastic bushing (13), circlip (14), seal (15), aluminum seal (16), and silicone grease (17).
How should the push rod piston be removed?
Apply light pressure on push rod piston (10), lift out circlip (14) and unscrew stop screw (18). Release push rod piston (10) slowly and pull out.
What tool is recommended for clamping the cylinder housing during assembly?
Clamp the cylinder housing in a vise fitted with aluminum jaws.
What should be done with the stepped short sleeve pipe during installation?
Push the stepped short sleeve pipe into the cylinder bore against the shoulder and hold.
How should the assembly sleeve contents be installed?
Push contents of assembly sleeve into cylinder bore carefully with a suitable mandrel until the intermediate piston touches the bottom of the cylinder.
What inspection should be performed on tandem brake master cylinders with surface damage?
Tandem brake master cylinders with surface damage in the cylinder bore may not be reused. Check whether all connecting, compensating and feeding bores are clean.
What components can be removed from the assembly sleeve according to the instructions?

The large plugs from assembly sleeve, short sleeve section on long sleeve pipe, stop washer (11), secondary cup (12), plastic bushing (13), circlip (14), aluminum seal (16) and silicone grease (17) can be removed, along with the small plugs.
What system is this wiring diagram for?
This is a wiring diagram for ABS System 2B, which was introduced gradually since 8/87.
What is the power rating of the lamp shown in the diagram?
The lamp has a power rating of 1.2W.
What are the connector numbers for the signal senders on the front axle?
The front axle signal senders use connectors 362 (front left) and 364 (front right).
What does KL61 represent in this diagram?
KL61 is Terminal 61, which is the charge indicator according to the legend.
Which component is labeled as 361 in the wiring diagram?
Component 361 is the Hydraulic control unit.
What special note is provided about the diode in valve relay?
The note states that the diode in valve relay applies to 1988 models.
What does the +BS connection represent in this ABS wiring diagram?
The +BS connection represents the ABS Stop light switch according to the component legend.
Which terminal numbers are shown connected to the hydraulic control unit (361)?
The hydraulic control unit (361) shows terminal connections 30, 85, 86, and 87.
What does callout number 1 identify in this ABS layout drawing?
Callout number 1 identifies the Electronic control unit.
How many pulse sensors are shown in this ABS system layout?
There are multiple pulse sensors shown, all labeled with callout number 3.
Where is the hydraulic unit positioned relative to the electronic control unit?
The hydraulic unit (2) is positioned below and to the left of the electronic control unit (1).
What type of lines connect the pulse sensors to the main ABS components?
Dashed lines connect the pulse sensors to the main ABS components, likely representing electrical connections.
Which wheels have pulse sensors according to this layout drawing?
All four wheels have pulse sensors, as indicated by the callout number 3 at each wheel position.
What are the three main components of the ABS system shown in this diagram?
The three main components are the Electronic control unit (1), Hydraulic unit (2), and Pulse sensors (3).
What could cause brake pads to seize and not move off the brake disc?
Dirty caliper recesses, damaged protective caps, corrosion in calipers, or compensation bore in master cylinder clogged.
How do you correct seized brake pads that won't move off the brake disc?
Remove and install, repair or replace calipers, or overhaul or replace master cylinder.
What are the possible causes of brakes that squeal or rattle?

Wrong type of pads, dirty caliper recesses, spring force insufficient, brake disc not aligned with caliper, brake disc runout, excessive thickness difference within braking surface, brake drums out-of-true, knocking brake drums, dirt and dust in brake drums, liner wear excessive or one-sided, rust edges on brake discs, pad loose, or wheel bearing play excessive.
How do you fix brake squeal caused by wrong type of brake pads?
Replace brake pads.
What correction is needed for excessive brake disc thickness variation?
Measure brake disc thickness; grind or replace discs.
If brake drums are out-of-true, what's the correction?
Grind or replace brake drums.
What should you do if there's air in the brake system causing dead pedal travel?
Bleed brake system.
How do you address brake system leaks that cause excessive pedal travel?
Check brake system for leaks.
What's the fix for automatic brake shoe slack control malfunctions?
Remove and install brake shoes; repair slack control.
What special tool is required when working with brake lines?
Use special bending tool when working with brake lines.
How should brake fluid be drawn off from the tank when replacing brake hoses?
Draw off brake fluid in tank with a syringe used exclusively with brake fluids.
What is the bleeding procedure reference for brakes after hose replacement?
Bleed brakes 34 00 046.
What are the important guidelines for bending brake lines?
Don't damage finish of brake lines; don't bend lines too sharply and don't bend back lines.
Where can brake lines be obtained for replacement?
Brake lines are only available from Parts in straight version and correct length with connecting nipples.
What should be used as a template for bending new brake lines?
Use the removed brake line as a template for bending.
What is the critical safety instruction when installing brake hoses?
Never twist brake hose when installing.
What section contains additional service information for brake work?
Also refer to Service Information of Group 34.
What is specified for tightening torque after brake hose installation?
Tightening torque* (with asterisk indicating to see Specifications).
What type of syringe should be used for brake fluid removal?
A syringe used exclusively with brake fluids.
What is the first step when replacing either front or rear brake hoses?
Disconnect brake hose, then draw off brake fluid in tank with a syringe used exclusively with brake fluids.
What procedure code covers checking the ABS system?
Procedure 34 50 000 covers checking the ABS system.
How is the ABS function checked?
The ABS function is checked with a BMW service test unit. The tester is connected to the wire harness and control unit with a special plug.
What important requirement must be followed when performing each step of the ABS test?
Each started step must be finished completely, without a break.
What does the electronic circuit in the ABS control unit monitor?
An electronic circuit in the control unit monitors ABS constantly.
When should the ABS system be checked according to the manual?
The system has to be checked if the ABS lamp does not go out or does not come on after turning on the ignition or when repairs were made on the ABS.
What is the first step when removing the hydraulic unit assembly for ABS?
Disconnect the battery ground lead and remove the air cleaner according to procedure 13 71 000.
Which brake lines need to be disconnected according to the numbered callouts in the diagram?

Lines 1 and 2 go to the rear brake pressure regulator and rear brake master cylinder, while lines 3, 4, and 5 connect to the left front brake caliper, right front brake caliper, and front brake master cylinder respectively.
What precaution should be taken when handling brake fluid during the procedure?
Catch brake fluid and keep it off of clothes or painted parts.
Does the ABS system require regular servicing?
No, basically the ABS does not require servicing.
What should be checked together with the general brake system when servicing ABS?
Check brake lines to and from the hydraulic unit for correct routing and leaks together with the general brake system.
What is the procedure code for bleeding the brakes after installation?
Bleed brakes according to procedure 34 00 046.
What should be done with the ABS system after installation of the hydraulic unit?
Check ABS with BMW service test unit as referenced in procedure 34 50 000.
What is the minimum vacuum value when checking engine vacuum for the brake booster?
The minimum value is -0.35 bar (-5 psi).
How many times should you operate the brake pedal during the function test with the engine stopped?
Operate the brake pedal 10 times with the engine stopped.
What should you do if the brake pedal does not give during the function test?
Check the valve, vacuum hose and/or rubber ring between tandem brake master cylinder and brake booster, as they could be defective.
What is the basic adjustment distance A on the piston rod?
The basic adjustment distance A on the piston rod is 125 mm (4.921 inches).
Which brake lines correspond to the 1st brake circuit?
Brake lines 2 (front left) and 3 (front right) correspond to the 1st brake circuit.
What vacuum tester specification is mentioned for checking vacuum between brake booster and check valve?
Install vacuum tester 34 3 100 between brake booster and check valve.
At what engine speed should you check vacuum when decelerating from operating temperature?
Check vacuum when decelerating from an engine speed of 3,000 rpm with the engine having operating temperature.
What callout numbers are shown in the brake booster filter diagram?
The diagram shows callout numbers 1, 2, 3, and 4, representing the cap, holder, damper, and filter respectively.
How should the damper and filter slots be positioned during installation?
Turn slots of damper (3) and filter (4) to be offset to each other by 180°.
What should you use to draw off brake fluid from the tank?
Draw off brake fluid in tank with a syringe used exclusively with brake fluids.
What is the minimum vacuum value for specified idle speed and engine with operating temperature?
The minimum value is -0.50 bar (-7 psi).
What should you disconnect when removing the instrument panel trim?
Disconnect the spring, press off clip (3) and pull out pin (4).
What should I do first when troubleshooting the wire harness relays and valves in step 02?
Turn off ignition for single tests, control unit not connected.
What resistance value indicates a break in wire to the valve relay?
A measured value reading greater than 100 ohms indicates a break in wire to valve relay (from ignition switch wire 27, wires in hydraulic unit).
What does a measured value reading less than 50 ohms indicate for the valve relay?
A measured value reading less than 50 ohms indicates a short circuit in wire to valve relay (wires 1 and 27, wires in hydraulic unit).
What resistance threshold indicates a break in wire to the motor relay?
A measured value reading greater than 58 ohms indicates a break in wire to motor relay (from ignition switch wire 28, wires in hydraulic control unit).
What should I check if specifications are not reached on all three valves?
First check wire 32 for breaks or short circuit, then pull off plugs on hydraulic unit.
How do I test the front left valve resistance?

Measure resistance direct on hydraulic unit between wires 1 and 4. If specification not reached, replace hydraulic unit. Check wire 2 from hydraulic unit plug to control unit plug for breaks or short circuit.
What wires should I check for the front right valve resistance test?
Measure resistance direct on hydraulic unit between wires 3 and 4. Check wire 35 from hydraulic unit plug to control unit plug for breaks or short circuit.
Which wires are used to test the rear valve resistance?
Measure resistance direct on hydraulic unit between wires 5 and 4. Check wire 18 from hydraulic unit plug to control unit plug for breaks or short circuit.
What should I do if there's no measured value from the car for the rear right valve?
Repeat test with connected diagnosis plug for 'wrong connection' display (better ground connection with tester).
What job position codes are referenced for valve and motor relay replacement?
Job position codes 61 31 570 and 61 11 530 are referenced for valve and motor relay replacement, and 34 51 520 for hydraulic unit replacement.
When does the ABS indicator lamp come on and when should it go out?
The ABS indicator lamp comes on after turning on the ignition. The indicator lamp should go out when the engine has started, if the ABS is okay.
What tools are needed to diagnose erroneous ABS indicator lamp behavior?
The causes for erroneous indication can be found with the help of a BMW service tester and a brake test dynamometer.
What important requirement must be followed when starting each test step?
Each started test step must be finished completely without a break!
What happens when the control unit detects an electric or electronic defect in ABS?

The control unit will automatically switch to 'normal braking' when there is an electric or electronic defect in ABS. This means the car can still be braked, but without control (the wheels could lock!).
How is a defective ABS system indicated to the driver?
The defective system will be indicated by a continuously burning ABS indicator lamp in the instrument panel.
What special procedure must be followed for BMW 325 iX with Four Driven Wheels before checking ABS?
First measure resistance on acceleration pick-up and power supply wire, see 34 52 000, prior to checking ABS, if ABS lamp comes on while driving.
What should be checked if comfort is impaired during ABS regulation?
Check throttle valve positioner, see 13 54 130, when comfort is impaired, e.g. shaking or stopping of engine during ABS regulation.
Which brake test dynamometer test steps cannot be performed on BMW 325 iX cars?
The ABS test on a brake test dynamometer (test steps 8, 9 and 10) may not be performed on BMW 325 iX cars.
What must be removed from the electronic control unit when welding?
Remove plugs from the electronic control unit and turn off ignition when welding with an electric welder.
What are the maximum temperature limits for the electronic control unit when painting?
When painting, the electronic control unit can be subjected to max. 95° C (203° F) briefly and to max. 85° C (185° F) for a longer period (about 2 hours).
What must be done with battery terminals after battery removal and reinstallation?
If the battery had been removed, the battery terminals must be tightened on the end poles perfectly after reinstallation of the battery.
What comprehensive check must be performed after hydraulic unit replacement?

After replacement of the hydraulic unit, the control unit, the speed sensors and the wire harness as well as after performance of jobs which are in contact with ABS equipment (e.g. repair of accident damage), the entire antiblock system has to be checked with the BMW service tester. It is important that brake lines be routed correctly.
What should you check for when installing the brake pedal position in models with an over-center helper spring?
Check for correct installed position in models with an over-center helper spring. Also refer to the pedal assembly drawing.
What important limitation exists regarding movement in the brake master cylinder?
Movement must be limited in the brake master cylinder and may not be accomplished with, for example, the stop light switch (distance B).
What is the first step shown for removing the master cylinder?
Unscrew master cylinder on pedal base.
What should be done with the bolts during installation?
Tightening torque (see specifications).
Where should the base be unscrewed during the removal process?
Unscrew base on engine compartment wall.
What special procedure applies to stop light switches on 1987 and later models?
Stop Light Switch Since 1987 Models: Adjust - see Group 61. Check function of stop lights.
What type of fastener removal is shown in the middle procedures?
Unscrew bolts, with installation requiring tightening torque per specifications.
What is the title of this diagram section?
Control Distances for Pedal Side Clearance
What measurement dimensions are labeled on the accelerator pedal?
The accelerator pedal shows dimensions labeled as F*, K*, and G*
What dimension is marked on the brake pedal assembly?
The brake pedal assembly shows dimension H*
Where does the note direct you to find the actual measurement specifications?
The note at the bottom states "See Specifications"
How many pedals are shown in this control distance diagram?
Two pedals are shown - the brake pedal on the left and the accelerator pedal on the right
What type of measurements does this diagram illustrate?
This diagram illustrates control distances for pedal side clearance measurements
Which pedal has more measurement dimensions labeled?
The accelerator pedal has more measurement dimensions labeled, showing F*, K*, and G* compared to the brake pedal's single H* dimension
What is the specified play measurement for the full throttle stop adjustment on manual transmission vehicles?
The full throttle stop should be adjusted so there is still 0.5 mm (0.020") play on the full throttle stop of the throttle valve with the accelerator pedal plate in full throttle position.
How much should you turn the adjusting screw to achieve the proper play adjustment?
Unscrewing the adjusting screw one and one half turns = 0.5 mm (0.020") play.
What are the first three steps for accelerator cable adjustment on both manual and automatic transmissions?
1. Accelerator pedal on neutral stop. 2. Throttle valve in neutral position (automatic choke switched off). 3. Adjust the cable to remove tension.
What components are shown in the photograph with callout numbers 1 and 2?
The photograph shows the accelerator cable adjustment area with callouts 1 and 2 indicating specific adjustment points or components.
What is the control distance specification that needs to be checked for automatic transmission full throttle stop adjustment?
Check control distance C* of the full throttle stop.
How should the full throttle stop be secured after adjustment on automatic transmission vehicles?
Lock with the M 8 nut.
What reference should be consulted for checking the pressure point on automatic transmission vehicles?
Check the pressure point for automatic transmission - see 24 00 004.
What is the part number for the replacing kickdown switch on EH transmission?
What steps are required for kickdown switch installation?
Adjust locknuts to distance C*. Make final adjustments after installation. Tightening torque*.
What should be done with the flat male plug during kickdown switch replacement?
Pull off flat male plug (1). Unscrew nuts (2). Unscrew switch.
Where can you find the BMW Test Plan referenced for the kickdown switch check?
See BMW Test Plan in Group 24.
What play measurement should be maintained in the kickdown position for automatic transmission full throttle stop adjustment?
Adjust full throttle stop that there is still 0.5 mm (0.020") play on full throttle stop of the throttle valve in kickdown position (pedal pressed beyond full throttle stop).
What is the first step when removing and installing the pedal base assembly?
Disconnect the battery ground lead and remove the dashboard trim panel at bottom left - see Group 51.
What electrical connections need to be removed from the steering column area?
Pull off the plug on the stop light switch and pull off the central electric plug on the steering column.
What special note applies to 1987 models regarding the stop light switch?
Beginning with 1987 models, pull off the plug of the stop light switch - see Group 61.
How do you remove the brake linkage shaft according to the diagram?
Press off clamp (1) on brake linkage and pull out shaft (2).
What lubrication is required during installation of the brake linkage?
Lubricate bearing surfaces with grease.
What components need to be disconnected on the clutch pedal version with return spring?
Disconnect the return spring on the body for the version with return spring on clutch pedal.
How do you remove the eccentric component shown in the diagram?
Unscrew the nut and pull out eccentric (1).
What lubrication is required for the setscrew during installation?
Lubricate setscrew with grease before installing and apply the specified tightening torque.
What adjustment is required during clutch pedal installation?
Adjust clutch pedal to distance (B) with the eccentric and apply the specified tightening torque.
What needs to be disconnected from both the accelerator and brake pedals?
Disconnect the accelerator pedal return spring on the pedal and disconnect the brake pedal return spring on the pedal.
What is shown in the bottom diagram with the distance marking 'B'?
The diagram shows the clutch pedal adjustment distance (B) that needs to be set using the eccentric during installation.
What are the three main pedal assemblies shown in this diagram?
The three main pedal assemblies shown are the clutch pedal (with over-center helper spring), brake pedal, and accelerator pedal.
What part number is associated with the clutch pedal assembly?
The clutch pedal assembly is labeled with part number 30 35 028.
What special feature is noted for the clutch pedal?
The clutch pedal has an over-center helper spring.
What part number corresponds to the brake pedal assembly?
The brake pedal assembly is labeled with part number 30 35 002.
What part number is shown for the brake pedal mechanism in the center diagram?
The brake pedal mechanism in the center diagram shows part number 30 35 001.
What part number is associated with the accelerator pedal?
The accelerator pedal is labeled with part number 20 35 022.
What dimension markings are visible on the brake pedal diagrams?
The brake pedal diagrams show dimension markings labeled as 'A' and 'B' with measurement arrows.
What note appears at the bottom of the page regarding specifications?
At the bottom of the page, there is a note that says 'See Specifications'.
What should be replaced when removing an accelerator pedal?
A removed accelerator pedal should be replaced with a new part in general because clips on the old part could be damaged, allowing the accelerator pedal to slide out of the plate.
What are the three steps to remove the accelerator pedal shaft?
Press off retainer (1) on the accelerator pedal shaft, press down on carpet (2) behind the accelerator pedal, and press in clips (3) in direction of arrow and lift out accelerator pedal upward.
What important check must be performed after installing accelerator pedal clips?
Always check that clips engage correctly.
How do you remove the accelerator pedal lever retainer?
Pull off retainer (1) and slide shaft to the left.
What must be removed before accessing the accelerator pedal lever?
Remove dashboard trim panel at bottom left - see Group 51.
What lubrication is required during accelerator pedal lever installation?
Lubricate bearing surfaces with grease.
What happens if the accelerator pedal clips are damaged?
If clips are damaged, the accelerator pedal can slide out of the plate, which could lead to an accident.
What does callout number 2 indicate in the accelerator pedal removal diagram?
Callout number 2 indicates the carpet behind the accelerator pedal that must be pressed down during removal.
What service procedures are covered in section 35 41 000?
Section 35 41 000 covers removing and installing accelerator pedal.
How do you disconnect the accelerator lever spring?
Disconnect accelerator lever spring on pedal.
What reference number is shown for the accelerator pedal removal procedure?
The reference number shown is 28 35 006.
What is the first step shown for disconnecting the accelerator cable?
Disconnect cable on pedal lever.
How do you remove the cable from the engine compartment wall?
Compress locking hooks and pull cable out of the engine compartment wall.
What should you do with the nipple when removing the accelerator cable?
Take nipple off of cable.
What does callout number 1 indicate in the bottom photograph?
The operating nipple that needs to be pressed out of the throttle valve lever.
What does callout number 2 point to in the throttle valve lever area?
The rubber pad on holder that needs to be disconnected.
What procedure is shown in the middle diagram with the arrows?
Compressing locking hooks and pulling the cable out of the engine compartment wall.
What are the two components that need to be disconnected at the throttle valve lever?
Press operating nipple (1) out of the throttle valve lever and disconnect rubber pad on holder (2).
What is the reference number for the diagram showing the cable removal from engine compartment?
What is the reference number for the photograph showing the pedal lever disconnection?
What are the procedure numbers for replacing brake pedal and clutch pedal bearing sleeves?
The procedure number for replacing brake pedal bearing sleeve is 35 21 011, and for replacing clutch pedal bearing sleeve is 35 31 011.
What should you do to remove the pedal according to this page?
Remove pedal by following procedures 35 21 000 or 35 31 000.
When should you replace a pedal with injection molded bearing sleeve?
Replace pedal in case of wear, or when pedal movement is difficult.
What is the production diameter specification for drilling or reaming the bearing sleeve?
The production diameter is 14.2 + 0.1 mm (0.559 + 0.004 inches).
What should be applied to the bearing surface after machining?
Lubricate bearing surface with grease.
How can you identify pedals with press fit bearing sleeves?
Bearing sleeves protrude into the guide pipe on the left and right sides by only approx. 17 mm (0.669 inches).
What procedure is used to press out bearing sleeves for brake and clutch pedals?
Press out bearing sleeves (1) for brake and clutch pedals using the method shown in the diagram.
Where can additional specifications be found according to this page?
Additional specifications can be found in the Specifications section, as indicated by the asterisk note at the bottom of the page.
What tool operation is required when pedal movement becomes difficult?
When pedal movement is difficult, drill or ream out the bearing sleeve to a production diameter of 14.2 + 0.1 mm.
What is the difference between injection molded and press fit bearing sleeves shown in the diagrams?
Press fit bearing sleeves protrude into the guide pipe by only about 17 mm on each side, while injection molded sleeves are integrated into the pedal and require drilling/reaming when worn.
Which dashboard component needs to be removed according to the brake pedal removal procedure?
Remove dashboard trim panel at bottom left - see Group 51.
What do callout numbers 1 and 2 indicate in the brake pedal removal diagram?
Callout 1 shows the clamp on brake linkage to press off, and callout 2 shows the shaft to pull out.
How do you disconnect the return spring on a clutch pedal version?
Disconnect return spring on body for the version with Return Spring on Clutch Pedal.
What is the procedure for removing the brake pedal shaft?
Unscrew nut, pull out shaft, then take off pedal.
What type of nuts should be used during brake pedal installation?
Replace self-locking nuts.
Where should you disconnect the brake pedal return spring?
Disconnect brake pedal return spring on pedal.
What should be checked during installation for models with an over-center helper spring?
Check for correct installed position in models with an over-center helper spring.
What reference should be consulted for proper pedal positioning?
Also refer to the pedal layout drawing.
What dashboard component needs to be removed before accessing the clutch pedal?
Remove the dashboard trim panel at bottom left - see Group 51.
What component should be disconnected from the brake pedal?
Disconnect the brake pedal return spring on the pedal.
What must be reached when adjusting the clutch pedal eccentric bolt?
Distance B must be reached. Turn the eccentric bolt 180° if distance B is not reached with the previously described adjustment.
What is prohibited regarding the eccentric bolt positioning?
Intermediate positioning of the eccentric bolt is not permitted.
How should the eccentric be removed from the pedal assembly?
Unscrew nut - pull out eccentric.
What lubricant should be used when installing the eccentric bolt?
Install eccentric bolt with Molykote Longterm 2.
What steps are required to remove the pedal completely?
Unscrew nut. Pull out shaft and take off pedal.
What type of nut should be used during pedal installation?
Replace with self-locking nut.
What should you do after applying mounting paste to the rim flange and tire beads?
Clamp the rim on the mounting machine, then slide on the tire with the lower bead over the rim flange partially.
What pressure should you initially increase to when inflating the tire?
Increase the pressure in steps to 3.3 bar (47 psi) using spring pressure.
What important warning is given regarding the tire bead during mounting?
Don't pinch or damage the bead.
What should you check when running the mounting machine forward clockwise a short distance?
Check that the lower tire bead remains in the well.
What is the maximum inflation pressure allowed if tire beads seat on rim flange correctly?
If tire beads seat on rim flange correctly, increase the inflation pressure to max. 4.0 bar (57 psi) to have the tire "settle".
Where should the tire bead seat in relation to the mounting finger?
The tire bead should seat in rollers next to the mounting finger.
What should you do if the tire bead does not slide on to the rim edge all around?

Do not increase the pressure. Instead, the tire must be deflated and the tire bead pressed off, then coat the tire bead and rim flange with mounting paste again and inflate again to 3.3 bar (47 psi) pressure.
What diagram number shows the tire being pressed underneath the mounting finger?
Diagram 30 36 047 shows the tire being pressed underneath the mounting finger.
What should you do first after mounting before inflating the tire?
After mounting, first release the clamps and then inflate the tire (without valve insert).
How should you position the upper tire bead during the mounting process?
Press the upper tire bead underneath the mounting finger, ensuring the tire bead should seat in rollers next to the mounting finger.
What is the final step mentioned for correcting tire inflation pressure?
Screw in the valve insert and correct the tire inflation pressure.
What is the first step when mounting tires with a modern mounting machine?
Unscrew valve and deflate the tire.
How should the tire beads be pressed off the rim flange?
Press off tire bead from rim flange all around on outside and inside with pressing-off horn of the machine.
What should you do if tire beads fit too tight during removal?
First only loosen tire from flange at several points with the pressing-off horn prior to the actual pressing-off.
How far should the tire beads be pushed into the rim well?
Push both tire beads into rim well completely until they are loose.
What should be done to the rim after removing the tire?
Pull off balance weights on rim and clean rim to remove large pieces of dirt.
What should be applied to tire beads before mounting?
Coat tire beads with mounting paste.
Which direction should the narrow rim shoulder always face when mounting?
Narrow rim shoulder always faces up.
What distance should the valve be positioned from the right of the mounting head?
Valve should be at about 10 cm (4") to the right of the mounting head.
What type of tire irons should be used for aluminum rims?
Use coated or shrink-fit hose covered tire irons for aluminum rims.
In which direction should the mounting machine run back initially to allow the tire bead to slide onto the mounting finger?
Let mounting machine run back a short distance (counterclockwise) so that the tire bead can slide fully on to the mounting finger.
What should be checked when the mounting machine runs forward briefly?
Always check whether the bottom bead is fully in the well and the tire is given enough time to move.
What is the final step to achieve complete separation of the tire from the rim?
Let machine run back a short distance again and then forward (clockwise) briefly, until there is complete separation of the tire from the rim.
At what speed and gear should balancing be performed?
Balancing is performed with engine power in fourth gear at about 100 km/h (50 mph).
What conditions must be met for the engine during balancing?
The engine must run smoothly without hesitation, doors, engine hood and trunk lid must be closed and the driver should sit in the car as still as possible.
What is the maximum acceptable finish balancing value for a wheel?
If a value of more than 15 grams is displayed for finish balancing of a wheel, the possible causes must be eliminated prior to finish balancing and before rechecking the finished wheel.
What precaution is given regarding the exhaust extraction hose?
The exhaust extraction hose may not touch the tail panel.
What special consideration applies to BMW 325 iX cars regarding wheel lifting?
This car has four driven wheels so that all four wheels must be able to turn freely and the car must be jacked up safely for finish balancing.
What must be done before electronic finish balancing on BMW 325 iX?
Always first balance all wheels stationary prior to electronic (finish) balancing.
How should BMW 325 iX cars be positioned for finish balancing?
Position car on four finish balancing measuring supports. When only two measuring supports are used, two further identical jacks with lateral movement must be used on the other axle.
What important check should be performed on BMW 325 iX transmission components?
Check the deflection angle of the transmission end joint.
What reference should be consulted for additional Service Information?
Refer to Service Information of Group 36.
What specific Service Information document is mentioned for finish balancing issues?
Service Information 36 0 483 (196) must be referenced when possible causes like inaccurate stationary balancing or centering need to be eliminated.
What is shown in the image labeled 30 36 018?
The image shows connecting leads for the test sender being attached to a wheel.
What is the first step when removing a wheel from the BMW E30?
Loosen wheel bolts.
Why should you mark the wheel position before removing it?
To avoid clamping errors when reinstalling. The wheel should be mounted in the same position with valve facing down.
What should you check on wheel bolt threads during installation?
Check wheel bolt threads and tapers for wear, replacing wheel bolts if necessary.
What cleaning product is recommended for the wheel hub centering collar?
Plastilube is recommended for cleaning the wheel hub centering collar and bearing surface of a disc wheel.
How should wheel bolt threads be prepared during installation?
Give wheel bolt threads a light coat of grease, but the taper must remain free of grease.
What should you check regarding brake clearance when mounting an M3 car wheel?
Check clearance on the brake caliper, as the pad spring holder in the brake caliper could be damaged or displaced.
What is the proper tightening sequence for wheel bolts?
Tighten bolts of wheel rims crosswise.
When should you recheck the wheel bolt tightening torque?
If new wheel rims are mounted for the first time, recheck the tightening torque after 1,000 km (600 miles).
What three types of wheel bolts are shown in the diagram?
a) Wheel bolt - galvanized, b) Wheel bolt - black chrome plated, c) Wheel bolt - black chrome plated and lockable (optional extra).
Can wheel bolts be used interchangeably between steel and aluminum wheels?
Yes, wheel bolts can be used for either steel or aluminum wheel rims since 9.82.
Where should pertinent wheel information be provided to the driver?
Provide pertinent information on a label or tag in view of the driver.
What is the source of supply reference mentioned at the bottom of the page?
HWB (Hella-Werk Behr) is listed as the source of supply.
What type of surface must balancing be carried out on?
Balancing must be carried out on firm underground (concrete floor without basement).
What condition must the car be in after jacking up for balancing?
The car must be level after jacking up and all wheels must turn easily.
What additional reference should be consulted for balancing procedures?
Also refer to Service Information of Group 36.
What equipment should be used to lift the car if applicable?
Lift car with a two-pillar hoist if applicable.
Where should measuring supports be applied on the front axle?
Apply measuring supports underneath the front axle on each wheel carrier/control arm joint, using suitable holding forks or additional forks.
Where should the workshop jack be positioned for the front axle final drive?
Apply a workshop jack underneath the front axle final drive in the middle and with light pressure, in order to suppress the oscillation of the front axle final drive.
How should the hoist arms be positioned during balancing procedures?
Lower the arms of the hoist until they have just barely cleared, but never touch the body during balancing procedures (resonance oscillation).
What documents should be referenced for additional fork information?
See Service Information or Workshop Equipment Planning Documents.
What is the purpose of applying light pressure with the workshop jack on the final drives?
The light pressure is applied in order to suppress the oscillation of the front axle final drive and rear axle final drive.
What critical safety consideration is mentioned regarding hoist arm positioning?
The hoist arms must never touch the body during balancing procedures to avoid resonance oscillation.
How should the car be secured during wheel balancing procedures?
Secure the car with a steel cable attached to the rear towing eye. The cable must not be tight to avoid wrong measuring values.
Which wheels should be balanced first during the balancing procedure?
Balance the wheels on the front axle first.
At what speed and in which gear is wheel balancing performed?
Balancing is performed with engine power in fourth gear at 100 km/h (60 mph).
Where should the chalk mark or adhesive tape be placed on the tire?
Paste adhesive tape or make a chalk mark, both 3 to 4 cm (1.18 to 1.575 inches) long, on the outside of the tire being balanced, opposite the valve.
What must not touch the tail panel during balancing?
The exhaust extraction hose must not touch the tail panel.
What should be done carefully after wheel balancing testing?
Brake the wheels carefully after testing.
When should the balance test be repeated?
Repeat test after installation of balance weights on the displayed positions.
What is the maximum acceptable imbalance value for finish balancing?
If a value of more than 15 grams is displayed for finish balancing of a wheel, the possible causes must be eliminated and the finish balanced wheels rechecked.
What equipment is needed to connect for testing during wheel balancing?
Connect leads for test sender and balance wheels to operating instructions supplied with pertinent balancing machine.
What must be adjusted on the finish balancer before starting?
Adjust the correct sensitivity on the finish balancer to the supplied operating instruction prior to balancing.
Can sensitivity settings for wheel balancing be transferred between different vehicles?
Since the sensitivity degree for balancing a wheel can not be transferred to a different wheel position or different car, it must be determined separately for each wheel.
What section number covers wheels and tires in this BMW manual?
Section 36 covers Wheels and Tires.
On which page can I find information about balancing front wheels on the car dynamically and electronically?
Information about balancing front wheels on the car dynamically and electronically can be found on page 36-1.
What procedure is covered on page 36-5 related to wheel inspection?
Page 36-5 covers checking the front or rear wheel for radial and lateral runout.
Where can I find information about tire replacement procedures?
Tire replacement procedures can be found on page 36-9.
What specific wheel size is mentioned for front and rear wheel balancing?
The 325 iX wheel size is specifically mentioned for front and rear wheel balancing procedures.
On which page would I find information about mounting tires with modern mounting machines?
Information about mounting tires with modern mounting machines can be found on page 36-10.
What should be removed from the wheel before balancing it dynamically?
Remove old balance weights, stones in treads and large pieces of dirt.
What three components are labeled 1, 2, and 3 in the balancing machine diagram?
1 is the basic flange, 2 is the center, and 3 is the type flange.
What should you check on the tire before balancing?
Check tire inflation pressure, condition of tire (damage, cuts, flat spots caused by not using car with hot tires for a long time).
What type of balancing machine should be used for this procedure?
Use a suitable center of pertinent balancing machine.
What important mounting requirement is specified to avoid clamping errors?
The wheel must be mounted on the balancing machine in the same manner (e.g. valve facing down) as mounted afterwards on the car.
If necessary, what additional inspection should be performed on the wheel and tire?
Check wheel and tire for radial and lateral runout - see 36 10 209.
For aluminum wheel rims, how should the tire be positioned relative to the rim?
Press the side of the tire away from the rim flange slightly at an appropriate point with a tire clamp and insert a holder.
What are the two components shown in the arrangement of balance weights for cast aluminum rims?
1 is the spring holder and 2 is the balance weight.
How should the balance weight be positioned for aluminum rims after using the tire clamp?
Remove the tire clamp and push a balance weight underneath the holder until it engages.
What is the final step mentioned for completing the wheel balancing procedure?
Balance wheel to operating instructions of pertinent balancing machine.
What type of wheels are shown in the two different balance weight arrangement diagrams?
Cast aluminum rims (top diagram) and steel rims (bottom diagram).
What is the procedure code for balancing both front wheels on car dynamically and electronically?
The procedure code is 36 10 030 for balancing both front wheels on car dynamically and electronically.
What must always be done before electronic finish balancing?
Always first balance the wheels stationary precisely prior to electronic (finish) balancing.
What measuring support is required for control arm end balancing up to 5 inch rims?
Apply measuring support for balancing on control arm end (1) up to 5 inch rims, using a suitable holding fork or additional fork.
What should be done when balancing wheels from 5 1/2 inch rims and larger?
From 5 1/2 inch rims on, apply the measuring support without an additional fork on control arm (2) and lift car with the measuring support.
What marking should be placed on the tire before balancing?
Paste adhesive tape or make a chalk mark, both 3 to 4 cm (0.181 to 1.575 inches) long, on the outside of the tire being balanced, opposite the valve.
What callout number indicates the control arm end in the wheel balancing diagram?
Callout number (1) indicates the control arm end in the wheel balancing setup.
Where should the jack be applied when balancing rear wheels?
Apply jack at middle of car on the rear axle carrier and lift the car.
What type of support should be used on the trailing arm during rear wheel balancing?
Use an unsprung support on the trailing arm of the running wheel to suppress the oscillation from the final drive.
What should be done to connect the balancing equipment?
Connect leads for test sender to the balancing machine.
What type of surface is required for wheel balancing?
Balancing must be carried out on firm underground (concrete floor without basement).
What should be checked after the rear wheel balancing setup is complete?
Check whether it is possible to turn the wheels easily after the balancing setup is complete.
What is the procedure number for checking front or rear wheel for lateral and radial runout?
36 10 209 is the procedure for checking front or rear wheel for lateral and radial runout.
What reference should you see for removing the wheel before checking runout?
You should see section 36 10 300 for wheel removal procedures.
How must the wheel be positioned when mounting it on the balancing machine?
The wheel must be mounted on the balancing machine in the same manner as mounted on the car, with the valve facing down, in order to avoid transmitted tension.
What special tool is required for measuring tire runout?
